## File: tf_backend_state/set-state.sh
```bash
  1: #!/bin/bash
  2: # Script to assume AWS role and upload Terraform state file to S3
  3: # ROLE_ARN is retrieved from GitHub repository secret 'AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN'
  4: # REGION is retrieved from GitHub repository variable 'AWS_REGION' (defaults to 'us-east-1' if not set)
  5: # Bucket name is retrieved from Terraform output and saved to GitHub repository variable
  6: # Bucket prefix is retrieved from GitHub repository variables
  7: set -euo pipefail
  8: # Run from script directory so terraform and variables.tfvars are found (works when called from repo root or tf_backend_state)
  9: SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
 10: cd "$SCRIPT_DIR"
 11: # Clean up any existing AWS credentials from environment to prevent conflicts
 12: # This ensures the script starts with a clean slate and uses the correct credentials
 13: unset AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID 2>/dev/null || true
 14: unset AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY 2>/dev/null || true
 15: unset AWS_SESSION_TOKEN 2>/dev/null || true
 16: unset AWS_PROFILE 2>/dev/null || true
 17: # Colors for output
 18: RED='\033[0;31m'
 19: GREEN='\033[0;32m'
 20: YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
 21: NC='\033[0m' # No Color
 22: # Function to print colored messages
 23: print_error() {
 24:     echo -e "${RED}ERROR:${NC} $1" >&2
 25: }
 26: print_success() {
 27:     echo -e "${GREEN}SUCCESS:${NC} $1"
 28: }
 29: print_info() {
 30:     echo -e "${YELLOW}INFO:${NC} $1"
 31: }
 32: # Check if AWS CLI is installed
 33: if ! command -v aws &> /dev/null; then
 34:     print_error "AWS CLI is not installed."
 35:     echo "Please install it from: https://aws.amazon.com/cli/"
 36:     exit 1
 37: fi
 38: # Check if GitHub CLI is installed
 39: if ! command -v gh &> /dev/null; then
 40:     print_error "GitHub CLI (gh) is not installed."
 41:     echo "Please install it from: https://cli.github.com/"
 42:     echo ""
 43:     echo "Or use the alternative method with curl (requires GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable):"
 44:     echo "  export GITHUB_TOKEN=your_token"
 45:     exit 1
 46: fi
 47: # Check if user is authenticated with GitHub CLI
 48: if ! gh auth status &> /dev/null; then
 49:     print_error "Not authenticated with GitHub CLI."
 50:     echo "Please run: gh auth login"
 51:     exit 1
 52: fi
 53: # Check if jq is installed (required for gh --jq flag)
 54: if ! command -v jq &> /dev/null; then
 55:     print_error "jq is not installed."
 56:     echo "Please install it:"
 57:     echo "  macOS: brew install jq"
 58:     echo "  Linux: sudo apt-get install jq (or use your package manager)"
 59:     echo "  Or visit: https://stedolan.github.io/jq/download/"
 60:     exit 1
 61: fi
 62: # Check if Terraform is installed
 63: if ! command -v terraform &> /dev/null; then
 64:     print_error "Terraform is not installed."
 65:     echo "Please install it from: https://www.terraform.io/downloads"
 66:     exit 1
 67: fi
 68: # Get repository owner and name
 69: REPO_OWNER=$(gh repo view --json owner --jq '.owner.login' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
 70: REPO_NAME=$(gh repo view --json name --jq '.name' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
 71: if [ -z "$REPO_OWNER" ] || [ -z "$REPO_NAME" ]; then
 72:     print_error "Could not determine repository information."
 73:     echo "Please ensure you're in a git repository and have proper permissions."
 74:     exit 1
 75: fi
 76: print_info "Repository: ${REPO_OWNER}/${REPO_NAME}"
 77: # Function to get repository variable using GitHub CLI
 78: get_repo_variable() {
 79:     local var_name=$1
 80:     local value
 81:     value=$(gh variable list --repo "${REPO_OWNER}/${REPO_NAME}" --json name,value --jq ".[] | select(.name == \"${var_name}\") | .value" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
 82:     if [ -z "$value" ]; then
 83:         return 1
 84:     fi
 85:     echo "$value"
 86: }
 87: # Function to set repository variable using GitHub CLI
 88: set_repo_variable() {
 89:     local var_name=$1
 90:     local var_value=$2
 91:     if gh variable set "${var_name}" --body "${var_value}" --repo "${REPO_OWNER}/${REPO_NAME}" 2>/dev/null; then
 92:         return 0
 93:     else
 94:         return 1
 95:     fi
 96: }
 97: # Function to retrieve secret from AWS Secrets Manager
 98: get_aws_secret() {
 99:     local secret_name=$1
100:     local secret_json
101:     local exit_code
102:     # Retrieve secret from AWS Secrets Manager
103:     # Use AWS_REGION if set, otherwise default to us-east-1
104:     secret_json=$(aws secretsmanager get-secret-value \
105:         --secret-id "$secret_name" \
106:         --region "${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}" \
107:         --query SecretString \
108:         --output text 2>&1)
109:     # Capture exit code before checking
110:     exit_code=$?
111:     # Validate secret retrieval
112:     if [ $exit_code -ne 0 ]; then
113:         print_error "Failed to retrieve secret '${secret_name}' from AWS Secrets Manager"
114:         print_error "Error: $secret_json"
115:         return 1
116:     fi
117:     # Validate JSON can be parsed
118:     if ! echo "$secret_json" | jq empty 2>/dev/null; then
119:         print_error "Secret '${secret_name}' contains invalid JSON"
120:         return 1
121:     fi
122:     echo "$secret_json"
123: }
124: # Function to get key value from secret JSON
125: get_secret_key_value() {
126:     local secret_json=$1
127:     local key_name=$2
128:     local value
129:     # Validate JSON can be parsed
130:     if ! echo "$secret_json" | jq empty 2>/dev/null; then
131:         print_error "Invalid JSON provided to get_secret_key_value"
132:         return 1
133:     fi
134:     # Extract key value using jq
135:     value=$(echo "$secret_json" | jq -r ".[\"${key_name}\"]" 2>/dev/null)
136:     # Check if jq command succeeded
137:     if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
138:         print_error "Failed to parse JSON or extract key '${key_name}'"
139:         return 1
140:     fi
141:     # Check if key exists (jq returns "null" for non-existent keys)
142:     if [ "$value" = "null" ] || [ -z "$value" ]; then
143:         print_error "Key '${key_name}' not found in secret JSON or value is empty"
144:         return 1
145:     fi
146:     echo "$value"
147: }
148: # Retrieve ROLE_ARN from AWS Secrets Manager
149: print_info "Retrieving AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN from AWS Secrets Manager..."
150: SECRET_JSON=$(get_aws_secret "github-role" || echo "")
151: if [ -z "$SECRET_JSON" ]; then
152:     print_error "Failed to retrieve secret from AWS Secrets Manager"
153:     exit 1
154: fi
155: ROLE_ARN=$(get_secret_key_value "$SECRET_JSON" "AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN" || echo "")
156: if [ -z "$ROLE_ARN" ]; then
157:     print_error "Failed to retrieve AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN from secret"
158:     exit 1
159: fi
160: print_success "Retrieved AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN"
161: # Retrieve REGION from repository variable
162: print_info "Retrieving AWS_REGION from repository variables..."
163: REGION=$(get_repo_variable "AWS_REGION" || echo "")
164: if [ -z "$REGION" ]; then
165:     print_info "AWS_REGION not found in repository variables, defaulting to 'us-east-1'"
166:     REGION="us-east-1"
167: else
168:     print_success "Retrieved AWS_REGION: $REGION"
169: fi
170: print_info "Assuming role: $ROLE_ARN"
171: print_info "Region: $REGION"
172: # Assume the role first
173: ROLE_SESSION_NAME="set-state-$(date +%s)"
174: # Assume role and capture output
175: ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT=$(aws sts assume-role \
176:     --role-arn "$ROLE_ARN" \
177:     --role-session-name "$ROLE_SESSION_NAME" \
178:     --region "$REGION" 2>&1)
179: if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
180:     print_error "Failed to assume role: $ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT"
181:     exit 1
182: fi
183: # Extract credentials from JSON output
184: # Try using jq if available (more reliable), otherwise use sed/grep
185: if command -v jq &> /dev/null; then
186:     export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=$(echo "$ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT" | jq -r '.Credentials.AccessKeyId')
187:     export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=$(echo "$ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT" | jq -r '.Credentials.SecretAccessKey')
188:     export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN=$(echo "$ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT" | jq -r '.Credentials.SessionToken')
189: else
190:     # Fallback: use sed for JSON parsing (works on both macOS and Linux)
191:     export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=$(echo "$ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT" | sed -n 's/.*"AccessKeyId"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
192:     export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=$(echo "$ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT" | sed -n 's/.*"SecretAccessKey"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
193:     export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN=$(echo "$ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT" | sed -n 's/.*"SessionToken"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
194: fi
195: if [ -z "$AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID" ] || [ -z "$AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY" ] || [ -z "$AWS_SESSION_TOKEN" ]; then
196:     print_error "Failed to extract credentials from assume-role output."
197:     print_error "Output was: $ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT"
198:     exit 1
199: fi
200: print_success "Successfully assumed role"
201: # Verify the credentials work
202: CALLER_ARN=$(aws sts get-caller-identity --region "$REGION" --query 'Arn' --output text 2>&1)
203: if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
204:     print_error "Failed to verify assumed role credentials: $CALLER_ARN"
205:     exit 1
206: fi
207: print_info "Assumed role identity: $CALLER_ARN"
208: # Retrieve BACKEND_PREFIX from repository variable (needed for both provisioning and upload)
209: print_info "Retrieving BACKEND_PREFIX from repository variables..."
210: BACKEND_PREFIX=$(get_repo_variable "BACKEND_PREFIX" || echo "")
211: if [ -z "$BACKEND_PREFIX" ]; then
212:     print_error "BACKEND_PREFIX not found in repository variables."
213:     echo "Please ensure BACKEND_PREFIX is set in GitHub repository variables."
214:     exit 1
215: fi
216: print_success "Retrieved BACKEND_PREFIX: $BACKEND_PREFIX"
217: # Check if BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME exists in repository variables
218: print_info "Checking for existing BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME in repository variables..."
219: BUCKET_NAME=$(get_repo_variable "BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME" || echo "")
220: if [ -z "$BUCKET_NAME" ]; then
221:     print_info "BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME not found in repository variables."
222:     print_info "This means the infrastructure has not been provisioned yet."
223:     print_info "Proceeding with Terraform provisioning..."
224:     # Check if variables.tfvars exists
225:     if [ ! -f "variables.tfvars" ]; then
226:         print_error "variables.tfvars file not found in current directory."
227:         echo "Please ensure variables.tfvars exists with required variables."
228:         exit 1
229:     fi
230:     print_success "Found variables.tfvars file"
231:     # Terraform init
232:     print_info "Running terraform init..."
233:     if ! terraform init -backend=false; then
234:         print_error "Terraform init failed."
235:         exit 1
236:     fi
237:     print_success "Terraform initialized"
238:     # Terraform validate
239:     print_info "Running terraform validate..."
240:     if ! terraform validate; then
241:         print_error "Terraform validation failed."
242:         exit 1
243:     fi
244:     print_success "Terraform validation passed"
245:     # Terraform plan
246:     print_info "Running terraform plan..."
247:     if ! terraform plan -var-file="variables.tfvars" -out terraform.tfplan; then
248:         print_error "Terraform plan failed."
249:         exit 1
250:     fi
251:     print_success "Terraform plan completed"
252:     # Terraform apply
253:     print_info "Running terraform apply..."
254:     if ! terraform apply -auto-approve terraform.tfplan; then
255:         print_error "Terraform apply failed."
256:         exit 1
257:     fi
258:     print_success "Terraform apply completed"
259:     # Get bucket name from Terraform output
260:     print_info "Retrieving bucket name from Terraform output..."
261:     BUCKET_NAME=$(terraform output -raw bucket_name 2>/dev/null || echo "")
262:     if [ -z "$BUCKET_NAME" ]; then
263:         print_error "Failed to retrieve bucket name from Terraform output."
264:         echo "Please check Terraform outputs."
265:         exit 1
266:     fi
267:     print_success "Retrieved bucket name: $BUCKET_NAME"
268: else
269:     print_success "Found existing BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME: $BUCKET_NAME"
270:     # Check if state file exists in S3 and download if available
271:     S3_PATH="s3://${BUCKET_NAME}/${BACKEND_PREFIX}"
272:     print_info "Checking for existing state file at: $S3_PATH"
273:     if aws s3 ls "$S3_PATH" --region "$REGION" &>/dev/null; then
274:         print_info "State file exists in S3, downloading..."
275:         if aws s3 cp "$S3_PATH" terraform.tfstate --region "$REGION"; then
276:             print_success "State file downloaded successfully from S3"
277:         else
278:             print_error "Failed to download state file from S3"
279:             exit 1
280:         fi
281:     else
282:         print_info "State file does not exist in S3"
283:         # Check if terraform.tfstate exists locally
284:         if [ ! -f "terraform.tfstate" ]; then
285:             print_error "terraform.tfstate file not found locally and not in S3."
286:             echo "Please ensure you have run 'terraform apply' first to generate the state file."
287:             exit 1
288:         fi
289:         print_success "Found terraform.tfstate file locally"
290:     fi
291:     # Verify bucket name from Terraform output matches
292:     print_info "Verifying bucket name from Terraform output..."
293:     TERRAFORM_BUCKET_NAME=$(terraform output -raw bucket_name 2>/dev/null || echo "")
294:     if [ -n "$TERRAFORM_BUCKET_NAME" ] && [ "$TERRAFORM_BUCKET_NAME" != "$BUCKET_NAME" ]; then
295:         print_error "Bucket name mismatch!"
296:         echo "Repository variable BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME: $BUCKET_NAME"
297:         echo "Terraform output bucket_name: $TERRAFORM_BUCKET_NAME"
298:         echo "Please verify the bucket name is correct."
299:         exit 1
300:     fi
301:     print_success "Bucket name verified"
302: fi
303: print_info "Saving bucket name to GitHub repository variable..."
304: if set_repo_variable "BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME" "$BUCKET_NAME"; then
305:     print_success "Saved BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME to repository variables"
306: else
307:     print_error "Failed to save BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME to repository variables."
308:     echo "Please ensure you have proper permissions to write repository variables."
309:     exit 1
310: fi
311: S3_PATH="s3://${BUCKET_NAME}/${BACKEND_PREFIX}"
312: print_info "Uploading state file to: $S3_PATH"
313: if aws s3 cp terraform.tfstate "$S3_PATH" --region "$REGION"; then
314:     print_success "State file uploaded successfully to $S3_PATH"
315: else
316:     print_error "Failed to upload state file to S3"
317:     exit 1
318: fi
319: print_success "Script completed successfully"
```

```yaml
 1: name: 00 - TF Backend State Destroying
 2: on:
 3:   workflow_dispatch:
 4:     inputs:
 5:       confirmation:
 6:         description: 'Type "yes" to confirm destruction (required)'
 7:         required: true
 8:         type: string
 9: jobs:
10:   ConfirmDestruction:
11:     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
12:     permissions: {}
13:     steps:
14:       - name: Confirm destruction
15:         run: |
16:           if [ "${{ inputs.confirmation }}" != "yes" ]; then
17:             echo "ERROR: Confirmation required. You must type 'yes' to proceed with destruction."
18:             echo "Received: '${{ inputs.confirmation }}'"
19:             exit 1
20:           fi
21:           echo "✓ Confirmation received. Proceeding with destruction..."
22:   InfraProvision:
23:     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
24:     needs:
25:       - ConfirmDestruction
26:     permissions:
27:       contents: write
28:       actions: write
29:       id-token: write
30:     env:
31:       # Default to us-east-1 when vars.AWS_REGION is not set (repository variable)
32:       AWS_REGION: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}
33:     defaults:
34:       run:
35:         working-directory: ./tf_backend_state
36:     steps:
37:       - name: Set AWS_REGION default
38:         run: |
39:           if [ -z "${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}" ]; then
40:             echo "AWS_REGION=us-east-1" >> $GITHUB_ENV
41:             echo "Using default AWS_REGION=us-east-1 (set vars.AWS_REGION to override)"
42:           fi
43:       - name: Checkout the repo code
44:         uses: actions/checkout@v4
45:       - name: Setup terraform
46:         uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
47:         with:
48:           terraform_version: 1.14.0
49:       - name: Configure AWS credentials (State Account)
50:         uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
51:         with:
52:           role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN }}
53:           role-session-name: GitHubActions-TFStateInfraDestroy
54:           aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
55:       - name: Download backend state file from S3
56:         run: |
57:           aws s3 cp \
58:             s3://${{ vars.BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME }}/${{ vars.BACKEND_PREFIX }} \
59:             terraform.tfstate
60:       - name: Terraform init
61:         run: terraform init -backend=false
62:       - name: Terraform validate
63:         run: terraform validate
64:       - name: Terraform plan destroy
65:         run: terraform plan -var-file="variables.tfvars" -destroy -out terraform.tfplan
66:       - name: Destroy backend state
67:         run: terraform apply -auto-approve terraform.tfplan
```

## File: .github/workflows/00-tfstate_infra_provisioning.yaml
```yaml
  1: name: 00 - TF Backend State Provisioning
  2: on:
  3:   workflow_dispatch:
  4: jobs:
  5:   InfraProvision:
  6:     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  7:     permissions:
  8:       contents: write
  9:       actions: write
 10:       id-token: write
 11:     env:
 12:       # Default to us-east-1 when vars.AWS_REGION is not set (repository variable)
 13:       AWS_REGION: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}
 14:     defaults:
 15:       run:
 16:         working-directory: ./tf_backend_state
 17:     steps:
 18:       - name: Set AWS_REGION default
 19:         run: |
 20:           if [ -z "${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}" ]; then
 21:             echo "AWS_REGION=us-east-1" >> $GITHUB_ENV
 22:             echo "Using default AWS_REGION=us-east-1 (set vars.AWS_REGION to override)"
 23:           fi
 24:       - name: Checkout the repo code
 25:         uses: actions/checkout@v4
 26:       - name: Setup terraform
 27:         uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
 28:         with:
 29:           terraform_version: 1.14.0
 30:       - name: Configure AWS credentials (State Account)
 31:         uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
 32:         with:
 33:           role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN }}
 34:           role-session-name: GitHubActions-TFStateInfraProvision
 35:           aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
 36:       - name: Check for existing state file
 37:         uses: actions/github-script@v7
 38:         id: check_state
 39:         with:
 40:           github-token: ${{ secrets.GH_TOKEN }}
 41:           script: |
 42:             const repo = context.repo;
 43:             let bucketName = '';
 44:             let exists = 'false';
 45:             try {
 46:               // Try to get existing BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME variable
 47:               const response = await github.rest.actions.getRepoVariable({
 48:                 owner: repo.owner,
 49:                 repo: repo.repo,
 50:                 name: 'BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME'
 51:               });
 52:               bucketName = response.data.value || '';
 53:               if (bucketName) {
 54:                 console.log(`Found existing BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME: ${bucketName}`);
 55:                 exists = 'true';
 56:               } else {
 57:                 console.log('BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME variable exists but is empty');
 58:                 exists = 'false';
 59:               }
 60:             } catch (error) {
 61:               if (error.status === 404) {
 62:                 console.log('BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME variable does not exist, proceeding with new provisioning');
 63:                 exists = 'false';
 64:               } else {
 65:                 console.error('Error checking repository variable:', error.message);
 66:                 throw error;
 67:               }
 68:             }
 69:             // Always set outputs to avoid linter warnings
 70:             core.setOutput('bucket_name', bucketName);
 71:             core.setOutput('exists', exists);
 72:       - name: Download existing state file if available
 73:         # Outputs are always set by check_state step (see line 70-71)
 74:         if: steps.check_state.outputs.exists == 'true' && steps.check_state.outputs.bucket_name != ''
 75:         env:
 76:           BUCKET_NAME: ${{ steps.check_state.outputs.bucket_name }}
 77:           BACKEND_PREFIX: ${{ vars.BACKEND_PREFIX }}
 78:         run: |
 79:           if [ -z "$BUCKET_NAME" ] || [ -z "$BACKEND_PREFIX" ]; then
 80:             echo "Bucket name or prefix is empty, skipping state file download"
 81:             exit 0
 82:           fi
 83:           S3_PATH="s3://${BUCKET_NAME}/${BACKEND_PREFIX}"
 84:           echo "Attempting to download state file from: ${S3_PATH}"
 85:           if aws s3 ls "$S3_PATH" 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
 86:             echo "State file exists, downloading..."
 87:             aws s3 cp "$S3_PATH" terraform.tfstate
 88:             echo "State file downloaded successfully"
 89:           else
 90:             echo "State file does not exist in S3, proceeding with new provisioning"
 91:           fi
 92:       - name: Terraform init
 93:         run: terraform init -backend=false
 94:       - name: Terraform validate
 95:         run: terraform validate
 96:       - name: Terraform plan
 97:         run: terraform plan -var-file="variables.tfvars" -out terraform.tfplan
 98:       - name: Provision backend state
 99:         id: provision_backend
100:         run: |
101:           terraform apply -auto-approve terraform.tfplan
102:           BUCKET_NAME=$(terraform output -raw bucket_name)
103:           echo "bucket_name=$BUCKET_NAME" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
104:       - name: Save bucket name to GitHub repository variable
105:         uses: actions/github-script@v7
106:         env:
107:           BUCKET_NAME: ${{ steps.provision_backend.outputs.bucket_name }}
108:         with:
109:           github-token: ${{ secrets.GH_TOKEN }}
110:           script: |
111:             const bucketName = process.env.BUCKET_NAME;
112:             const repo = context.repo;
113:             if (!bucketName || bucketName.trim() === '') {
114:               throw new Error('BUCKET_NAME is not set or is empty');
115:             }
116:             console.log(`Saving bucket name: ${bucketName}`);
117:             try {
118:               // Try to get existing bucket name variable
119:               try {
120:                 await github.rest.actions.getRepoVariable({
121:                   owner: repo.owner,
122:                   repo: repo.repo,
123:                   name: 'BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME'
124:                 });
125:                 // Update existing bucket name variable
126:                 await github.rest.actions.updateRepoVariable({
127:                   owner: repo.owner,
128:                   repo: repo.repo,
129:                   name: 'BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME',
130:                   value: bucketName
131:                 });
132:                 console.log('Updated repository variable BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME');
133:               } catch (error) {
134:                 if (error.status === 404) {
135:                   // Variable doesn't exist, create it
136:                   await github.rest.actions.createRepoVariable({
137:                     owner: repo.owner,
138:                     repo: repo.repo,
139:                     name: 'BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME',
140:                     value: bucketName
141:                   });
142:                   console.log('Created repository variable BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME');
143:                 } else {
144:                   throw error;
145:                 }
146:               }
147:             } catch (error) {
148:               console.error('Error saving repository variable:', error.message);
149:               console.error('Note: GITHUB_TOKEN may need write permissions for repository variables.');
150:               console.error('Please ensure "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" is enabled in repository settings.');
151:               throw error;
152:             }
153:       - name: Upload backend state file to S3
154:         # Always upload state file to ensure synchronization
155:         env:
156:           BUCKET_NAME: ${{ steps.provision_backend.outputs.bucket_name }}
157:           BACKEND_PREFIX: ${{ vars.BACKEND_PREFIX }}
158:         run: |
159:           if [ -z "$BUCKET_NAME" ] || [ -z "$BACKEND_PREFIX" ]; then
160:             echo "Error: BUCKET_NAME or BACKEND_PREFIX is empty"
161:             exit 1
162:           fi
163:           echo "Uploading state file to s3://${BUCKET_NAME}/${BACKEND_PREFIX}"
164:           aws s3 cp terraform.tfstate s3://${BUCKET_NAME}/${BACKEND_PREFIX}
165:           echo "State file uploaded successfully"
```

```yaml
  1: name: 01 - Backend Infra Destroying
  2: on:
  3:   workflow_dispatch:
  4:     inputs:
  5:       region:
  6:         description: 'Select AWS Region'
  7:         required: true
  8:         type: choice
  9:         default: 'us-east-1: N. Virginia'
 10:         options:
 11:           - 'us-east-1: N. Virginia'
 12:           - 'us-east-2: Ohio'
 13:       environment:
 14:         description: 'Select Environment'
 15:         required: true
 16:         type: choice
 17:         default: prod
 18:         options:
 19:           - prod
 20:           - dev
 21:       confirmation:
 22:         description: 'Type "yes" to confirm destruction (required)'
 23:         required: true
 24:         type: string
 25: jobs:
 26:   ConfirmDestruction:
 27:     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
 28:     permissions: {}
 29:     steps:
 30:       - name: Confirm destruction
 31:         run: |
 32:           if [ "${{ inputs.confirmation }}" != "yes" ]; then
 33:             echo "ERROR: Confirmation required. You must type 'yes' to proceed with destruction."
 34:             echo "Received: '${{ inputs.confirmation }}'"
 35:             exit 1
 36:           fi
 37:           echo "✓ Confirmation received. Proceeding with destruction..."
 38:   SetRegion:
 39:     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
 40:     needs:
 41:       - ConfirmDestruction
 42:     permissions: {}
 43:     outputs:
 44:       region_code: ${{ steps.set_region.outputs.region_code }}
 45:     steps:
 46:       - name: Set Region
 47:         id: set_region
 48:         run: |
 49:           SELECTED_REGION="${{ inputs.region }}"
 50:           echo "region_code=${SELECTED_REGION%%:*}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
 51:   InfraDestroy:
 52:     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
 53:     needs:
 54:       - ConfirmDestruction
 55:       - SetRegion
 56:     permissions:
 57:       contents: write
 58:       actions: write
 59:       id-token: write
 60:     env:
 61:       AWS_REGION: ${{ needs.SetRegion.outputs.region_code }}
 62:     defaults:
 63:       run:
 64:         working-directory: ./backend_infra
 65:     steps:
 66:       - name: Checkout the repo code
 67:         uses: actions/checkout@v4
 68:       - name: Setup terraform
 69:         uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
 70:         with:
 71:           terraform_version: 1.14.0
 72:       - name: Configure AWS credentials (State Account)
 73:         uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
 74:         with:
 75:           role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN }}
 76:           role-session-name: GitHubActions-BackendInfraDestroy
 77:           aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
 78:       - name: Create backend.hcl from placeholder
 79:         run: |
 80:           cp tfstate-backend-values-template.hcl backend.hcl
 81:           sed -i -e "s|<BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME>|${{ vars.BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME }}|g" \
 82:           -e "s|<BACKEND_PREFIX>|${{ vars.BACKEND_PREFIX }}|g" \
 83:           -e "s|<AWS_REGION>|${{ env.AWS_REGION }}|g" \
 84:           backend.hcl
 85:           echo "Created backend.hcl:"
 86:           cat backend.hcl
 87:       - name: Update variables.tfvars
 88:         run: |
 89:           sed -i "s|^env[[:space:]]*=.*|env = \"${{ inputs.environment }}\"|" variables.tfvars
 90:           sed -i "s|^region[[:space:]]*=.*|region = \"${{ env.AWS_REGION }}\"|" variables.tfvars
 91:           # Set deployment account role ARN based on environment
 92:           DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN="${{ inputs.environment == 'prod' && secrets.AWS_PRODUCTION_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN || secrets.AWS_DEVELOPMENT_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN }}"
 93:           if ! grep -q "^deployment_account_role_arn" variables.tfvars; then
 94:             echo "deployment_account_role_arn = \"${DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN}\"" >> variables.tfvars
 95:           else
 96:             sed -i "s|^deployment_account_role_arn[[:space:]]*=.*|deployment_account_role_arn = \"${DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN}\"|" variables.tfvars
 97:           fi
 98:           # Set ExternalId for cross-account role assumption security
 99:           EXTERNAL_ID="${{ secrets.AWS_ASSUME_EXTERNAL_ID }}"
100:           if ! grep -q "^deployment_account_external_id" variables.tfvars; then
101:             echo "deployment_account_external_id = \"${EXTERNAL_ID}\"" >> variables.tfvars
102:           else
103:             sed -i "s|^deployment_account_external_id[[:space:]]*=.*|deployment_account_external_id = \"${EXTERNAL_ID}\"|" variables.tfvars
104:           fi
105:           echo "Updated variables.tfvars:"
106:           cat variables.tfvars
107:       - name: Terraform init
108:         run: terraform init -backend-config=backend.hcl
109:       - name: Terraform workspace
110:         run: |
111:           WORKSPACE="${{ env.AWS_REGION }}-${{ inputs.environment }}"
112:           terraform workspace select $WORKSPACE || terraform workspace new $WORKSPACE
113:       - name: Terraform validate
114:         run: terraform validate
115:       - name: Terraform plan destroy
116:         run: terraform plan -var-file="variables.tfvars" -destroy -out terraform.tfplan
117:       - name: Destroy backend infrastructure
118:         run: terraform apply -auto-approve terraform.tfplan
```

## File: .github/workflows/02-application_infra_destroying.yaml
```yaml
  1: name: 02 - Application Infra Destroying
  2: # Required GitHub Repository Secrets:
  3: # - AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN: IAM role ARN for backend state operations
  4: # - AWS_PRODUCTION_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN: IAM role ARN for production deployments
  5: # - AWS_DEVELOPMENT_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN: IAM role ARN for development deployments
  6: # - AWS_ASSUME_EXTERNAL_ID: ExternalId for cross-account role assumption security
  7: # - TF_VAR_OPENLDAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD: OpenLDAP admin password
  8: # - TF_VAR_OPENLDAP_CONFIG_PASSWORD: OpenLDAP config password
  9: #
 10: # Note: GitHub workflows use repository secrets, while bash scripts use AWS Secrets Manager.
 11: # The secrets listed above must be configured in GitHub repository settings.
 12: on:
 13:   workflow_dispatch:
 14:     inputs:
 15:       region:
 16:         description: 'Select AWS Region'
 17:         required: true
 18:         type: choice
 19:         default: 'us-east-1: N. Virginia'
 20:         options:
 21:           - 'us-east-1: N. Virginia'
 22:           - 'us-east-2: Ohio'
 23:       environment:
 24:         description: 'Select Environment'
 25:         required: true
 26:         type: choice
 27:         default: prod
 28:         options:
 29:           - prod
 30:           - dev
 31:       confirmation:
 32:         description: 'Type "yes" to confirm destruction (required)'
 33:         required: true
 34:         type: string
 35: jobs:
 36:   ConfirmDestruction:
 37:     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
 38:     permissions: {}
 39:     steps:
 40:       - name: Confirm destruction
 41:         run: |
 42:           if [ "${{ inputs.confirmation }}" != "yes" ]; then
 43:             echo "ERROR: Confirmation required. You must type 'yes' to proceed with destruction."
 44:             echo "Received: '${{ inputs.confirmation }}'"
 45:             exit 1
 46:           fi
 47:           echo "✓ Confirmation received. Proceeding with destruction..."
 48:   SetRegion:
 49:     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
 50:     needs:
 51:       - ConfirmDestruction
 52:     permissions:
 53:       contents: read
 54:     outputs:
 55:       region_code: ${{ steps.set_region.outputs.region_code }}
 56:     steps:
 57:       - name: Set Region
 58:         id: set_region
 59:         run: |
 60:           SELECTED_REGION="${{ inputs.region }}"
 61:           echo "region_code=${SELECTED_REGION%%:*}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
 62:   InfraDestroy:
 63:     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
 64:     needs:
 65:       - ConfirmDestruction
 66:       - SetRegion
 67:     permissions:
 68:       contents: write
 69:       actions: write
 70:       id-token: write
 71:     env:
 72:       AWS_REGION: ${{ needs.SetRegion.outputs.region_code }}
 73:       # Note: TF_VAR environment variables are case-sensitive and must match variable names in variables.tf
 74:       # Secrets in GitHub remain uppercase, but environment variables must be lowercase
 75:       TF_VAR_openldap_admin_password: ${{ secrets.TF_VAR_OPENLDAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD }}
 76:       TF_VAR_openldap_config_password: ${{ secrets.TF_VAR_OPENLDAP_CONFIG_PASSWORD }}
 77:     defaults:
 78:       run:
 79:         working-directory: ./application_infra
 80:     steps:
 81:       - name: Checkout the repo code
 82:         uses: actions/checkout@v4
 83:       - name: Setup terraform
 84:         uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
 85:         with:
 86:           terraform_version: 1.14.0
 87:       - name: Install jq
 88:         run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y jq
 89:       - name: Export environment variables for set-k8s-env.sh
 90:         run: |
 91:           # Export required variables for set-k8s-env.sh (matching setup-application-infra.sh)
 92:           echo "BACKEND_FILE=backend.hcl" >> $GITHUB_ENV
 93:           echo "VARIABLES_FILE=variables.tfvars" >> $GITHUB_ENV
 94:           echo "ENVIRONMENT=${{ inputs.environment }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
 95:           echo "TERRAFORM_WORKSPACE=${{ env.AWS_REGION }}-${{ inputs.environment }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
 96:           echo "BACKEND_PREFIX=${{ vars.BACKEND_PREFIX }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
 97:           # Determine deployment account role ARN based on environment
 98:           if [ "${{ inputs.environment }}" = "prod" ]; then
 99:             echo "DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN=${{ secrets.AWS_PRODUCTION_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
100:           else
101:             echo "DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN=${{ secrets.AWS_DEVELOPMENT_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
102:           fi
103:           echo "EXTERNAL_ID=${{ secrets.AWS_ASSUME_EXTERNAL_ID }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
104:           # Export state account role ARN for Route53/ACM access
105:           echo "STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN=${{ secrets.AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
106:       - name: Configure AWS credentials (State Account)
107:         uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
108:         with:
109:           role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN }}
110:           role-session-name: GitHubActions-ApplicationInfraDestroy-State
111:           aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
112:       - name: Create backend.hcl from placeholder
113:         run: |
114:           # Only create if it doesn't exist (matching setup-application-infra.sh behavior)
115:           if [ ! -f "backend.hcl" ]; then
116:             cp tfstate-backend-values-template.hcl backend.hcl
117:             sed -i -e "s|<BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME>|${{ vars.BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME }}|g" \
118:             -e "s|<APPLICATION_INFRA_PREFIX>|${{ vars.APPLICATION_INFRA_PREFIX }}|g" \
119:             -e "s|<AWS_REGION>|${{ env.AWS_REGION }}|g" \
120:             backend.hcl
121:             echo "Created backend.hcl:"
122:             cat backend.hcl
123:           else
124:             echo "backend.hcl already exists. Skipping creation."
125:           fi
126:       - name: Terraform init
127:         run: terraform init -backend-config=backend.hcl
128:       - name: Terraform workspace
129:         run: |
130:           WORKSPACE="${{ env.AWS_REGION }}-${{ inputs.environment }}"
131:           terraform workspace select $WORKSPACE || terraform workspace new $WORKSPACE
132:       - name: Terraform validate
133:         run: terraform validate
134:       - name: Set Kubernetes environment variables
135:         run: |
136:           # set-k8s-env.sh expects State Account credentials to be active for S3 operations
137:           # It will assume Deployment Account role internally for EKS operations
138:           chmod +x ../scripts/set-k8s-env.sh
139:           source ../scripts/set-k8s-env.sh
140:           # Export as TF_VAR_ environment variables for Terraform
141:           echo "TF_VAR_kubernetes_master=$KUBERNETES_MASTER" >> $GITHUB_ENV
142:           echo "TF_VAR_kube_config_path=$KUBE_CONFIG_PATH" >> $GITHUB_ENV
143:       - name: Configure AWS credentials (State Account for Terraform)
144:         uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
145:         with:
146:           role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN }}
147:           role-session-name: GitHubActions-ApplicationInfraDestroy-Terraform
148:           aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
149:       - name: Create backend_infra backend.hcl from placeholder
150:         run: |
151:           # Create backend_infra/backend.hcl if it doesn't exist
152:           # This is needed for application_infra/providers.tf to read backend_infra state configuration
153:           if [ ! -f "../backend_infra/backend.hcl" ]; then
154:             cp ../backend_infra/tfstate-backend-values-template.hcl ../backend_infra/backend.hcl
155:             sed -i -e "s|<BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME>|${{ vars.BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME }}|g" \
156:             -e "s|<BACKEND_PREFIX>|${{ vars.BACKEND_PREFIX }}|g" \
157:             -e "s|<AWS_REGION>|${{ env.AWS_REGION }}|g" \
158:             ../backend_infra/backend.hcl
159:             echo "Created ../backend_infra/backend.hcl:"
160:             cat ../backend_infra/backend.hcl
161:           else
162:             echo "../backend_infra/backend.hcl already exists. Skipping creation."
163:           fi
164:       - name: Ensure assume-github-role.sh is executable
165:         run: chmod +x ../scripts/assume-github-role.sh
166:       - name: Ensure get-eks-token.sh is executable
167:         run: chmod +x ../scripts/get-eks-token.sh
168:       - name: Terraform plan destroy
169:         run: terraform plan -var-file="variables.tfvars" -destroy -out terraform.tfplan
170:       - name: Destroy application infrastructure
171:         run: terraform apply -auto-approve terraform.tfplan
172:       - name: Configure AWS credentials (Deployment Account for kubectl)
173:         uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
174:         with:
175:           role-to-assume: ${{ inputs.environment == 'prod' && secrets.AWS_PRODUCTION_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN || secrets.AWS_DEVELOPMENT_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN }}
176:           role-session-name: GitHubActions-ApplicationInfraDestroy-PVC-Cleanup
177:           aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
178:       - name: Clean up PVCs
179:         continue-on-error: true
180:         run: |
181:           # Helm does not delete PVCs by default to prevent data loss
182:           # We need to manually delete them to trigger the reclaim policy (Delete)
183:           # which will also delete the underlying EBS volumes
184:           echo "Checking for remaining PVCs in ldap namespace..."
185:           # Use the kubeconfig from set-k8s-env.sh
186:           export KUBECONFIG="${TF_VAR_kube_config_path:-$HOME/.kube/config}"
187:           # Check if kubeconfig file exists
188:           if [ ! -f "$KUBECONFIG" ]; then
189:             echo "::warning::Kubeconfig file not found at $KUBECONFIG. Skipping PVC cleanup."
190:             echo "This is normal if the cluster was already destroyed or kubeconfig was not created."
191:             exit 0
192:           fi
193:           # Check if kubectl is available
194:           if ! command -v kubectl &> /dev/null; then
195:             echo "Installing kubectl..."
196:             curl -LO "https://dl.k8s.io/release/$(curl -L -s https://dl.k8s.io/release/stable.txt)/bin/linux/amd64/kubectl"
197:             chmod +x kubectl
198:             sudo mv kubectl /usr/local/bin/
199:           fi
200:           # Test cluster connectivity
201:           if ! kubectl cluster-info &>/dev/null; then
202:             echo "::warning::Cannot connect to cluster. Skipping PVC cleanup."
203:             echo "This is normal if the cluster was already destroyed."
204:             exit 0
205:           fi
206:           # Check if namespace exists and count PVCs
207:           if kubectl get namespace ldap &>/dev/null; then
208:             PVC_COUNT=$(kubectl get pvc -n ldap --no-headers 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ' || echo "0")
209:             if [ "$PVC_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
210:               echo "Found ${PVC_COUNT} PVC(s) remaining in ldap namespace."
211:               echo "Helm does not delete PVCs by default. Deleting PVCs now..."
212:               echo "This will also delete the underlying EBS volumes (reclaim_policy=Delete)."
213:               # Use --wait=false so we don't block: EBS detach/delete can take minutes.
214:               # PVCs will finish terminating and EBS volumes will be reclaimed asynchronously.
215:               if kubectl delete pvc --all -n ldap --wait=false; then
216:                 echo "✅ PVC delete requested. They will terminate in the background."
217:               else
218:                 echo "::warning::Failed to delete PVCs. You may need to delete them manually:"
219:                 echo "  kubectl delete pvc --all -n ldap --wait=false"
220:               fi
221:             else
222:               echo "No PVCs found in ldap namespace (already cleaned up)."
223:             fi
224:           else
225:             echo "ldap namespace does not exist (already cleaned up or never created)."
226:           fi
227:         env:
228:           KUBECONFIG: ${{ env.TF_VAR_kube_config_path }}
```

## File: .github/workflows/02-application_infra_provisioning.yaml
```yaml
  1: name: 02 - Application Infra Provisioning
  2: # Required GitHub Repository Secrets:
  3: # - AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN: IAM role ARN for backend state operations
  4: # - AWS_PRODUCTION_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN: IAM role ARN for production deployments
  5: # - AWS_DEVELOPMENT_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN: IAM role ARN for development deployments
  6: # - AWS_ASSUME_EXTERNAL_ID: ExternalId for cross-account role assumption security
  7: # - TF_VAR_OPENLDAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD: OpenLDAP admin password
  8: # - TF_VAR_OPENLDAP_CONFIG_PASSWORD: OpenLDAP config password
  9: #
 10: # Note: GitHub workflows use repository secrets, while bash scripts use AWS Secrets Manager.
 11: # The secrets listed above must be configured in GitHub repository settings.
 12: on:
 13:   workflow_dispatch:
 14:     inputs:
 15:       region:
 16:         description: 'Select AWS Region'
 17:         required: true
 18:         type: choice
 19:         default: 'us-east-1: N. Virginia'
 20:         options:
 21:           - 'us-east-1: N. Virginia'
 22:           - 'us-east-2: Ohio'
 23:       environment:
 24:         description: 'Select Environment'
 25:         required: true
 26:         type: choice
 27:         default: prod
 28:         options:
 29:           - prod
 30:           - dev
 31: jobs:
 32:   SetRegion:
 33:     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
 34:     permissions:
 35:       contents: read
 36:     outputs:
 37:       region_code: ${{ steps.set_region.outputs.region_code }}
 38:     steps:
 39:       - name: Set Region
 40:         id: set_region
 41:         run: |
 42:           SELECTED_REGION="${{ inputs.region }}"
 43:           echo "region_code=${SELECTED_REGION%%:*}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
 44:   InfraProvision:
 45:     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
 46:     needs:
 47:       - SetRegion
 48:     permissions:
 49:       contents: write
 50:       actions: write
 51:       id-token: write
 52:     env:
 53:       AWS_REGION: ${{ needs.SetRegion.outputs.region_code }}
 54:       # Note: TF_VAR environment variables are case-sensitive and must match variable names in variables.tf
 55:       # Secrets in GitHub remain uppercase, but environment variables must be lowercase
 56:       TF_VAR_openldap_admin_password: ${{ secrets.TF_VAR_OPENLDAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD }}
 57:       TF_VAR_openldap_config_password: ${{ secrets.TF_VAR_OPENLDAP_CONFIG_PASSWORD }}
 58:     defaults:
 59:       run:
 60:         working-directory: ./application_infra
 61:     steps:
 62:       - name: Checkout the repo code
 63:         uses: actions/checkout@v4
 64:       - name: Setup terraform
 65:         uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
 66:         with:
 67:           terraform_version: 1.14.0
 68:       - name: Install jq
 69:         run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y jq
 70:       - name: Export environment variables for set-k8s-env.sh
 71:         run: |
 72:           # Export required variables for set-k8s-env.sh (matching setup-application-infra.sh)
 73:           echo "BACKEND_FILE=backend.hcl" >> $GITHUB_ENV
 74:           echo "VARIABLES_FILE=variables.tfvars" >> $GITHUB_ENV
 75:           echo "ENVIRONMENT=${{ inputs.environment }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
 76:           echo "TERRAFORM_WORKSPACE=${{ env.AWS_REGION }}-${{ inputs.environment }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
 77:           echo "BACKEND_PREFIX=${{ vars.BACKEND_PREFIX }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
 78:           # Determine deployment account role ARN based on environment
 79:           if [ "${{ inputs.environment }}" = "prod" ]; then
 80:             echo "DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN=${{ secrets.AWS_PRODUCTION_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
 81:           else
 82:             echo "DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN=${{ secrets.AWS_DEVELOPMENT_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
 83:           fi
 84:           echo "EXTERNAL_ID=${{ secrets.AWS_ASSUME_EXTERNAL_ID }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
 85:           # Export state account role ARN for Route53/ACM access
 86:           echo "STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN=${{ secrets.AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
 87:       - name: Setup Docker Buildx
 88:         uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
 89:       - name: Configure AWS credentials (State Account)
 90:         uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
 91:         with:
 92:           role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN }}
 93:           role-session-name: GitHubActions-ApplicationInfraProvision-State
 94:           aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
 95:       - name: Create backend.hcl from placeholder
 96:         run: |
 97:           # Only create if it doesn't exist (matching setup-application-infra.sh behavior)
 98:           if [ ! -f "backend.hcl" ]; then
 99:             cp tfstate-backend-values-template.hcl backend.hcl
100:             sed -i -e "s|<BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME>|${{ vars.BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME }}|g" \
101:             -e "s|<APPLICATION_INFRA_PREFIX>|${{ vars.APPLICATION_INFRA_PREFIX }}|g" \
102:             -e "s|<AWS_REGION>|${{ env.AWS_REGION }}|g" \
103:             backend.hcl
104:             echo "Created backend.hcl:"
105:             cat backend.hcl
106:           else
107:             echo "backend.hcl already exists. Skipping creation."
108:           fi
109:       - name: Terraform init
110:         run: terraform init -backend-config=backend.hcl
111:       - name: Terraform workspace
112:         run: |
113:           WORKSPACE="${{ env.AWS_REGION }}-${{ inputs.environment }}"
114:           terraform workspace select $WORKSPACE || terraform workspace new $WORKSPACE
115:       - name: Terraform validate
116:         run: terraform validate
117:       - name: Mirror Docker images to ECR
118:         run: |
119:           # Mirror third-party images to ECR (if not already present)
120:           # This script:
121:           # 1. Fetches ECR URL from backend_infra state (using State Account credentials)
122:           # 2. Assumes Deployment Account role for ECR operations
123:           # 3. Checks if images exist, mirrors only missing ones
124:           chmod +x ../scripts/mirror-images-to-ecr.sh
125:           ../scripts/mirror-images-to-ecr.sh
126:       - name: Set Kubernetes environment variables
127:         run: |
128:           # set-k8s-env.sh expects State Account credentials to be active for S3 operations
129:           # It will assume Deployment Account role internally for EKS operations
130:           chmod +x ../scripts/set-k8s-env.sh
131:           source ../scripts/set-k8s-env.sh
132:           # Export as TF_VAR_ environment variables for Terraform
133:           echo "TF_VAR_kubernetes_master=$KUBERNETES_MASTER" >> $GITHUB_ENV
134:           echo "TF_VAR_kube_config_path=$KUBE_CONFIG_PATH" >> $GITHUB_ENV
135:       - name: Configure AWS credentials (State Account for Terraform)
136:         uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
137:         with:
138:           role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN }}
139:           role-session-name: GitHubActions-ApplicationInfraProvision-Terraform
140:           aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
141:       - name: Create backend_infra backend.hcl from placeholder
142:         run: |
143:           # Create backend_infra/backend.hcl if it doesn't exist
144:           # This is needed for application_infra/providers.tf to read backend_infra state configuration
145:           if [ ! -f "../backend_infra/backend.hcl" ]; then
146:             cp ../backend_infra/tfstate-backend-values-template.hcl ../backend_infra/backend.hcl
147:             sed -i -e "s|<BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME>|${{ vars.BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME }}|g" \
148:             -e "s|<BACKEND_PREFIX>|${{ vars.BACKEND_PREFIX }}|g" \
149:             -e "s|<AWS_REGION>|${{ env.AWS_REGION }}|g" \
150:             ../backend_infra/backend.hcl
151:             echo "Created ../backend_infra/backend.hcl:"
152:             cat ../backend_infra/backend.hcl
153:           else
154:             echo "../backend_infra/backend.hcl already exists. Skipping creation."
155:           fi
156:       - name: Ensure assume-github-role.sh is executable
157:         run: chmod +x ../scripts/assume-github-role.sh
158:       - name: Ensure get-eks-token.sh is executable
159:         run: chmod +x ../scripts/get-eks-token.sh
160:       - name: Terraform plan
161:         run: terraform plan -var-file="variables.tfvars" -out terraform.tfplan
162:       - name: Provision application infrastructure
163:         run: terraform apply -auto-approve terraform.tfplan
164:       - name: Log troubleshooting hint on failure
165:         if: failure()
166:         run: |
167:           echo "## Application Infra deployment failed" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
168:           echo "See **application_infra/TROUBLESHOOTING.md** for ArgoCD and OpenLDAP failure causes and fixes." >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
169:           echo "Expand the failed step above for the exact Terraform/Helm error." >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
```

## File: .github/workflows/04-application_destroying.yaml
```yaml
  1: name: 04 - Application Destroying
  2: # Required GitHub Repository Secrets:
  3: # - AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN: IAM role ARN for backend state operations
  4: # - AWS_PRODUCTION_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN: IAM role ARN for production deployments
  5: # - AWS_DEVELOPMENT_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN: IAM role ARN for development deployments
  6: # - AWS_ASSUME_EXTERNAL_ID: ExternalId for cross-account role assumption security
  7: # - TF_VAR_POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD: PostgreSQL database password
  8: # - TF_VAR_REDIS_PASSWORD: Redis password for SMS OTP storage
  9: # - TF_VAR_OPENLDAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD: OpenLDAP admin password (for backend ldap-admin-secret and destroy)
 10: #
 11: # Optional (if first admin seed was used, set these so Terraform can destroy admin-seed resources):
 12: # - ADMIN_SEED_USERNAME, ADMIN_SEED_EMAIL, ADMIN_SEED_FIRST_NAME, ADMIN_SEED_LAST_NAME
 13: # - ADMIN_SEED_PHONE_COUNTRY_CODE, ADMIN_SEED_PHONE_NUMBER
 14: #
 15: # Note: GitHub workflows use repository secrets, while bash scripts use AWS Secrets Manager.
 16: # The secrets listed above must be configured in GitHub repository settings.
 17: on:
 18:   workflow_dispatch:
 19:     inputs:
 20:       region:
 21:         description: 'Select AWS Region'
 22:         required: true
 23:         type: choice
 24:         default: 'us-east-1: N. Virginia'
 25:         options:
 26:           - 'us-east-1: N. Virginia'
 27:           - 'us-east-2: Ohio'
 28:       environment:
 29:         description: 'Select Environment'
 30:         required: true
 31:         type: choice
 32:         default: prod
 33:         options:
 34:           - prod
 35:           - dev
 36:       confirmation:
 37:         description: 'Type "yes" to confirm destruction (required)'
 38:         required: true
 39:         type: string
 40: jobs:
 41:   ConfirmDestruction:
 42:     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
 43:     permissions: {}
 44:     steps:
 45:       - name: Confirm destruction
 46:         run: |
 47:           if [ "${{ inputs.confirmation }}" != "yes" ]; then
 48:             echo "ERROR: Confirmation required. You must type 'yes' to proceed with destruction."
 49:             echo "Received: '${{ inputs.confirmation }}'"
 50:             exit 1
 51:           fi
 52:           echo "✓ Confirmation received. Proceeding with destruction..."
 53:   SetRegion:
 54:     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
 55:     needs:
 56:       - ConfirmDestruction
 57:     permissions:
 58:       contents: read
 59:     outputs:
 60:       region_code: ${{ steps.set_region.outputs.region_code }}
 61:     steps:
 62:       - name: Set Region
 63:         id: set_region
 64:         run: |
 65:           SELECTED_REGION="${{ inputs.region }}"
 66:           echo "region_code=${SELECTED_REGION%%:*}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
 67:   ApplicationDestroy:
 68:     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
 69:     needs:
 70:       - ConfirmDestruction
 71:       - SetRegion
 72:     permissions:
 73:       contents: write
 74:       actions: write
 75:       id-token: write
 76:     env:
 77:       AWS_REGION: ${{ needs.SetRegion.outputs.region_code }}
 78:       # Note: TF_VAR environment variables are case-sensitive and must match variable names in variables.tf
 79:       # Secrets in GitHub remain uppercase, but environment variables must be lowercase
 80:       # PostgreSQL password for User management database
 81:       TF_VAR_postgresql_database_password: ${{ secrets.TF_VAR_POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD }}
 82:       # Redis password for SMS OTP storage
 83:       TF_VAR_redis_password: ${{ secrets.TF_VAR_REDIS_PASSWORD }}
 84:       # OpenLDAP admin password for backend LDAP bind (ldap-admin-secret) and for destroy
 85:       TF_VAR_openldap_admin_password: ${{ secrets.TF_VAR_OPENLDAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD }}
 86:       # First admin seed (optional; pass so Terraform can destroy admin-seed secret and Job if present)
 87:       TF_VAR_admin_seed_username: ${{ secrets.ADMIN_SEED_USERNAME }}
 88:       TF_VAR_admin_seed_email: ${{ secrets.ADMIN_SEED_EMAIL }}
 89:       TF_VAR_admin_seed_first_name: ${{ secrets.ADMIN_SEED_FIRST_NAME }}
 90:       TF_VAR_admin_seed_last_name: ${{ secrets.ADMIN_SEED_LAST_NAME }}
 91:       TF_VAR_admin_seed_phone_country_code: ${{ secrets.ADMIN_SEED_PHONE_COUNTRY_CODE }}
 92:       TF_VAR_admin_seed_phone_number: ${{ secrets.ADMIN_SEED_PHONE_NUMBER }}
 93:     defaults:
 94:       run:
 95:         working-directory: ./application
 96:     steps:
 97:       - name: Checkout the repo code
 98:         uses: actions/checkout@v4
 99:       - name: Setup terraform
100:         uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
101:         with:
102:           terraform_version: 1.14.0
103:       - name: Export environment variables for set-k8s-env.sh
104:         run: |
105:           # Export required variables for set-k8s-env.sh (matching setup-application.sh)
106:           echo "BACKEND_FILE=backend.hcl" >> $GITHUB_ENV
107:           echo "VARIABLES_FILE=variables.tfvars" >> $GITHUB_ENV
108:           echo "ENVIRONMENT=${{ inputs.environment }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
109:           echo "TERRAFORM_WORKSPACE=${{ env.AWS_REGION }}-${{ inputs.environment }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
110:           echo "BACKEND_PREFIX=${{ vars.BACKEND_PREFIX }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
111:           # Determine deployment account role ARN based on environment
112:           if [ "${{ inputs.environment }}" = "prod" ]; then
113:             echo "DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN=${{ secrets.AWS_PRODUCTION_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
114:           else
115:             echo "DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN=${{ secrets.AWS_DEVELOPMENT_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
116:           fi
117:           echo "EXTERNAL_ID=${{ secrets.AWS_ASSUME_EXTERNAL_ID }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
118:           # Export state account role ARN for Route53/ACM access
119:           echo "STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN=${{ secrets.AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
120:       - name: Configure AWS credentials (State Account)
121:         uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
122:         with:
123:           role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN }}
124:           role-session-name: GitHubActions-ApplicationDestroy-State
125:           aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
126:       - name: Create backend.hcl from placeholder
127:         run: |
128:           # Only create if it doesn't exist (matching setup-application.sh behavior)
129:           if [ ! -f "backend.hcl" ]; then
130:             cp tfstate-backend-values-template.hcl backend.hcl
131:             sed -i -e "s|<BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME>|${{ vars.BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME }}|g" \
132:             -e "s|<APPLICATION_PREFIX>|${{ vars.APPLICATION_PREFIX }}|g" \
133:             -e "s|<AWS_REGION>|${{ env.AWS_REGION }}|g" \
134:             backend.hcl
135:             echo "Created backend.hcl:"
136:             cat backend.hcl
137:           else
138:             echo "backend.hcl already exists. Skipping creation."
139:           fi
140:       - name: Create backend_infra backend.hcl from placeholder
141:         run: |
142:           # Create backend_infra/backend.hcl if it doesn't exist
143:           # This is needed for application/providers.tf to read backend_infra state configuration
144:           if [ ! -f "../backend_infra/backend.hcl" ]; then
145:             cp ../backend_infra/tfstate-backend-values-template.hcl ../backend_infra/backend.hcl
146:             sed -i -e "s|<BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME>|${{ vars.BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME }}|g" \
147:             -e "s|<BACKEND_PREFIX>|${{ vars.BACKEND_PREFIX }}|g" \
148:             -e "s|<AWS_REGION>|${{ env.AWS_REGION }}|g" \
149:             ../backend_infra/backend.hcl
150:             echo "Created ../backend_infra/backend.hcl:"
151:             cat ../backend_infra/backend.hcl
152:           else
153:             echo "../backend_infra/backend.hcl already exists. Skipping creation."
154:           fi
155:       - name: Create application_infra backend.hcl from placeholder
156:         run: |
157:           # Create application_infra/backend.hcl if it doesn't exist
158:           # This is needed for application/providers.tf to read application_infra state configuration
159:           if [ ! -f "../application_infra/backend.hcl" ]; then
160:             cp ../application_infra/tfstate-backend-values-template.hcl ../application_infra/backend.hcl
161:             sed -i -e "s|<BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME>|${{ vars.BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME }}|g" \
162:             -e "s|<APPLICATION_INFRA_PREFIX>|${{ vars.APPLICATION_INFRA_PREFIX }}|g" \
163:             -e "s|<AWS_REGION>|${{ env.AWS_REGION }}|g" \
164:             ../application_infra/backend.hcl
165:             echo "Created ../application_infra/backend.hcl:"
166:             cat ../application_infra/backend.hcl
167:           else
168:             echo "../application_infra/backend.hcl already exists. Skipping creation."
169:           fi
170:       - name: Terraform init
171:         run: terraform init -backend-config=backend.hcl
172:       - name: Terraform workspace
173:         run: |
174:           WORKSPACE="${{ env.AWS_REGION }}-${{ inputs.environment }}"
175:           terraform workspace select $WORKSPACE || terraform workspace new $WORKSPACE
176:       - name: Terraform validate
177:         run: terraform validate
178:       - name: Set Kubernetes environment variables
179:         run: |
180:           # set-k8s-env.sh expects State Account credentials to be active for S3 operations
181:           # It will assume Deployment Account role internally for EKS operations
182:           # Use the infrastructure's set-k8s-env.sh script (shared between infrastructure and application)
183:           chmod +x ../scripts/set-k8s-env.sh
184:           source ../scripts/set-k8s-env.sh
185:           # Export as TF_VAR_ environment variables for Terraform
186:           echo "TF_VAR_kubernetes_master=$KUBERNETES_MASTER" >> $GITHUB_ENV
187:           echo "TF_VAR_kube_config_path=$KUBE_CONFIG_PATH" >> $GITHUB_ENV
188:       - name: Extract image tags from Helm values
189:         run: |
190:           # Extract backend image tag
191:           # Note: For destroy operations, we use empty string as fallback (passes validation)
192:           # since the resources being destroyed may not need valid tags
193:           BACKEND_VALUES_FILE="backend/helm/ldap-2fa-backend/values.yaml"
194:           if [ ! -f "$BACKEND_VALUES_FILE" ]; then
195:             echo "::warning::Backend Helm values file not found. Using empty string for destroy."
196:             echo "TF_VAR_backend_image_tag=" >> $GITHUB_ENV
197:           else
198:             BACKEND_IMAGE_TAG=$(grep -E '^[[:space:]]*tag:' "$BACKEND_VALUES_FILE" | head -n 1 | sed -E 's/.*tag:[[:space:]]*//' | sed 's/^"//' | sed "s/^'//" | sed 's/"$//' | sed "s/'$//" | tr -d '\r')
199:             if [ -z "$BACKEND_IMAGE_TAG" ] || [ "$BACKEND_IMAGE_TAG" = "latest" ]; then
200:               echo "::warning::Could not extract valid backend image tag (got: '${BACKEND_IMAGE_TAG:-empty}'). Using empty string for destroy."
201:               echo "TF_VAR_backend_image_tag=" >> $GITHUB_ENV
202:             else
203:               echo "TF_VAR_backend_image_tag=$BACKEND_IMAGE_TAG" >> $GITHUB_ENV
204:               echo "✅ Using backend image tag: $BACKEND_IMAGE_TAG"
205:             fi
206:           fi
207:           # Extract frontend image tag
208:           FRONTEND_VALUES_FILE="frontend/helm/ldap-2fa-frontend/values.yaml"
209:           if [ ! -f "$FRONTEND_VALUES_FILE" ]; then
210:             echo "::warning::Frontend Helm values file not found. Using empty string for destroy."
211:             echo "TF_VAR_frontend_image_tag=" >> $GITHUB_ENV
212:           else
213:             FRONTEND_IMAGE_TAG=$(grep -E '^[[:space:]]*tag:' "$FRONTEND_VALUES_FILE" | head -n 1 | sed -E 's/.*tag:[[:space:]]*//' | sed 's/^"//' | sed "s/^'//" | sed 's/"$//' | sed "s/'$//" | tr -d '\r')
214:             if [ -z "$FRONTEND_IMAGE_TAG" ] || [ "$FRONTEND_IMAGE_TAG" = "latest" ]; then
215:               echo "::warning::Could not extract valid frontend image tag (got: '${FRONTEND_IMAGE_TAG:-empty}'). Using empty string for destroy."
216:               echo "TF_VAR_frontend_image_tag=" >> $GITHUB_ENV
217:             else
218:               echo "TF_VAR_frontend_image_tag=$FRONTEND_IMAGE_TAG" >> $GITHUB_ENV
219:               echo "✅ Using frontend image tag: $FRONTEND_IMAGE_TAG"
220:             fi
221:           fi
222:       - name: Configure AWS credentials (State Account for Terraform)
223:         uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
224:         with:
225:           role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN }}
226:           role-session-name: GitHubActions-ApplicationDestroy-Terraform
227:           aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
228:       - name: Ensure get-eks-token.sh is executable
229:         run: chmod +x ../scripts/get-eks-token.sh
230:       - name: Terraform plan destroy
231:         run: terraform plan -var-file="variables.tfvars" -destroy -out terraform.tfplan
232:       - name: Destroy application
233:         run: terraform apply -auto-approve terraform.tfplan
```
