```hcl
 61: #
 62: # # Kubernetes Service for the App
 63: # resource "kubernetes_service_v1" "service_alb" {
 64: #   metadata {
 65: #     name      = local.service_alb_name
 66: #     namespace = "default"
 67: #     labels = {
 68: #       app = var.app_name
 69: #     }
 70: #   }
 71: #
 72: #   spec {

 75: #     }
 76: #

 79: #       target_port = 8080
 80: #     }
 81: #
 82: #     type = "ClusterIP"
 83: #   }
 84: # }
 85: 
 86: # The IngressClassParams resource is a custom Kubernetes resource (CRD) provided by EKS Auto Mode.
 87: # We use the `kubernetes_manifest` resource to manage it in a Terraform-native way.
 88: #
 89: # ⚠️ RISKS AND MITIGATION:
 90: #
 91: # 1. CRD Availability Risk:
 92: #    - The IngressClassParams CRD is installed by EKS Auto Mode when the cluster is created
 93: #    - If Terraform runs before Auto Mode finishes initializing, the CRD may not exist
 94: #    - This causes failures during `terraform apply` (not plan, since we can't check CRD existence in plan)
 95: #
 96: # 2. Mitigation Strategies:
 97: #    a) Ensure cluster is fully ready: The Kubernetes provider uses data sources that require
 98: #       the cluster to exist, but doesn't guarantee CRD availability
 99: #    b) Use time_sleep for initial deployments: Adds a delay to allow Auto Mode to initialize
100: #    c) Retry logic: Terraform will retry on apply, but you may need to run apply multiple times
101: #    d) Manual verification: Check CRD exists: `kubectl get crd ingressclassparams.eks.amazonaws.com`
102: #
103: # 3. Alternative Approach:
104: #    If you experience frequent CRD availability issues, consider:
105: #    - Using the original null_resource + kubectl approach (more forgiving)
106: #    - Adding a data source to check CRD existence first (requires kubectl provider)
107: #    - Using a Helm chart that handles CRD installation
108: #
109: # Annotation Strategy (cluster-wide defaults):
110: # - IngressClassParams defines cluster-wide defaults that apply to all Ingresses using this IngressClass
111: # - EKS Auto Mode IngressClassParams supports: scheme, ipAddressType, group.name, and certificateARNs
112: # - Per-Ingress ALB configuration (load-balancer-name, listen-ports, ssl-redirect, target-type)
113: #   should be defined at the Ingress level via annotations
114: # - All Ingresses using this IngressClass inherit cluster-wide settings from IngressClassParams
115: 
116: # Optional: Add a delay for initial cluster setup to allow EKS Auto Mode to install CRDs
117: #
118: # IMPORTANT: There is NO Terraform resource that represents "CRD is installed"
119: # The IngressClassParams CRD is installed asynchronously by EKS Auto Mode after cluster creation.
120: # The cluster resource (module.eks in backend_infra) completes before CRDs are guaranteed to exist.
121: #
122: # What we're actually waiting for:
123: # - NOT a Terraform resource (there isn't one for CRD availability)
124: # - The asynchronous EKS Auto Mode process to install the CRD
125: # - This typically happens within seconds of cluster creation, but isn't guaranteed
126: #
127: # Set wait_for_crd = true for initial deployments, false after cluster is established
128: resource "time_sleep" "wait_for_eks_auto_mode" {
129:   # Always create the resource, but use 0s duration when wait_for_crd is false
130:   # This allows us to always reference it in depends_on (which requires a static list)
131:   create_duration = var.wait_for_crd ? "2m" : "0s"
132: 
133:   # Trigger recreation if cluster changes (helps with new cluster deployments)
134:   triggers = {
135:     cluster_name = var.cluster_name
136:   }
137: }
138: 
139: # If apply fails with "resource ... already exists", the IngressClassParams exists in the
140: # cluster but is not in Terraform state. Import it so Terraform can manage/update it:
141: #
142: #   terraform import 'module.alb[0].kubernetes_manifest.ingressclassparams_alb' \
143: #     "apiVersion=eks.amazonaws.com/v1,kind=IngressClassParams,name=<name>"
144: #
145: # Replace <name> with the value from the error (e.g. talo-tf-us-east-1-icp-alb-ldap-prod)
146: # or with the module name: prefix-region-ingressclassparams_alb_name-env (e.g. talo-tf-us-east-1-icp-alb-ldap-prod).
147: resource "kubernetes_manifest" "ingressclassparams_alb" {
148:   # Wait for:
149:   # 1. The Kubernetes provider to be configured (implicit via data.aws_eks_cluster)
150:   # 2. Optionally, a delay to allow EKS Auto Mode to install the CRD
151:   #
152:   # Note: We can't explicitly depend on the CRD existing because there's no Terraform
153:   # resource for it. The time_sleep is a workaround for the asynchronous CRD installation.
154:   # When wait_for_crd is false, time_sleep has 0s duration (no actual delay).
155:   depends_on = [time_sleep.wait_for_eks_auto_mode]
156: 
157:   manifest = {
158:     apiVersion = "eks.amazonaws.com/v1"
159:     kind       = "IngressClassParams"
160:     metadata = {
161:       name = local.ingressclassparams_alb_name
162:     }
163:     spec = merge(
164:       {
165:         scheme        = var.alb_scheme
166:         ipAddressType = var.alb_ip_address_type
167:         group = {
168:           name = var.alb_group_name
169:         }
170:       },
171:       var.acm_certificate_arn != null && var.acm_certificate_arn != "" ? {
172:         certificateARNs = [var.acm_certificate_arn]
173:       } : {}
174:     )
175:   }
176: 
177:   # Wait for the resource to be created and ready
178:   # This ensures the resource exists before dependent resources are created
179:   wait {
180:     fields = {
181:       "metadata.name" = local.ingressclassparams_alb_name
182:     }
183:   }
184: 
185:   # Use server-side apply to handle conflicts better
186:   # This is safer for custom resources that might be managed elsewhere
187:   computed_fields = ["metadata.labels", "metadata.annotations"]
188: }
189: 
190: # IngressClass binds Ingress resources to EKS Auto Mode controller
191: # and references IngressClassParams for cluster-wide ALB defaults
192: resource "kubernetes_ingress_class_v1" "ingressclass_alb" {
193:   depends_on = [kubernetes_manifest.ingressclassparams_alb]
194:   metadata {
195:     name = local.ingressclass_alb_name
196: 
197:     # Use this annotation to set an IngressClass as Default
198:     # If an Ingress doesn't specify a class, it will use the Default
199:     annotations = {
200:       "ingressclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class" = "true"
201:     }
202:   }
203: 
204:   spec {
205:     # Configures the IngressClass to use EKS Auto Mode (built-in load balancer driver)
206:     controller = "eks.amazonaws.com/alb"
207:     parameters {
208:       api_group = "eks.amazonaws.com"
209:       kind      = "IngressClassParams"
210:       # References IngressClassParams which contains cluster-wide defaults (scheme, ipAddressType, group.name, certificateARNs)
211:       name = local.ingressclassparams_alb_name
212:     }
213:   }
214: }
```

## File: application_infra/modules/network-policies/main.tf
```hcl
  1: # Network Policies for securing internal cluster communication
  2: # These policies enforce secure communication between all services in the namespace
  3: # Generic approach: Any service can talk to any service, but only on secure ports
  4: 
  5: # Generic Network Policy: Allow secure inter-pod communication within namespace
  6: # This policy applies to ALL pods in the namespace and allows them to communicate
  7: # with each other, but only on secure/encrypted ports
  8: resource "kubernetes_network_policy_v1" "namespace_secure_communication" {
  9:   metadata {
 10:     name      = "namespace-secure-communication"
 11:     namespace = var.namespace
 12:   }
 13: 
 14:   spec {
 15:     # Apply to all pods in the namespace
 16:     pod_selector {}
 17:     policy_types = ["Ingress", "Egress"]
 18: 
 19:     # Ingress: Allow traffic from any pod in the same namespace on LDAP and secure ports
 20:     ingress {
 21:       # Allow from any pod in the same namespace
 22:       from {
 23:         pod_selector {}
 24:       }
 25:       ports {
 26:         port     = "389"
 27:         protocol = "TCP"
 28:       }
 29:     }
 30: 
 31:     ingress {
 32:       from {
 33:         pod_selector {}
 34:       }
 35:       ports {
 36:         port     = "443"
 37:         protocol = "TCP"
 38:       }
 39:     }
 40: 
 41:     ingress {
 42:       from {
 43:         pod_selector {}
 44:       }
 45:       ports {
 46:         port     = "636"
 47:         protocol = "TCP"
 48:       }
 49:     }
 50: 
 51:     # Allow HTTPS on common alternative ports if needed
 52:     ingress {
 53:       from {
 54:         pod_selector {}
 55:       }
 56:       ports {
 57:         port     = "8443"
 58:         protocol = "TCP"
 59:       }
 60:     }
 61: 
 62:     # Ingress: Allow traffic from any pod in other namespaces on LDAP and secure ports
 63:     # This enables cross-namespace communication for LDAP service access
 64:     ingress {
 65:       # Allow from any pod in any namespace
 66:       from {
 67:         namespace_selector {}
 68:       }
 69:       ports {
 70:         port     = "389"
 71:         protocol = "TCP"
 72:       }
 73:     }
 74: 
 75:     ingress {
 76:       from {
 77:         namespace_selector {}
 78:       }
 79:       ports {
 80:         port     = "443"
 81:         protocol = "TCP"
 82:       }
 83:     }
 84: 
 85:     ingress {
 86:       from {
 87:         namespace_selector {}
 88:       }
 89:       ports {
 90:         port     = "636"
 91:         protocol = "TCP"
 92:       }
 93:     }
 94: 
 95:     ingress {
 96:       from {
 97:         namespace_selector {}
 98:       }
 99:       ports {
100:         port     = "8443"
101:         protocol = "TCP"
102:       }
103:     }
104: 
105:     # Egress: Allow traffic to any pod in the same namespace on LDAP and secure ports
106:     egress {
107:       # Allow to any pod in the same namespace
108:       to {
109:         pod_selector {}
110:       }
111:       ports {
112:         port     = "389"
113:         protocol = "TCP"
114:       }
115:     }
116: 
117:     egress {
118:       to {
119:         pod_selector {}
120:       }
121:       ports {
122:         port     = "443"
123:         protocol = "TCP"
124:       }
125:     }
126: 
127:     egress {
128:       to {
129:         pod_selector {}
130:       }
131:       ports {
132:         port     = "636"
133:         protocol = "TCP"
134:       }
135:     }
136: 
137:     egress {
138:       to {
139:         pod_selector {}
140:       }
141:       ports {
142:         port     = "8443"
143:         protocol = "TCP"
144:       }
145:     }
146: 
147:     # Egress: Allow DNS resolution (required for service discovery)
148:     egress {
149:       to {
150:         namespace_selector {}
151:       }
152:       ports {
153:         port     = "53"
154:         protocol = "UDP"
155:       }
156:     }
157: 
158:     egress {
159:       to {
160:         namespace_selector {}
161:       }
162:       ports {
163:         port     = "53"
164:         protocol = "TCP"
165:       }
166:     }
167: 
168:     # Egress: Allow HTTPS for external API calls (2FA providers, etc.)
169:     egress {
170:       ports {
171:         port     = "443"
172:         protocol = "TCP"
173:       }
174:     }
175: 
176:     # Egress: Allow HTTP for external API calls if needed (though HTTPS is preferred)
177:     # Note: This is included for compatibility, but services should prefer HTTPS
178:     egress {
179:       ports {
180:         port     = "80"
181:         protocol = "TCP"
182:       }
183:     }
184:   }
185: }
186: 
187: # Note: We don't need a separate default deny policy because:
188: # 1. The namespace_secure_communication policy above applies to all pods
189: # 2. It only allows specific ports (389 LDAP, 443/636/8443 TLS)
190: # 3. All other ports are implicitly denied
191: # 4. This approach is simpler and avoids policy conflicts
```

## File: application_infra/modules/openldap/outputs.tf
```hcl
 1: output "namespace" {

20: }

25: }

27: output "ldap_base_dn" {

35: }
36: 
37: output "ldap_admin_group_dn" {

39:   value       = "cn=admins,ou=groups,${join(",", [for p in split(".", var.openldap_ldap_domain) : "dc=${p}"])}"
40: }
41: 
42: output "ldap_user_search_base" {

44:   value       = "ou=users"
45: }
```

```bash
206: # ===================== Report tracking =====================
207: # Parallel arrays to track per-check results

215: # Record a check result into the report arrays.

217: record_result() {

249:                 fi

251:                 echo "=== Recent Events (ldap namespace, warnings/errors) ==="
252:                 kubectl get events -n ldap --sort-by=.lastTimestamp --field-selector=type!=Normal 2>&1 || true

266:                 ;;
267:         esac

269: }
270: # Write structured report file for agent investigation
271: write_report_file() {
272:     local report_file="$1"
273:     {
274:         echo "============================================="
275:         echo "DEPLOYMENT MONITOR REPORT"
276:         echo "============================================="
277:         echo "Layer:         application_infra"
278:         echo "Region:        $REGION"
279:         echo "Environment:   $ENVIRONMENT"
280:         echo "Cluster:       $CLUSTER_NAME"
281:         echo "Timestamp:     $(date -u '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')"
282:         echo "Timeout:       ${TIMEOUT}s"
283:         echo "Poll interval: ${POLL_INTERVAL}s"
284:         echo ""
285:         # Summary table
286:         echo "============================================="
287:         echo "CHECK SUMMARY"
288:         echo "============================================="
289:         printf "%-30s  %-12s  %-9s  %-10s\n" "CHECK" "STATUS" "RETRIES" "DURATION"
290:         printf "%-30s  %-12s  %-9s  %-10s\n" \
291:             "$(printf '%0.s-' $(seq 1 30))" \
292:             "$(printf '%0.s-' $(seq 1 12))" \
293:             "$(printf '%0.s-' $(seq 1 9))" \
294:             "$(printf '%0.s-' $(seq 1 10))"
295:         local passed=0 failed=0 timed_out=0
296:         for i in "${!REPORT_NAMES[@]}"; do
297:             local name="${REPORT_NAMES[$i]}"
298:             local status="${REPORT_STATUSES[$i]}"
299:             local retries="${REPORT_RETRIES[$i]}"
300:             local dur="${REPORT_DURATIONS[$i]}"
301:             local dur_min=$(( dur / 60 ))
302:             local dur_sec=$(( dur % 60 ))
303:             printf "%-30s  %-12s  %-9s  %-10s\n" "$name" "$status" "$retries" "${dur_min}m ${dur_sec}s"
304:             case "$status" in
305:                 PASSED)    passed=$((passed + 1)) ;;
306:                 FAILED)    failed=$((failed + 1)) ;;
307:                 TIMED_OUT) timed_out=$((timed_out + 1)) ;;
308:             esac
309:         done
310:         echo ""
311:         local total=${#REPORT_NAMES[@]}
312:         echo "Total: $total  |  Passed: $passed  |  Failed: $failed  |  Timed out: $timed_out"
313:         echo ""
314:         # Detailed output for each check
315:         echo "============================================="
316:         echo "DETAILED CHECK OUTPUT"
317:         echo "============================================="
318:         for i in "${!REPORT_NAMES[@]}"; do
319:             local name="${REPORT_NAMES[$i]}"
320:             local status="${REPORT_STATUSES[$i]}"
321:             local output_file="$REPORT_DIR/${i}_output.txt"
322:             local diag_file="$REPORT_DIR/${i}_diag.txt"
323:             echo ""
324:             echo "--- $name [$status] ---"
325:             if [ -f "$output_file" ] && [ -s "$output_file" ]; then
326:                 echo "[Check Output]"
327:                 strip_ansi < "$output_file"
328:             fi
329:             if [ -f "$diag_file" ] && [ -s "$diag_file" ]; then
330:                 echo ""
331:                 echo "[Diagnostics]"
332:                 strip_ansi < "$diag_file"
333:             fi
334:         done
335:         # Informational sections
336:         if [ -f "$REPORT_DIR/informational.txt" ] && [ -s "$REPORT_DIR/informational.txt" ]; then
337:             echo ""
338:             echo "============================================="
339:             echo "INFORMATIONAL (collected once)"
340:             echo "============================================="
341:             strip_ansi < "$REPORT_DIR/informational.txt"
342:         fi
343:         echo ""
344:         echo "============================================="
345:         echo "PROJECT CONTEXT"
346:         echo "============================================="
347:         echo "Repository: ldap-2fa-on-k8s"
348:         echo "Layer:      application_infra"
349:         echo "Key files for investigation:"
350:         echo "  - application_infra/main.tf"
351:         echo "  - application_infra/variables.tf"
352:         echo "  - application_infra/variables.tfvars"
353:         echo "  - application_infra/providers.tf"
354:         echo "  - application_infra/modules/openldap/"
355:         echo "  - application_infra/modules/alb/"
356:         echo "  - application_infra/modules/argocd/"
357:         echo "  - application_infra/modules/network-policies/"
358:         echo "  - application_infra/helm/openldap-values.tpl.yaml"
359:         echo "  - application_infra/charts/openldap-stack-ha/"
360:         echo ""
361:         echo "============================================="
362:         echo "END REPORT"
363:         echo "============================================="
364:     } > "$report_file"
365: }
366: # Print the final report table.
367: print_report() {
368:     print_header "Detailed Check Report"
369:     # Column widths
370:     local name_width=30
371:     local status_width=12
372:     local retries_width=9
373:     local duration_width=10
374:     # Header
375:     printf "%-${name_width}s  %-${status_width}s  %-${retries_width}s  %-${duration_width}s\n" \
376:         "CHECK" "STATUS" "RETRIES" "DURATION"
377:     printf "%-${name_width}s  %-${status_width}s  %-${retries_width}s  %-${duration_width}s\n" \
378:         "$(printf '%0.s-' $(seq 1 $name_width))" \
379:         "$(printf '%0.s-' $(seq 1 $status_width))" \
380:         "$(printf '%0.s-' $(seq 1 $retries_width))" \
381:         "$(printf '%0.s-' $(seq 1 $duration_width))"
382:     local passed=0 failed=0 timed_out=0
383:     for i in "${!REPORT_NAMES[@]}"; do
384:         local name="${REPORT_NAMES[$i]}"
385:         local status="${REPORT_STATUSES[$i]}"
386:         local retries="${REPORT_RETRIES[$i]}"
387:         local dur="${REPORT_DURATIONS[$i]}"
388:         local dur_min=$(( dur / 60 ))
389:         local dur_sec=$(( dur % 60 ))
390:         local dur_str="${dur_min}m ${dur_sec}s"
391:         local color="$GREEN"
392:         case "$status" in
393:             PASSED)    color="$GREEN"; passed=$((passed + 1)) ;;
394:             FAILED)    color="$RED";   failed=$((failed + 1)) ;;
395:             TIMED_OUT) color="$RED";   timed_out=$((timed_out + 1)) ;;
396:         esac
397:         printf "%-${name_width}s  ${color}%-${status_width}s${NC}  %-${retries_width}s  %-${duration_width}s\n" \
398:             "$name" "$status" "$retries" "$dur_str"
399:     done
400:     echo ""
401:     local total=${#REPORT_NAMES[@]}
402:     echo "Total: $total  |  Passed: $passed  |  Failed: $failed  |  Timed out: $timed_out"
403: }
404: # Polling helper: retries a check function until it passes or timeout is reached.
405: # Tracks retries, duration, and final status for the report.
406: # Captures check output for the report file and collects diagnostics on failure.
407: # Usage: wait_for_check "Display Name" check_function [args...]
408: # Returns 0 on success, 1 on timeout/failure.
409: wait_for_check() {
410:     local check_name=$1
411:     shift
412:     local retries=0
413:     local check_start=$(date +%s)
414:     local check_idx=${#REPORT_NAMES[@]}
415:     local output_file="$REPORT_DIR/${check_idx}_output.txt"
416:     local diag_file="$REPORT_DIR/${check_idx}_diag.txt"
417:     : > "$output_file"
418:     : > "$diag_file"
419:     while true; do
420:         if "$@" 2>&1 | tee "$output_file"; then
421:             local check_duration=$(( $(date +%s) - check_start ))
422:             record_result "$check_name" "PASSED" "$retries" "$check_duration"
423:             return 0
424:         fi
425:         retries=$((retries + 1))
426:         local elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - START_TIME ))
427:         if [ $elapsed -ge $TIMEOUT ]; then
428:             local check_duration=$(( $(date +%s) - check_start ))
429:             record_result "$check_name" "TIMED_OUT" "$retries" "$check_duration"
430:             print_error "Timeout reached waiting for: $check_name"
431:             collect_diagnostics "$check_name" "$diag_file"
432:             return 1
433:         fi
434:         local remaining=$(( TIMEOUT - elapsed ))
435:         local remaining_min=$(( remaining / 60 ))
436:         local remaining_sec=$(( remaining % 60 ))
437:         print_color "$YELLOW" "\n$check_name not ready (attempt $retries). Retrying in ${POLL_INTERVAL}s... (${remaining_min}m ${remaining_sec}s remaining)"
438:         sleep $POLL_INTERVAL
439:     done
440: }
441: # Function to check pod status
442: check_pods() {
443:     local namespace=$1
444:     local label=$2
445:     local resource_name=$3
446:     print_header "Checking $resource_name in namespace: $namespace"
447:     if ! kubectl get namespace "$namespace" &> /dev/null; then
448:         print_warning "Namespace '$namespace' does not exist"
449:         return 1
450:     fi
451:     local pods=$(kubectl get pods -n "$namespace" -l "$label" -o json 2>/dev/null)
452:     if [ -z "$pods" ] || [ "$(echo "$pods" | jq '.items | length')" -eq 0 ]; then
453:         print_warning "No pods found with label '$label' in namespace '$namespace'"
454:         return 1
455:     fi
456:     # Count pods by status
457:     local total=$(echo "$pods" | jq '.items | length')
458:     local running=$(echo "$pods" | jq '[.items[] | select(.status.phase == "Running")] | length')
459:     local pending=$(echo "$pods" | jq '[.items[] | select(.status.phase == "Pending")] | length')
460:     local failed=$(echo "$pods" | jq '[.items[] | select(.status.phase == "Failed")] | length')
461:     echo "Total pods: $total"
462:     echo "Running: $running"
463:     echo "Pending: $pending"
464:     echo "Failed: $failed"
465:     # Show pod details
466:     echo ""
467:     kubectl get pods -n "$namespace" -l "$label" -o wide
468:     # Check if all pods are running
469:     if [ "$running" -eq "$total" ]; then
470:         print_success "All $resource_name pods are running"
471:         return 0
472:     else
473:         print_warning "Not all $resource_name pods are running"
474:         return 1
475:     fi
476: }
477: # Function to check helm releases
478: check_helm_release() {
479:     local namespace=$1
480:     local release_name_pattern=$2
481:     local resource_name=$3
482:     print_header "Checking Helm Release: $resource_name"
483:     if ! kubectl get namespace "$namespace" &> /dev/null; then
484:         print_warning "Namespace '$namespace' does not exist"
485:         return 1
486:     fi
487:     local releases=$(helm list -n "$namespace" -o json 2>/dev/null)
488:     if [ -z "$releases" ] || [ "$(echo "$releases" | jq '. | length')" -eq 0 ]; then
489:         print_warning "No Helm releases found in namespace '$namespace'"
490:         return 1
491:     fi
492:     # Filter releases matching pattern
493:     local matching_release=$(echo "$releases" | jq -r ".[] | select(.name | contains(\"$release_name_pattern\")) | .name" | head -1)
494:     if [ -z "$matching_release" ]; then
495:         print_warning "No Helm release matching pattern '$release_name_pattern' found"
496:         return 1
497:     fi
498:     echo "Release: $matching_release"
499:     helm status "$matching_release" -n "$namespace"
500:     local status=$(echo "$releases" | jq -r ".[] | select(.name == \"$matching_release\") | .status")
501:     if [ "$status" = "deployed" ]; then
502:         print_success "$resource_name is deployed"
503:         return 0
504:     else
505:         print_warning "$resource_name status: $status"
506:         return 1
507:     fi
508: }
509: # Function to check ArgoCD capability (if enabled)
510: check_argocd_capability() {
511:     print_header "Checking ArgoCD Capability"
512:     # Check if ArgoCD namespace exists as a simpler indicator
513:     if kubectl get namespace argocd &> /dev/null; then
514:         echo "ArgoCD namespace: argocd"
515:         # Check for ArgoCD pods
516:         local argocd_pods=$(kubectl get pods -n argocd -o json 2>/dev/null)
517:         if [ -n "$argocd_pods" ]; then
518:             local total=$(echo "$argocd_pods" | jq '.items | length')
519:             local running=$(echo "$argocd_pods" | jq '[.items[] | select(.status.phase == "Running")] | length')
520:             echo "ArgoCD pods: $running/$total running"
521:             kubectl get pods -n argocd -o wide
522:             if [ "$running" -eq "$total" ] && [ "$total" -gt 0 ]; then
523:                 print_success "ArgoCD is deployed and running"
524:                 return 0
525:             else
526:                 print_warning "ArgoCD namespace exists but pods are not all running"
527:                 return 1
528:             fi
529:         else
530:             print_warning "ArgoCD namespace exists but no pods found"
531:             return 1
532:         fi
533:     else
534:         print_warning "ArgoCD namespace not found - ArgoCD may not be enabled"
535:         return 1
536:     fi
537: }
538: # Monitor all deployments (watch mode: poll each check until healthy or timeout)
539: STATUS=0
540: START_TIME=$(date +%s)
541: print_color "$BLUE" "\nPolling interval: ${POLL_INTERVAL}s | Timeout: $(( TIMEOUT / 60 ))m"
542: # Check ArgoCD Capability
543: wait_for_check "ArgoCD Capability" check_argocd_capability || STATUS=1
544: # Check OpenLDAP
545: wait_for_check "OpenLDAP Helm Release" check_helm_release "ldap" "openldap" "OpenLDAP" || STATUS=1
546: wait_for_check "OpenLDAP Pods" check_pods "ldap" "app.kubernetes.io/name=openldap-stack-ha" "OpenLDAP" || STATUS=1
547: # Informational checks (run once after all polling completes)
548: {
549:     print_header "Checking Ingress Resources"
550:     kubectl get ingress -A 2>&1 || true
551:     print_header "Checking Application Load Balancers"
552:     aws elbv2 describe-load-balancers --region "$REGION" --output table 2>&1 || true
553: } 2>&1 | tee "$REPORT_DIR/informational.txt"
554: # Report and summary
555: print_report
556: # Write report file
557: SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
558: REPORT_TIMESTAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
559: REPORT_FILE="${SCRIPT_DIR}/monitor-report-${REGION}-${ENVIRONMENT}-${REPORT_TIMESTAMP}.txt"
560: write_report_file "$REPORT_FILE"
561: ELAPSED=$(( $(date +%s) - START_TIME ))
562: ELAPSED_MIN=$(( ELAPSED / 60 ))
563: ELAPSED_SEC=$(( ELAPSED % 60 ))
564: print_header "Monitoring Summary (completed in ${ELAPSED_MIN}m ${ELAPSED_SEC}s)"
565: if [ $STATUS -eq 0 ]; then
566:     print_success "All deployments are healthy!"
567: else
568:     print_warning "Some deployments have issues. Review the report above for details."
569: fi
570: print_color "$BLUE" "\nReport saved to: $REPORT_FILE"
571: print_color "$BLUE" "Submit this file to an agent for failure investigation and code fix suggestions."
572: exit $STATUS
```

## File: backend_infra/destroy-backend.sh
```bash
  1: #!/bin/bash
  2: # Script to configure backend.hcl and variables.tfvars with user-selected region and environment
  3: # and run Terraform destroy commands
  4: # Usage: ./destroy-backend.sh  (from backend_infra/) or ./backend_infra/destroy-backend.sh (from repo root)
  5: set -euo pipefail
  6: # Run from script directory so placeholder and variables are found (works when called from repo root or backend_infra)
  7: SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
  8: cd "$SCRIPT_DIR"
  9: # Clean up any existing AWS credentials from environment to prevent conflicts
 10: # This ensures the script starts with a clean slate and uses the correct credentials
 11: unset AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID 2>/dev/null || true
 12: unset AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY 2>/dev/null || true
 13: unset AWS_SESSION_TOKEN 2>/dev/null || true
 14: unset AWS_PROFILE 2>/dev/null || true
 15: # Colors for output
 16: RED='\033[0;31m'
 17: GREEN='\033[0;32m'
 18: YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
 19: NC='\033[0m' # No Color
 20: # Configuration
 21: PLACEHOLDER_FILE="tfstate-backend-values-template.hcl"
 22: BACKEND_FILE="backend.hcl"
 23: VARIABLES_FILE="variables.tfvars"
 24: # Function to print colored messages
 25: print_error() {
 26:     echo -e "${RED}ERROR:${NC} $1" >&2
 27: }
 28: print_success() {
 29:     echo -e "${GREEN}SUCCESS:${NC} $1"
 30: }
 31: print_info() {
 32:     echo -e "${YELLOW}INFO:${NC} $1"
 33: }
 34: print_warning() {
 35:     echo -e "${YELLOW}WARNING:${NC} $1"
 36: }
 37: # Check if AWS CLI is installed
 38: if ! command -v aws &> /dev/null; then
 39:     print_error "AWS CLI is not installed."
 40:     echo "Please install it from: https://aws.amazon.com/cli/"
 41:     exit 1
 42: fi
 43: # Check if Terraform is installed
 44: if ! command -v terraform &> /dev/null; then
 45:     print_error "Terraform is not installed."
 46:     echo "Please install it from: https://www.terraform.io/downloads"
 47:     exit 1
 48: fi
 49: # Check if GitHub CLI is installed
 50: if ! command -v gh &> /dev/null; then
 51:     print_error "GitHub CLI (gh) is not installed."
 52:     echo "Please install it from: https://cli.github.com/"
 53:     exit 1
 54: fi
 55: # Check if user is authenticated with GitHub CLI
 56: if ! gh auth status &> /dev/null; then
 57:     print_error "Not authenticated with GitHub CLI."
 58:     echo "Please run: gh auth login"
 59:     exit 1
 60: fi
 61: # Check if jq is installed (required for gh --jq flag)
 62: if ! command -v jq &> /dev/null; then
 63:     print_error "jq is not installed."
 64:     echo "Please install it:"
 65:     echo "  macOS: brew install jq"
 66:     echo "  Linux: sudo apt-get install jq (or use your package manager)"
 67:     echo "  Or visit: https://stedolan.github.io/jq/download/"
 68:     exit 1
 69: fi
 70: # Get repository owner and name
 71: REPO_OWNER=$(gh repo view --json owner --jq '.owner.login' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
 72: REPO_NAME=$(gh repo view --json name --jq '.name' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
 73: if [ -z "$REPO_OWNER" ] || [ -z "$REPO_NAME" ]; then
 74:     print_error "Could not determine repository information."
 75:     echo "Please ensure you're in a git repository and have proper permissions."
 76:     exit 1
 77: fi
 78: print_info "Repository: ${REPO_OWNER}/${REPO_NAME}"
 79: # Function to get repository variable using GitHub CLI
 80: get_repo_variable() {
 81:     local var_name=$1
 82:     local value
 83:     value=$(gh variable list --repo "${REPO_OWNER}/${REPO_NAME}" --json name,value --jq ".[] | select(.name == \"${var_name}\") | .value" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
 84:     if [ -z "$value" ]; then
 85:         print_error "Repository variable '${var_name}' not found or not accessible."
 86:         return 1
 87:     fi
 88:     echo "$value"
 89: }
 90: # Function to retrieve secret from AWS Secrets Manager
 91: get_aws_secret() {
 92:     local secret_name=$1
 93:     local secret_json
 94:     local exit_code
 95:     # Retrieve secret from AWS Secrets Manager
 96:     # Use AWS_REGION if set, otherwise default to us-east-1
 97:     secret_json=$(aws secretsmanager get-secret-value \
 98:         --secret-id "$secret_name" \
 99:         --region "${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}" \
100:         --query SecretString \
101:         --output text 2>&1)
102:     # Capture exit code before checking
103:     exit_code=$?
104:     # Validate secret retrieval
105:     if [ $exit_code -ne 0 ]; then
106:         print_error "Failed to retrieve secret '${secret_name}' from AWS Secrets Manager"
107:         print_error "Error: $secret_json"
108:         return 1
109:     fi
110:     # Validate JSON can be parsed
111:     if ! echo "$secret_json" | jq empty 2>/dev/null; then
112:         print_error "Secret '${secret_name}' contains invalid JSON"
113:         return 1
114:     fi
115:     echo "$secret_json"
116: }
117: # Function to retrieve plain text secret from AWS Secrets Manager
118: get_aws_plaintext_secret() {
119:     local secret_name=$1
120:     local secret_value
121:     local exit_code
122:     # Retrieve secret from AWS Secrets Manager
123:     # Use AWS_REGION if set, otherwise default to us-east-1
124:     secret_value=$(aws secretsmanager get-secret-value \
125:         --secret-id "$secret_name" \
126:         --region "${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}" \
127:         --query SecretString \
128:         --output text 2>&1)
129:     # Capture exit code before checking
130:     exit_code=$?
131:     # Validate secret retrieval
132:     if [ $exit_code -ne 0 ]; then
133:         print_error "Failed to retrieve secret '${secret_name}' from AWS Secrets Manager"
134:         print_error "Error: $secret_value"
135:         return 1
136:     fi
137:     # Check if secret value is empty
138:     if [ -z "$secret_value" ]; then
139:         print_error "Secret '${secret_name}' is empty"
140:         return 1
141:     fi
142:     echo "$secret_value"
143: }
144: # Function to get key value from secret JSON
145: get_secret_key_value() {
146:     local secret_json=$1
147:     local key_name=$2
148:     local value
149:     # Validate JSON can be parsed
150:     if ! echo "$secret_json" | jq empty 2>/dev/null; then
151:         print_error "Invalid JSON provided to get_secret_key_value"
152:         return 1
153:     fi
154:     # Extract key value using jq
155:     value=$(echo "$secret_json" | jq -r ".[\"${key_name}\"]" 2>/dev/null)
156:     # Check if jq command succeeded
157:     if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
158:         print_error "Failed to parse JSON or extract key '${key_name}'"
159:         return 1
160:     fi
161:     # Check if key exists (jq returns "null" for non-existent keys)
162:     if [ "$value" = "null" ] || [ -z "$value" ]; then
163:         print_error "Key '${key_name}' not found in secret JSON or value is empty"
164:         return 1
165:     fi
166:     echo "$value"
167: }
168: # Warning about destructive operation
169: echo ""
170: print_warning "=========================================="
171: print_warning "  DESTRUCTIVE OPERATION WARNING"
172: print_warning "=========================================="
173: print_warning "This script will DESTROY all infrastructure"
174: print_warning "in the selected region and environment."
175: print_warning ""
176: print_warning "This action CANNOT be undone!"
177: print_warning "=========================================="
178: echo ""
179: read -p "Are you sure you want to continue? (type 'yes' to confirm): " confirmation
180: if [ "$confirmation" != "yes" ]; then
181:     print_info "Operation cancelled."
182:     exit 0
183: fi
184: # Interactive prompts
185: echo ""
186: print_info "Select AWS Region:"
187: echo "1) us-east-1: N. Virginia (default)"
188: echo "2) us-east-2: Ohio"
189: read -p "Enter choice [1-2] (default: 1): " region_choice
190: case ${region_choice:-1} in
191:     1)
192:         SELECTED_REGION="us-east-1: N. Virginia"
193:         ;;
194:     2)
195:         SELECTED_REGION="us-east-2: Ohio"
196:         ;;
197:     *)
198:         print_error "Invalid choice. Using default: us-east-1: N. Virginia"
199:         SELECTED_REGION="us-east-1: N. Virginia"
200:         ;;
201: esac
202: # Extract region code (everything before the colon)
203: AWS_REGION="${SELECTED_REGION%%:*}"
204: print_success "Selected region: ${SELECTED_REGION} (${AWS_REGION})"
205: echo ""
206: print_info "Select Environment:"
207: echo "1) prod (default)"
208: echo "2) dev"
209: read -p "Enter choice [1-2] (default: 1): " env_choice
210: case ${env_choice:-1} in
211:     1)
212:         ENVIRONMENT="prod"
213:         ;;
214:     2)
215:         ENVIRONMENT="dev"
216:         ;;
217:     *)
218:         print_error "Invalid choice. Using default: prod"
219:         ENVIRONMENT="prod"
220:         ;;
221: esac
222: print_success "Selected environment: ${ENVIRONMENT}"
223: echo ""
224: # Final confirmation with environment details
225: print_warning "You are about to DESTROY infrastructure in:"
226: print_warning "  Region: ${AWS_REGION}"
227: print_warning "  Environment: ${ENVIRONMENT}"
228: echo ""
229: read -p "Type 'DESTROY' to confirm: " final_confirmation
230: if [ "$final_confirmation" != "DESTROY" ]; then
231:     print_info "Operation cancelled."
232:     exit 0
233: fi
234: # Retrieve all role ARNs from AWS Secrets Manager in a single call
235: # This minimizes AWS CLI calls by fetching all required role ARNs at once
236: print_info "Retrieving role ARNs from AWS Secrets Manager..."
237: SECRET_JSON=$(get_aws_secret "github-role" || echo "")
238: if [ -z "$SECRET_JSON" ]; then
239:     print_error "Failed to retrieve secret from AWS Secrets Manager"
240:     exit 1
241: fi
242: # Extract STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN for backend state operations
243: STATE_ROLE_ARN=$(get_secret_key_value "$SECRET_JSON" "AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN" || echo "")
244: if [ -z "$STATE_ROLE_ARN" ]; then
245:     print_error "Failed to retrieve AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN from secret"
246:     exit 1
247: fi
248: print_success "Retrieved AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN"
249: # Determine which deployment account role ARN to use based on environment
250: if [ "$ENVIRONMENT" = "prod" ]; then
251:     DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN_KEY="AWS_PRODUCTION_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN"
252: else
253:     DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN_KEY="AWS_DEVELOPMENT_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN"
254: fi
255: # Extract deployment account role ARN for provider assume_role
256: DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN=$(get_secret_key_value "$SECRET_JSON" "$DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN_KEY" || echo "")
257: if [ -z "$DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN" ]; then
258:     print_error "Failed to retrieve ${DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN_KEY} from secret"
259:     exit 1
260: fi
261: print_success "Retrieved ${DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN_KEY}"
262: # Use STATE_ROLE_ARN for backend operations
263: ROLE_ARN="$STATE_ROLE_ARN"
264: print_info "Assuming role: $ROLE_ARN"
265: print_info "Region: $AWS_REGION"
266: # Assume the role
267: ROLE_SESSION_NAME="destroy-backend-$(date +%s)"
268: # Assume role and capture output
269: ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT=$(aws sts assume-role \
270:     --role-arn "$ROLE_ARN" \
271:     --role-session-name "$ROLE_SESSION_NAME" \
272:     --region "$AWS_REGION" 2>&1)
273: if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
274:     print_error "Failed to assume role: $ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT"
275:     exit 1
276: fi
277: # Extract credentials from JSON output
278: # Try using jq if available (more reliable), otherwise use sed/grep
279: if command -v jq &> /dev/null; then
280:     export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=$(echo "$ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT" | jq -r '.Credentials.AccessKeyId')
281:     export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=$(echo "$ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT" | jq -r '.Credentials.SecretAccessKey')
282:     export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN=$(echo "$ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT" | jq -r '.Credentials.SessionToken')
283: else
284:     # Fallback: use sed for JSON parsing (works on both macOS and Linux)
285:     export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=$(echo "$ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT" | sed -n 's/.*"AccessKeyId"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
286:     export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=$(echo "$ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT" | sed -n 's/.*"SecretAccessKey"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')

316: BACKEND_PREFIX=$(get_repo_variable "BACKEND_PREFIX") || exit 1

335:         sed -i '' "s|<BACKEND_PREFIX>|${BACKEND_PREFIX}|g" "$BACKEND_FILE"

355:     sed -i '' "s|^region[[:space:]]*=.*|region                 = \"${AWS_REGION}\"|" "$VARIABLES_FILE"
356:     # Add or update deployment_account_role_arn

359:     else

361:     fi
362:     # Add or update deployment_account_external_id
363:     if ! grep -q "^deployment_account_external_id" "$VARIABLES_FILE"; then
364:         echo "deployment_account_external_id = \"${EXTERNAL_ID}\"" >> "$VARIABLES_FILE"
365:     else
366:         sed -i '' "s|^deployment_account_external_id[[:space:]]*=.*|deployment_account_external_id = \"${EXTERNAL_ID}\"|" "$VARIABLES_FILE"
367:     fi

371:     sed -i "s|^region[[:space:]]*=.*|region                 = \"${AWS_REGION}\"|" "$VARIABLES_FILE"
372:     # Add or update deployment_account_role_arn

396: print_info "  - region: ${AWS_REGION}"

400: # Terraform init

406: # Terraform validate

415: echo ""
```

```bash
329:     if [ "$endpoint_count" -gt 0 ]; then
330:         echo "$vpc_endpoints" | jq -r '.VpcEndpoints[] | "  \(.ServiceName)  State: \(.State)"'
331:         available_count=$(echo "$vpc_endpoints" | jq '[.VpcEndpoints[] | select(.State == "available")] | length')
332:         if [ "$available_count" -eq "$endpoint_count" ]; then
333:             print_success "All VPC endpoints are available"
334:             return 0
335:         else
336:             print_warning "$available_count/$endpoint_count VPC endpoints are available"
337:             return 1
338:         fi
339:     else
340:         print_warning "No VPC endpoints found"
341:         return 1
342:     fi
343: }
344: check_ecr_repository() {
345:     print_header "Checking ECR Repository"
346:     local ecr_repo
347:     ecr_repo=$(aws ecr describe-repositories --repository-names "$ECR_NAME" --region "$REGION" --output json 2>/dev/null)
348:     if [ -z "$ecr_repo" ] || [ "$(echo "$ecr_repo" | jq '.repositories | length')" -eq 0 ]; then
349:         print_error "ECR repository '$ECR_NAME' not found"
350:         return 1
351:     fi
352:     local ecr_uri ecr_tag_mutability images image_count
353:     ecr_uri=$(echo "$ecr_repo" | jq -r '.repositories[0].repositoryUri')
354:     ecr_tag_mutability=$(echo "$ecr_repo" | jq -r '.repositories[0].imageTagMutability')
355:     echo "Repository: $ECR_NAME"
356:     echo "URI:        $ecr_uri"
357:     echo "Tag mutability: $ecr_tag_mutability"
358:     images=$(aws ecr list-images --repository-name "$ECR_NAME" --region "$REGION" --output json 2>/dev/null)
359:     image_count=$(echo "$images" | jq '.imageIds | length')
360:     echo "Images:     $image_count"
361:     if [ "$image_count" -gt 0 ]; then
362:         echo ""
363:         echo "Image tags:"
364:         echo "$images" | jq -r '.imageIds[] | select(.imageTag != null) | "  \(.imageTag)"' | sort | head -20
365:     fi
366:     print_success "ECR repository exists"
367:     return 0
368: }
369: check_cloudwatch_logs() {
370:     print_header "Checking EKS CloudWatch Logs"
371:     local log_group log_group_info log_group_count
372:     log_group="/aws/eks/${CLUSTER_NAME}/cluster"
373:     log_group_info=$(aws logs describe-log-groups --log-group-name-prefix "$log_group" --region "$REGION" --output json 2>/dev/null)
374:     log_group_count=$(echo "$log_group_info" | jq '.logGroups | length')
375:     if [ "$log_group_count" -gt 0 ]; then
376:         echo "Log group: $log_group"
377:         local stored_bytes
378:         stored_bytes=$(echo "$log_group_info" | jq -r '.logGroups[0].storedBytes // 0')
379:         echo "Stored bytes: $stored_bytes"
380:         print_success "EKS CloudWatch log group exists"
381:         return 0
382:     else
383:         print_warning "EKS CloudWatch log group not found"
384:         return 1
385:     fi

387: # ===================== Report tracking =====================
388: REPORT_NAMES=()
389: REPORT_STATUSES=()
390: REPORT_RETRIES=()
391: REPORT_DURATIONS=()
392: # Temp directory for capturing check output and diagnostics
393: REPORT_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
394: trap 'rm -rf "$REPORT_DIR"' EXIT
395: record_result() {
396:     REPORT_NAMES+=("$1")
397:     REPORT_STATUSES+=("$2")
398:     REPORT_RETRIES+=("$3")
399:     REPORT_DURATIONS+=("$4")
400: }
401: # Strip ANSI escape codes from text
402: strip_ansi() {
403:     sed $'s/\033\[[0-9;]*m//g'
404: }
405: # Collect additional diagnostics for failed/timed-out checks
406: collect_diagnostics() {
407:     local check_name="$1"
408:     local diag_file="$2"
409:     {
410:         case "$check_name" in
411:             "VPC")
412:                 echo "=== All VPCs in Region ==="
413:                 aws ec2 describe-vpcs --region "$REGION" --output json 2>&1 || true
414:                 ;;
415:             "Subnets")
416:                 echo "=== All Subnets in VPC $VPC_ID ==="
417:                 aws ec2 describe-subnets --filters "Name=vpc-id,Values=$VPC_ID" --region "$REGION" --output json 2>&1 || true
418:                 ;;
419:             "NAT Gateway")
420:                 echo "=== All NAT Gateways in VPC (including non-available) ==="
421:                 aws ec2 describe-nat-gateways --filter "Name=vpc-id,Values=$VPC_ID" --region "$REGION" --output json 2>&1 || true
422:                 ;;
423:             "Internet Gateway")
424:                 echo "=== All Internet Gateways ==="
425:                 aws ec2 describe-internet-gateways --filters "Name=attachment.vpc-id,Values=$VPC_ID" --region "$REGION" --output json 2>&1 || true
426:                 ;;
427:             "EKS Cluster")
428:                 echo "=== Full EKS Cluster Description ==="
429:                 aws eks describe-cluster --name "$CLUSTER_NAME" --region "$REGION" --output json 2>&1 || true
430:                 ;;
431:             "EKS Node Pools")
432:                 echo "=== EKS Node Pools ==="
433:                 aws eks list-node-pools --cluster-name "$CLUSTER_NAME" --region "$REGION" --output json 2>&1 || true
434:                 echo ""
435:                 echo "=== EKS Node Groups ==="
436:                 aws eks list-nodegroups --cluster-name "$CLUSTER_NAME" --region "$REGION" --output json 2>&1 || true
437:                 ;;
438:             "VPC Endpoints")
439:                 echo "=== All VPC Endpoints (detailed) ==="
440:                 aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --filters "Name=vpc-id,Values=$VPC_ID" --region "$REGION" --output json 2>&1 || true
441:                 ;;
442:             "ECR Repository")
443:                 echo "=== ECR Repository Details ==="
444:                 aws ecr describe-repositories --repository-names "$ECR_NAME" --region "$REGION" --output json 2>&1 || true
445:                 echo ""
446:                 echo "=== ECR Lifecycle Policy ==="
447:                 aws ecr get-lifecycle-policy --repository-name "$ECR_NAME" --region "$REGION" --output json 2>&1 || true
448:                 ;;
449:             "CloudWatch Logs")
450:                 echo "=== CloudWatch Log Groups ==="
451:                 aws logs describe-log-groups --log-group-name-prefix "/aws/eks/${CLUSTER_NAME}/" --region "$REGION" --output json 2>&1 || true
452:                 ;;
453:         esac
454:     } > "$diag_file" 2>&1
455: }
456: # Write structured report file for agent investigation
457: write_report_file() {
458:     local report_file="$1"
459:     {
460:         echo "============================================="
461:         echo "DEPLOYMENT MONITOR REPORT"
462:         echo "============================================="
463:         echo "Layer:         backend_infra"
464:         echo "Region:        $REGION"
465:         echo "Environment:   $ENVIRONMENT"
466:         echo "Cluster:       $CLUSTER_NAME"
467:         echo "VPC:           $VPC_ID"
468:         echo "ECR:           $ECR_URL"
469:         echo "Timestamp:     $(date -u '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')"
470:         echo "Timeout:       ${TIMEOUT}s"
471:         echo "Poll interval: ${POLL_INTERVAL}s"
472:         echo ""
473:         # Summary table
474:         echo "============================================="
475:         echo "CHECK SUMMARY"
476:         echo "============================================="
477:         printf "%-30s  %-12s  %-9s  %-10s\n" "CHECK" "STATUS" "RETRIES" "DURATION"
478:         printf "%-30s  %-12s  %-9s  %-10s\n" \
479:             "$(printf '%0.s-' $(seq 1 30))" \
480:             "$(printf '%0.s-' $(seq 1 12))" \
481:             "$(printf '%0.s-' $(seq 1 9))" \
482:             "$(printf '%0.s-' $(seq 1 10))"
483:         local passed=0 failed=0 timed_out=0
484:         for i in "${!REPORT_NAMES[@]}"; do
485:             local name="${REPORT_NAMES[$i]}"
486:             local status="${REPORT_STATUSES[$i]}"
487:             local retries="${REPORT_RETRIES[$i]}"
488:             local dur="${REPORT_DURATIONS[$i]}"
489:             local dur_min=$(( dur / 60 ))
490:             local dur_sec=$(( dur % 60 ))
491:             printf "%-30s  %-12s  %-9s  %-10s\n" "$name" "$status" "$retries" "${dur_min}m ${dur_sec}s"
492:             case "$status" in
493:                 PASSED)    passed=$((passed + 1)) ;;
494:                 FAILED)    failed=$((failed + 1)) ;;
495:                 TIMED_OUT) timed_out=$((timed_out + 1)) ;;
496:             esac
497:         done
498:         echo ""
499:         local total=${#REPORT_NAMES[@]}
500:         echo "Total: $total  |  Passed: $passed  |  Failed: $failed  |  Timed out: $timed_out"
501:         echo ""
502:         # Detailed output for each check
503:         echo "============================================="
504:         echo "DETAILED CHECK OUTPUT"
505:         echo "============================================="
506:         for i in "${!REPORT_NAMES[@]}"; do
507:             local name="${REPORT_NAMES[$i]}"
508:             local status="${REPORT_STATUSES[$i]}"
509:             local output_file="$REPORT_DIR/${i}_output.txt"
510:             local diag_file="$REPORT_DIR/${i}_diag.txt"
511:             echo ""
512:             echo "--- $name [$status] ---"
513:             if [ -f "$output_file" ] && [ -s "$output_file" ]; then
514:                 echo "[Check Output]"
515:                 strip_ansi < "$output_file"
516:             fi
517:             if [ -f "$diag_file" ] && [ -s "$diag_file" ]; then
518:                 echo ""
519:                 echo "[Diagnostics]"
520:                 strip_ansi < "$diag_file"
521:             fi
522:         done
523:         echo ""
524:         echo "============================================="
525:         echo "PROJECT CONTEXT"
526:         echo "============================================="
527:         echo "Repository: ldap-2fa-on-k8s"
528:         echo "Layer:      backend_infra"
529:         echo "Key files for investigation:"
530:         echo "  - backend_infra/main.tf"
531:         echo "  - backend_infra/variables.tf"
532:         echo "  - backend_infra/variables.tfvars"
533:         echo "  - backend_infra/providers.tf"
534:         echo "  - backend_infra/modules/ecr/"
535:         echo "  - backend_infra/modules/endpoints/"
536:         echo "  - backend_infra/modules/ebs/"
537:         echo ""
538:         echo "============================================="
539:         echo "END REPORT"
540:         echo "============================================="
541:     } > "$report_file"
542: }
543: print_report() {
544:     print_header "Detailed Check Report"
545:     local name_width=30
546:     local status_width=12
547:     local retries_width=9
548:     local duration_width=10
549:     printf "%-${name_width}s  %-${status_width}s  %-${retries_width}s  %-${duration_width}s\n" \
550:         "CHECK" "STATUS" "RETRIES" "DURATION"
551:     printf "%-${name_width}s  %-${status_width}s  %-${retries_width}s  %-${duration_width}s\n" \
552:         "$(printf '%0.s-' $(seq 1 $name_width))" \
553:         "$(printf '%0.s-' $(seq 1 $status_width))" \
554:         "$(printf '%0.s-' $(seq 1 $retries_width))" \
555:         "$(printf '%0.s-' $(seq 1 $duration_width))"
556:     local passed=0 failed=0 timed_out=0
557:     for i in "${!REPORT_NAMES[@]}"; do
558:         local name="${REPORT_NAMES[$i]}"
559:         local status="${REPORT_STATUSES[$i]}"
560:         local retries="${REPORT_RETRIES[$i]}"
561:         local dur="${REPORT_DURATIONS[$i]}"
562:         local dur_min=$(( dur / 60 ))
563:         local dur_sec=$(( dur % 60 ))
564:         local dur_str="${dur_min}m ${dur_sec}s"
565:         local color="$GREEN"
566:         case "$status" in
567:             PASSED)    color="$GREEN"; passed=$((passed + 1)) ;;
568:             FAILED)    color="$RED";   failed=$((failed + 1)) ;;
569:             TIMED_OUT) color="$RED";   timed_out=$((timed_out + 1)) ;;
570:         esac
571:         printf "%-${name_width}s  ${color}%-${status_width}s${NC}  %-${retries_width}s  %-${duration_width}s\n" \
572:             "$name" "$status" "$retries" "$dur_str"
573:     done
574:     echo ""
575:     local total=${#REPORT_NAMES[@]}
576:     echo "Total: $total  |  Passed: $passed  |  Failed: $failed  |  Timed out: $timed_out"
577: }
578: # Polling helper: retries a check function until it passes or timeout is reached.
579: # Tracks retries, duration, and final status for the report.
580: # Captures check output for the report file and collects diagnostics on failure.
581: # Usage: wait_for_check "Display Name" check_function [args...]
582: # Returns 0 on success, 1 on timeout/failure.
583: wait_for_check() {
584:     local check_name=$1
585:     shift
586:     local retries=0
587:     local check_start=$(date +%s)
588:     local check_idx=${#REPORT_NAMES[@]}
589:     local output_file="$REPORT_DIR/${check_idx}_output.txt"
590:     local diag_file="$REPORT_DIR/${check_idx}_diag.txt"
591:     : > "$output_file"
592:     : > "$diag_file"
593:     while true; do
594:         if "$@" 2>&1 | tee "$output_file"; then
595:             local check_duration=$(( $(date +%s) - check_start ))
596:             record_result "$check_name" "PASSED" "$retries" "$check_duration"
597:             return 0
598:         fi
599:         retries=$((retries + 1))
600:         local elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - START_TIME ))
601:         if [ $elapsed -ge $TIMEOUT ]; then
602:             local check_duration=$(( $(date +%s) - check_start ))
603:             record_result "$check_name" "TIMED_OUT" "$retries" "$check_duration"
604:             print_error "Timeout reached waiting for: $check_name"
605:             collect_diagnostics "$check_name" "$diag_file"
606:             return 1
607:         fi
608:         local remaining=$(( TIMEOUT - elapsed ))
609:         local remaining_min=$(( remaining / 60 ))
610:         local remaining_sec=$(( remaining % 60 ))
611:         print_color "$YELLOW" "\n$check_name not ready (attempt $retries). Retrying in ${POLL_INTERVAL}s... (${remaining_min}m ${remaining_sec}s remaining)"
612:         sleep $POLL_INTERVAL
613:     done
614: }
615: # ===================== Monitor all resources (watch mode) =====================
616: STATUS=0
617: START_TIME=$(date +%s)
618: print_color "$BLUE" "\nPolling interval: ${POLL_INTERVAL}s | Timeout: $(( TIMEOUT / 60 ))m"
619: wait_for_check "VPC" check_vpc || STATUS=1
620: wait_for_check "Subnets" check_subnets || STATUS=1
621: wait_for_check "NAT Gateway" check_nat_gateway || STATUS=1
622: wait_for_check "Internet Gateway" check_internet_gateway || STATUS=1
623: wait_for_check "EKS Cluster" check_eks_cluster || STATUS=1
624: wait_for_check "EKS Node Pools" check_eks_node_pools || STATUS=1
625: wait_for_check "VPC Endpoints" check_vpc_endpoints || STATUS=1
626: wait_for_check "ECR Repository" check_ecr_repository || STATUS=1
627: wait_for_check "CloudWatch Logs" check_cloudwatch_logs || STATUS=1
628: ##################### Report and Summary ##########################
629: print_report
630: # Write report file
631: SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
632: REPORT_TIMESTAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
633: REPORT_FILE="${SCRIPT_DIR}/monitor-report-${REGION}-${ENVIRONMENT}-${REPORT_TIMESTAMP}.txt"
634: write_report_file "$REPORT_FILE"
635: ELAPSED=$(( $(date +%s) - START_TIME ))
636: ELAPSED_MIN=$(( ELAPSED / 60 ))
637: ELAPSED_SEC=$(( ELAPSED % 60 ))
638: print_header "Monitoring Summary (completed in ${ELAPSED_MIN}m ${ELAPSED_SEC}s)"
639: if [ $STATUS -eq 0 ]; then
640:     print_success "All backend infrastructure resources are healthy!"
641: else
642:     print_warning "Some backend infrastructure resources have issues. Review the report above for details."
643: fi
644: print_color "$BLUE" "\nReport saved to: $REPORT_FILE"
645: print_color "$BLUE" "Submit this file to an agent for failure investigation and code fix suggestions."
646: exit $STATUS
```

## File: backend_infra/providers.tf
```hcl
 1: terraform {
 2:   required_providers {
 3:     aws = {
 4:       source  = "hashicorp/aws"
 5:       version = ">= 6.21.0"
 6:     }
 7:     kubernetes = {
 8:       source  = "hashicorp/kubernetes"
 9:       version = "~> 2.0"
10:     }
11:   }
12: 
13:   backend "s3" {
14:     # Backend configuration provided via backend.hcl file
15:     encrypt      = true
16:     use_lockfile = true
17:   }
18: 
19:   required_version = "~> 1.14.0"
20: }
21: 
22: provider "aws" {
23:   region = var.region
24: 
25:   # Assume role in deployment account (Account B) if role ARN is provided
26:   # This allows GitHub Actions to authenticate with Account A (for state)
27:   # while Terraform provider uses Account B (for resource deployment)
28:   # ExternalId is required for security when assuming cross-account roles
29:   dynamic "assume_role" {
30:     for_each = var.deployment_account_role_arn != null ? [1] : []
31:     content {
32:       role_arn    = var.deployment_account_role_arn
33:       external_id = var.deployment_account_external_id
34:     }
35:   }
36: }
37: 
38: # EKS token exec configuration
39: # Uses get-eks-token.sh to generate fresh tokens on every Kubernetes API call,
40: # preventing token expiration during long Terraform operations.
41: locals {
42:   eks_exec_env = {
43:     EKS_CLUSTER_NAME   = module.eks.cluster_name
44:     EKS_REGION         = var.region
45:     ASSUME_ROLE_ARN    = var.deployment_account_role_arn != null ? var.deployment_account_role_arn : ""
46:     ASSUME_EXTERNAL_ID = var.deployment_account_external_id != null ? var.deployment_account_external_id : ""
47:   }
48: }
49: 
50: provider "kubernetes" {
51:   host                   = module.eks.cluster_endpoint
52:   cluster_ca_certificate = base64decode(module.eks.cluster_certificate_authority_data)
53: 
54:   exec {
55:     api_version = "client.authentication.k8s.io/v1beta1"
56:     command     = "${path.module}/../scripts/get-eks-token.sh"
57:     env         = local.eks_exec_env
58:   }
59: }
```

```bash
142: get_secret_key_value() {
143:     local secret_json=$1
144:     local key_name=$2
145:     local value
146:     # Validate JSON can be parsed
147:     if ! echo "$secret_json" | jq empty 2>/dev/null; then
148:         print_error "Invalid JSON provided to get_secret_key_value"
149:         return 1
150:     fi
151:     # Extract key value using jq
152:     value=$(echo "$secret_json" | jq -r ".[\"${key_name}\"]" 2>/dev/null)
153:     # Check if jq command succeeded
154:     if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
155:         print_error "Failed to parse JSON or extract key '${key_name}'"
156:         return 1
157:     fi
158:     # Check if key exists (jq returns "null" for non-existent keys)
159:     if [ "$value" = "null" ] || [ -z "$value" ]; then
160:         print_error "Key '${key_name}' not found in secret JSON or value is empty"
161:         return 1
162:     fi
163:     echo "$value"
164: }
165: # Interactive prompts
166: echo ""
167: print_info "Select AWS Region:"
168: echo "1) us-east-1: N. Virginia (default)"
169: echo "2) us-east-2: Ohio"
170: read -p "Enter choice [1-2] (default: 1): " region_choice
171: case ${region_choice:-1} in
172:     1)
173:         SELECTED_REGION="us-east-1: N. Virginia"
174:         ;;
175:     2)
176:         SELECTED_REGION="us-east-2: Ohio"
177:         ;;
178:     *)
179:         print_error "Invalid choice. Using default: us-east-1: N. Virginia"
180:         SELECTED_REGION="us-east-1: N. Virginia"
181:         ;;
182: esac
183: # Extract region code (everything before the colon)
184: AWS_REGION="${SELECTED_REGION%%:*}"
185: print_success "Selected region: ${SELECTED_REGION} (${AWS_REGION})"
186: echo ""
187: print_info "Select Environment:"
188: echo "1) prod (default)"
189: echo "2) dev"
190: read -p "Enter choice [1-2] (default: 1): " env_choice
191: case ${env_choice:-1} in
192:     1)
193:         ENVIRONMENT="prod"
194:         ;;
195:     2)
196:         ENVIRONMENT="dev"
197:         ;;
198:     *)
199:         print_error "Invalid choice. Using default: prod"
200:         ENVIRONMENT="prod"
201:         ;;
202: esac
203: print_success "Selected environment: ${ENVIRONMENT}"
204: echo ""
205: # Retrieve all role ARNs from AWS Secrets Manager in a single call
206: # This minimizes AWS CLI calls by fetching all required role ARNs at once
207: print_info "Retrieving role ARNs from AWS Secrets Manager..."
208: SECRET_JSON=$(get_aws_secret "github-role" || echo "")
209: if [ -z "$SECRET_JSON" ]; then
210:     print_error "Failed to retrieve secret from AWS Secrets Manager"
211:     exit 1
212: fi
213: # Extract STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN for backend state operations
214: STATE_ROLE_ARN=$(get_secret_key_value "$SECRET_JSON" "AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN" || echo "")
215: if [ -z "$STATE_ROLE_ARN" ]; then
216:     print_error "Failed to retrieve AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN from secret"
217:     exit 1
218: fi
219: print_success "Retrieved AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN"
220: # Determine which deployment account role ARN to use based on environment
221: if [ "$ENVIRONMENT" = "prod" ]; then
222:     DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN_KEY="AWS_PRODUCTION_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN"
223: else
224:     DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN_KEY="AWS_DEVELOPMENT_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN"
225: fi
226: # Extract deployment account role ARN for provider assume_role
227: DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN=$(get_secret_key_value "$SECRET_JSON" "$DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN_KEY" || echo "")
228: if [ -z "$DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN" ]; then
229:     print_error "Failed to retrieve ${DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN_KEY} from secret"
230:     exit 1
231: fi
232: print_success "Retrieved ${DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN_KEY}"
233: # Use STATE_ROLE_ARN for backend operations
234: ROLE_ARN="$STATE_ROLE_ARN"
235: print_info "Assuming role: $ROLE_ARN"
236: print_info "Region: $AWS_REGION"
237: # Assume the role
238: ROLE_SESSION_NAME="setup-backend-$(date +%s)"
239: # Assume role and capture output
240: ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT=$(aws sts assume-role \
241:     --role-arn "$ROLE_ARN" \
242:     --role-session-name "$ROLE_SESSION_NAME" \
243:     --region "$AWS_REGION" 2>&1)
244: if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
245:     print_error "Failed to assume role: $ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT"
246:     exit 1
247: fi
248: # Extract credentials from JSON output
249: # Try using jq if available (more reliable), otherwise use sed/grep
250: if command -v jq &> /dev/null; then
251:     export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=$(echo "$ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT" | jq -r '.Credentials.AccessKeyId')
252:     export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=$(echo "$ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT" | jq -r '.Credentials.SecretAccessKey')
253:     export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN=$(echo "$ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT" | jq -r '.Credentials.SessionToken')
254: else
255:     # Fallback: use sed for JSON parsing (works on both macOS and Linux)
256:     export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=$(echo "$ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT" | sed -n 's/.*"AccessKeyId"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
257:     export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=$(echo "$ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT" | sed -n 's/.*"SecretAccessKey"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
258:     export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN=$(echo "$ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT" | sed -n 's/.*"SessionToken"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
259: fi
260: if [ -z "$AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID" ] || [ -z "$AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY" ] || [ -z "$AWS_SESSION_TOKEN" ]; then
261:     print_error "Failed to extract credentials from assume-role output."
262:     print_error "Output was: $ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT"
263:     exit 1
264: fi
265: print_success "Successfully assumed role"
266: # Verify the credentials work
267: CALLER_ARN=$(aws sts get-caller-identity --region "$AWS_REGION" --query 'Arn' --output text 2>&1)
268: if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
269:     print_error "Failed to verify assumed role credentials: $CALLER_ARN"
270:     exit 1
271: fi
272: print_info "Assumed role identity: $CALLER_ARN"
273: echo ""
274: # Retrieve ExternalId from AWS Secrets Manager (plain text secret)
275: # Must be retrieved after assuming role to have AWS credentials
276: print_info "Retrieving ExternalId from AWS Secrets Manager..."
277: EXTERNAL_ID=$(get_aws_plaintext_secret "external-id" || echo "")
278: if [ -z "$EXTERNAL_ID" ]; then
279:     print_error "Failed to retrieve 'external-id' secret from AWS Secrets Manager"
280:     exit 1
281: fi
282: print_success "Retrieved ExternalId"
283: # Retrieve repository variables
284: print_info "Retrieving repository variables..."
285: BUCKET_NAME=$(get_repo_variable "BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME") || exit 1
286: print_success "Retrieved BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME"
287: BACKEND_PREFIX=$(get_repo_variable "BACKEND_PREFIX") || exit 1
288: print_success "Retrieved BACKEND_PREFIX"
289: # Check if backend.hcl already exists
290: if [ -f "$BACKEND_FILE" ]; then
291:     print_info "${BACKEND_FILE} already exists. Skipping creation."
292: else
293:     # Check if placeholder file exists
294:     if [ ! -f "$PLACEHOLDER_FILE" ]; then
295:         print_error "Placeholder file '${PLACEHOLDER_FILE}' not found."
296:         exit 1
297:     fi
298:     # Copy placeholder to backend file and replace placeholders
299:     print_info "Creating ${BACKEND_FILE} from ${PLACEHOLDER_FILE} with retrieved values..."
300:     # Copy placeholder file to backend file
301:     cp "$PLACEHOLDER_FILE" "$BACKEND_FILE"
302:     # Replace placeholders (works on macOS and Linux)
303:     if [[ "$OSTYPE" == "darwin"* ]]; then
304:         # macOS sed requires -i '' for in-place editing
305:         sed -i '' "s|<BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME>|${BUCKET_NAME}|g" "$BACKEND_FILE"
306:         sed -i '' "s|<BACKEND_PREFIX>|${BACKEND_PREFIX}|g" "$BACKEND_FILE"
307:         sed -i '' "s|<AWS_REGION>|${AWS_REGION}|g" "$BACKEND_FILE"
308:     else
309:         # Linux sed
310:         sed -i "s|<BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME>|${BUCKET_NAME}|g" "$BACKEND_FILE"
311:         sed -i "s|<BACKEND_PREFIX>|${BACKEND_PREFIX}|g" "$BACKEND_FILE"
312:         sed -i "s|<AWS_REGION>|${AWS_REGION}|g" "$BACKEND_FILE"
313:     fi
314:     print_success "Created ${BACKEND_FILE}"
315: fi
316: # Update variables.tfvars
317: print_info "Updating ${VARIABLES_FILE} with selected values..."
318: if [ ! -f "$VARIABLES_FILE" ]; then
319:     print_error "Variables file '${VARIABLES_FILE}' not found."
320:     exit 1
321: fi
322: # Update variables.tfvars (works on macOS and Linux)
323: if [[ "$OSTYPE" == "darwin"* ]]; then
324:     # macOS sed requires -i '' for in-place editing
325:     sed -i '' "s|^env[[:space:]]*=.*|env                    = \"${ENVIRONMENT}\"|" "$VARIABLES_FILE"
326:     sed -i '' "s|^region[[:space:]]*=.*|region                 = \"${AWS_REGION}\"|" "$VARIABLES_FILE"
327:     # Add or update deployment_account_role_arn
328:     if ! grep -q "^deployment_account_role_arn" "$VARIABLES_FILE"; then
329:         echo "deployment_account_role_arn = \"${DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN}\"" >> "$VARIABLES_FILE"
330:     else
331:         sed -i '' "s|^deployment_account_role_arn[[:space:]]*=.*|deployment_account_role_arn = \"${DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN}\"|" "$VARIABLES_FILE"
332:     fi
333:     # Add or update deployment_account_external_id
334:     if ! grep -q "^deployment_account_external_id" "$VARIABLES_FILE"; then
335:         echo "deployment_account_external_id = \"${EXTERNAL_ID}\"" >> "$VARIABLES_FILE"
336:     else
337:         sed -i '' "s|^deployment_account_external_id[[:space:]]*=.*|deployment_account_external_id = \"${EXTERNAL_ID}\"|" "$VARIABLES_FILE"
338:     fi
339: else
340:     # Linux sed
341:     sed -i "s|^env[[:space:]]*=.*|env                    = \"${ENVIRONMENT}\"|" "$VARIABLES_FILE"
342:     sed -i "s|^region[[:space:]]*=.*|region                 = \"${AWS_REGION}\"|" "$VARIABLES_FILE"
343:     # Add or update deployment_account_role_arn
344:     if ! grep -q "^deployment_account_role_arn" "$VARIABLES_FILE"; then
345:         echo "deployment_account_role_arn = \"${DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN}\"" >> "$VARIABLES_FILE"
346:     else
347:         sed -i "s|^deployment_account_role_arn[[:space:]]*=.*|deployment_account_role_arn = \"${DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN}\"|" "$VARIABLES_FILE"
348:     fi
349:     # Add or update deployment_account_external_id
350:     if ! grep -q "^deployment_account_external_id" "$VARIABLES_FILE"; then
351:         echo "deployment_account_external_id = \"${EXTERNAL_ID}\"" >> "$VARIABLES_FILE"
352:     else
353:         sed -i "s|^deployment_account_external_id[[:space:]]*=.*|deployment_account_external_id = \"${EXTERNAL_ID}\"|" "$VARIABLES_FILE"
354:     fi
355: fi
356: print_success "Updated ${VARIABLES_FILE}"
357: echo ""
358: print_success "Configuration files updated successfully!"
359: echo ""
360: print_info "Backend file: ${BACKEND_FILE}"
361: print_info "  - bucket: ${BUCKET_NAME}"
362: print_info "  - key: ${BACKEND_PREFIX}"
363: print_info "  - region: ${AWS_REGION}"
364: echo ""
365: print_info "Variables file: ${VARIABLES_FILE}"
366: print_info "  - env: ${ENVIRONMENT}"
367: print_info "  - region: ${AWS_REGION}"
368: echo ""
369: # Terraform workspace name
370: WORKSPACE_NAME="${AWS_REGION}-${ENVIRONMENT}"
371: # Terraform init
372: print_info "Running terraform init with backend configuration..."
373: terraform init -backend-config="${BACKEND_FILE}"
374: # Terraform workspace
375: print_info "Selecting or creating workspace: ${WORKSPACE_NAME}..."
376: terraform workspace select "${WORKSPACE_NAME}" || terraform workspace new "${WORKSPACE_NAME}"
377: # Terraform validate
378: print_info "Running terraform validate..."
379: terraform validate
380: # Terraform plan
381: print_info "Running terraform plan..."
382: terraform plan -var-file="${VARIABLES_FILE}" -out terraform.tfplan
383: # Terraform apply
384: print_info "Running terraform apply..."
385: terraform apply -auto-approve terraform.tfplan
386: # Get ECR repository name from Terraform outputs
387: print_info "Retrieving ECR repository name from Terraform outputs..."
388: ECR_REPOSITORY_NAME=$(terraform output -raw ecr_repository 2>/dev/null || echo "")
389: if [ -z "$ECR_REPOSITORY_NAME" ] || [ "$ECR_REPOSITORY_NAME" = "null" ]; then
390:     print_error "Could not retrieve ECR repository name from Terraform outputs."
391:     print_error "Make sure backend_infra has been deployed and outputs ecr_repository."
392:     exit 1
393: fi
394: print_success "Retrieved ECR repository name: ${ECR_REPOSITORY_NAME}"
395: # Function to set repository variable using GitHub CLI
396: set_repo_variable() {
397:     local var_name=$1
398:     local var_value=$2
399:     if gh variable set "${var_name}" --body "${var_value}" --repo "${REPO_OWNER}/${REPO_NAME}" 2>/dev/null; then
400:         return 0
401:     else
402:         return 1
403:     fi
404: }
405: # Save ECR repository name to GitHub repository variable
406: print_info "Saving ECR repository name to GitHub repository variable..."
407: if set_repo_variable "ECR_REPOSITORY_NAME" "${ECR_REPOSITORY_NAME}"; then
408:     print_success "Saved ECR_REPOSITORY_NAME to GitHub repository variables"
409: else
410:     print_error "Failed to save ECR_REPOSITORY_NAME to GitHub repository variables"
411:     exit 1
412: fi
413: echo ""
414: print_success "Script completed successfully!"
```
