```bash
  1: #!/bin/bash
  2: # Script to assume the 'github-role' for different AWS accounts (State, Dev, Prod)
  3: # Usage: source ./assume-github-role.sh [state|dev|prod|clean] [--help]
  4: #   OR:   eval $(./assume-github-role.sh [state|dev|prod|clean])
  5: #   If no argument is provided, the script will prompt for account selection
  6: #   If an argument is provided, it will skip the prompt and use the specified account
  7: #   Use 'clean' to remove all AWS credentials from the environment
  8: #
  9: # IMPORTANT: This script must be SOURCED (not executed) for credentials to persist
 10: #   in your current shell. Use: source ./assume-github-role.sh [option]
 11: #   OR use: eval $(./assume-github-role.sh [option])
 12: # Detect if script is being sourced or executed
 13: # If ${BASH_SOURCE[0]} == ${0}, script is being executed
 14: # If ${BASH_SOURCE[0]} != ${0}, script is being sourced
 15: IS_SOURCED=false
 16: if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-}" != "${0}" ]]; then
 17:     IS_SOURCED=true
 18: fi
 19: # Detect if running in non-interactive mode (e.g., Terraform external data source)
 20: # Suppress all output in this mode to avoid breaking JSON output
 21: # Detection methods (any of these will enable silent mode):
 22: # 1. GITHUB_ACTIONS - GitHub Actions CI/CD environment
 23: # 2. TERRAFORM_CLI_PATH - Set by Terraform setup actions
 24: # 3. TF_DATA_DIR - Terraform data directory (set during terraform operations)
 25: # 4. TERM=dumb - Non-interactive terminal
 26: # 5. ! -t 0 - No TTY (non-interactive)
 27: SILENT_MODE=false
 28: if [ -n "${GITHUB_ACTIONS:-}" ] || \
 29:    [ -n "${TERRAFORM_CLI_PATH:-}" ] || \
 30:    [ -n "${TF_DATA_DIR:-}" ] || \
 31:    [ "${TERM:-}" = "dumb" ] || \
 32:    [ ! -t 0 ]; then
 33:     SILENT_MODE=true
 34: fi
 35: # Only use strict error handling in interactive mode
 36: # In silent mode, we need to handle errors manually to avoid breaking JSON output
 37: if [ "$SILENT_MODE" = false ]; then
 38:     set -euo pipefail
 39: else
 40:     set +euo pipefail
 41: fi
 42: # Clean up any existing AWS credentials from environment to prevent conflicts
 43: # This ensures the script starts with a clean slate and uses the correct credentials
 44: # However, in silent mode (Terraform), we may need existing credentials to assume roles
 45: # so we only clean if not in silent mode
 46: if [ "$SILENT_MODE" = false ]; then
 47:     unset AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID 2>/dev/null || true
 48:     unset AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY 2>/dev/null || true
 49:     unset AWS_SESSION_TOKEN 2>/dev/null || true
 50:     unset AWS_PROFILE 2>/dev/null || true
 51: fi
 52: # Colors for output
 53: RED='\033[0;31m'
 54: GREEN='\033[0;32m'
 55: YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
 56: NC='\033[0m' # No Color
 57: # Function to print colored messages
 58: print_error() {
 59:     if [ "$SILENT_MODE" = false ]; then
 60:         echo -e "${RED}ERROR:${NC} $1" >&2
 61:     fi
 62: }
 63: print_success() {
 64:     if [ "$SILENT_MODE" = false ]; then
 65:         if [ "$IS_SOURCED" = true ]; then
 66:             echo -e "${GREEN}SUCCESS:${NC} $1"
 67:         else
 68:             echo -e "${GREEN}SUCCESS:${NC} $1" >&2
 69:         fi
 70:     fi
 71: }
 72: print_info() {
 73:     if [ "$SILENT_MODE" = false ]; then
 74:         if [ "$IS_SOURCED" = true ]; then
 75:             echo -e "${YELLOW}INFO:${NC} $1"
 76:         else
 77:             echo -e "${YELLOW}INFO:${NC} $1" >&2
 78:         fi
 79:     fi
 80: }
 81: # Function to display help message
 82: show_help() {
 83:     cat << EOF
 84: Usage: ./assume-github-role.sh [OPTION]
 85: This script allows you to assume the 'github-role' for different AWS accounts
 86: (State, Dev, Prod) or clean existing AWS credentials from your environment.
 87: OPTIONS:
 88:     state           Assume the State Account role
 89:     dev             Assume the Dev Account role
 90:     prod            Assume the Prod Account role
 91:     clean           Remove all AWS credentials from the environment
 92:     --help, -h      Display this help message and exit
 93: EXAMPLES:
 94:     # IMPORTANT: This script must be SOURCED for credentials to persist!
 95:     # Interactive mode (prompts for selection) - SOURCED
 96:     source ./assume-github-role.sh
 97:     # Assume State Account role - SOURCED
 98:     source ./assume-github-role.sh state
 99:     # Assume Dev Account role - SOURCED
100:     source ./assume-github-role.sh dev
101:     # Assume Prod Account role - SOURCED
102:     source ./assume-github-role.sh prod
103:     # Clean all AWS credentials - SOURCED
104:     source ./assume-github-role.sh clean
105:     # Alternative: Use eval to execute and apply exports
106:     eval $(./assume-github-role.sh state)
107:     # Display help (can be executed directly)
108:     ./assume-github-role.sh --help
109: NOTES:
110:     - Arguments are case-insensitive (state, State, STATE all work)
111:     - When assuming Dev or Prod roles, ExternalId is automatically retrieved
112:     - IMPORTANT: You must SOURCE this script (source ./assume-github-role.sh) for
113:     credentials to persist in your current shell session
114:     - If executed directly (./assume-github-role.sh), the script will output export
115:     commands that can be eval'd: eval $(./assume-github-role.sh state)
116:     - Use 'clean' to remove credentials when switching accounts
117: EOF
118: }
119: # Function to clean AWS credentials from environment
120: clean_aws_credentials() {
121:     print_info "Cleaning AWS credentials from environment..."
122:     unset AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID 2>/dev/null || true
123:     unset AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY 2>/dev/null || true
124:     unset AWS_SESSION_TOKEN 2>/dev/null || true
125:     unset AWS_PROFILE 2>/dev/null || true
126:     print_success "AWS credentials have been removed from the environment"
127:     # Verify credentials are cleared
128:     if [ -z "${AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID:-}" ] && [ -z "${AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY:-}" ] && [ -z "${AWS_SESSION_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
129:         print_info "Verification: All AWS credential environment variables are unset"
130:     else
131:         print_error "Warning: Some AWS credentials may still be set"
132:     fi
133:     echo ""
134:     return 0
135: }
136: # Check if AWS CLI is installed
137: if ! command -v aws &> /dev/null; then
138:     print_error "AWS CLI is not installed."
139:     echo "Please install it from: https://aws.amazon.com/cli/"
140:     exit 1
141: fi
142: # Check if jq is installed
143: if ! command -v jq &> /dev/null; then
144:     print_error "jq is not installed."
145:     echo "Please install it:"
146:     echo "  macOS: brew install jq"
147:     echo "  Linux: sudo apt-get install jq (or use your package manager)"
148:     echo "  Or visit: https://stedolan.github.io/jq/download/"
149:     exit 1
150: fi
151: # Function to retrieve secret from AWS Secrets Manager
152: get_aws_secret() {
153:     local secret_name=$1
154:     local secret_json
155:     local exit_code
156:     # Retrieve secret from AWS Secrets Manager
157:     # Use AWS_REGION if set, otherwise default to us-east-1
158:     secret_json=$(aws secretsmanager get-secret-value \
159:         --secret-id "$secret_name" \
160:         --region "${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}" \
161:         --query SecretString \
162:         --output text 2>&1)
163:     # Capture exit code before checking
164:     exit_code=$?
165:     # Validate secret retrieval
166:     if [ $exit_code -ne 0 ]; then
167:         print_error "Failed to retrieve secret '${secret_name}' from AWS Secrets Manager"
168:         print_error "Error: $secret_json"
169:         return 1
170:     fi
171:     # Validate JSON can be parsed
172:     if ! echo "$secret_json" | jq empty 2>/dev/null; then
173:         print_error "Secret '${secret_name}' contains invalid JSON"
174:         return 1
175:     fi
176:     echo "$secret_json"
177: }
178: # Function to get key value from secret JSON
179: get_secret_key_value() {
180:     local secret_json=$1
181:     local key_name=$2
182:     local value
183:     # Validate JSON can be parsed
184:     if ! echo "$secret_json" | jq empty 2>/dev/null; then
185:         print_error "Invalid JSON provided to get_secret_key_value"
186:         return 1
187:     fi
188:     # Extract key value using jq
189:     value=$(echo "$secret_json" | jq -r ".[\"${key_name}\"]" 2>/dev/null)
190:     # Check if jq command succeeded
191:     if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
192:         print_error "Failed to parse JSON or extract key '${key_name}'"
193:         return 1
194:     fi
195:     # Check if key exists (jq returns "null" for non-existent keys)
196:     if [ "$value" = "null" ] || [ -z "$value" ]; then
197:         print_error "Key '${key_name}' not found in secret JSON or value is empty"
198:         return 1
199:     fi
200:     echo "$value"
201: }
202: # Function to assume an AWS IAM role and export credentials
203: # Usage: assume_aws_role <role_arn> [external_id] [role_description] [session_name_suffix]
204: #   role_arn: The ARN of the role to assume (required)
205: #   external_id: Optional external ID for cross-account role assumption
206: #   role_description: Optional description for logging (defaults to "role")
207: #   session_name_suffix: Optional suffix for session name (defaults to "assume-github-role")
208: assume_aws_role() {
209:     local role_arn=$1
210:     local external_id=${2:-}
211:     local role_description=${3:-"role"}
212:     local session_name_suffix=${4:-"assume-github-role"}
213:     if [ -z "$role_arn" ]; then
214:         print_error "Role ARN is required for assume_aws_role"
215:         return 1
216:     fi
217:     print_info "Assuming ${role_description}: $role_arn"
218:     print_info "Region: ${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}"
219:     # Assume the role
220:     local role_session_name="${session_name_suffix}-$(date +%s)"
221:     local assume_role_output
222:     # Assume role and capture output
223:     # Add external ID if provided
224:     if [ -n "$external_id" ]; then
225:         assume_role_output=$(aws sts assume-role \
226:             --role-arn "$role_arn" \
227:             --role-session-name "$role_session_name" \
228:             --external-id "$external_id" \
229:             --region "${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}" 2>&1)
230:     else
231:         assume_role_output=$(aws sts assume-role \
232:             --role-arn "$role_arn" \
233:             --role-session-name "$role_session_name" \
234:             --region "${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}" 2>&1)
235:     fi
236:     if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
237:         print_error "Failed to assume ${role_description}: $assume_role_output"
238:         return 1
239:     fi
240:     # Extract credentials from JSON output
241:     local access_key_id
242:     local secret_access_key
243:     local session_token
244:     access_key_id=$(echo "$assume_role_output" | jq -r '.Credentials.AccessKeyId')
245:     secret_access_key=$(echo "$assume_role_output" | jq -r '.Credentials.SecretAccessKey')
246:     session_token=$(echo "$assume_role_output" | jq -r '.Credentials.SessionToken')
247:     if [ -z "$access_key_id" ] || [ -z "$secret_access_key" ] || [ -z "$session_token" ]; then
248:         print_error "Failed to extract credentials from assume-role output."
249:         print_error "Output was: $assume_role_output"
250:         return 1
251:     fi
252:     # Store credentials in global variables for later export
253:     ASSUMED_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="$access_key_id"
254:     ASSUMED_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="$secret_access_key"
255:     ASSUMED_AWS_SESSION_TOKEN="$session_token"
256:     # Export credentials to environment variables (only if sourced)
257:     if [ "$IS_SOURCED" = true ]; then
258:         export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="$access_key_id"
259:         export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="$secret_access_key"
260:         export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN="$session_token"
261:     fi
262:     print_success "Successfully assumed ${role_description}"
263:     # Verify the credentials work
264:     local caller_arn
265:     if [ "$IS_SOURCED" = true ]; then
266:         # Use exported credentials
267:         caller_arn=$(aws sts get-caller-identity --region "${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}" --query 'Arn' --output text 2>&1)
268:     else
269:         # Temporarily set credentials for verification
270:         caller_arn=$(AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="$access_key_id" \
271:                     AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="$secret_access_key" \
272:                     AWS_SESSION_TOKEN="$session_token" \
273:                     aws sts get-caller-identity --region "${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}" --query 'Arn' --output text 2>&1)
274:     fi
275:     if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
276:         print_error "Failed to verify assumed role credentials: $caller_arn"
277:         return 1
278:     fi
279:     print_info "${role_description} identity: $caller_arn"
280:     return 0
281: }
282: # Error flag for silent mode (when sourced, we can't use exit/return)
283: SCRIPT_ERROR=false
284: SCRIPT_ERROR_MSG=""
285: # Function to handle script exit/return based on mode
286: script_exit() {
287:     local exit_code=${1:-0}
288:     local error_msg=${2:-""}
289:     if [ "$SILENT_MODE" = true ] && [ "$IS_SOURCED" = true ]; then
290:         # In silent mode when sourced, set error flag instead of exiting
291:         if [ $exit_code -ne 0 ]; then
292:             SCRIPT_ERROR=true
293:             SCRIPT_ERROR_MSG="$error_msg"
294:         fi
295:         # Don't exit - let the script continue so credentials can be checked
296:         return $exit_code
297:     else
298:         # Normal mode - exit normally
299:         exit $exit_code
300:     fi
301: }
302: # Check for --help flag first
303: if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then
304:     ARG=$(echo "$1" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
305:     case "$ARG" in
306:         --help|-h|help)
307:             show_help
308:             script_exit 0
309:             ;;
310:     esac
311: fi
312: # Check if account selection or clean was provided as argument
313: if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then
314:     # Use argument if provided
315:     ACCOUNT_ARG=$(echo "$1" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
316:     case "$ACCOUNT_ARG" in
317:         state)
318:             ACCOUNT_TYPE="State"
319:             ROLE_ARN_KEY="AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN"
320:             ACTION="assume"
321:             ;;
322:         dev)
323:             ACCOUNT_TYPE="Dev"
324:             ROLE_ARN_KEY="AWS_DEVELOPMENT_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN"
325:             ACTION="assume"
326:             ;;
327:         prod)
328:             ACCOUNT_TYPE="Prod"
329:             ROLE_ARN_KEY="AWS_PRODUCTION_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN"
330:             ACTION="assume"
331:             ;;
332:         clean)
333:             ACTION="clean"

336:             print_error "Invalid argument: $1"
337:             if [ "$SILENT_MODE" = false ]; then
338:                 echo ""
339:                 show_help
340:             fi
341:             script_exit 1
342:             ;;
343:     esac
344:     if [ "$ACTION" = "assume" ]; then
345:         print_info "Using account from argument: ${ACCOUNT_TYPE}"
346:     fi
347: else
348:     # Interactive prompt for account selection
349:     while true; do
350:         echo ""
351:         print_info "Select an option:"
352:         echo "1) Assume State Account role"
353:         echo "2) Assume Dev Account role"
354:         echo "3) Assume Prod Account role"
355:         echo "4) Clean AWS credentials"
356:         echo "5) Cancel"
357:         read -p "Enter choice [1-5]: " account_choice
358:         case "$account_choice" in
359:             1)
360:                 ACCOUNT_TYPE="State"
361:                 ROLE_ARN_KEY="AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN"
362:                 ACTION="assume"
363:                 break
364:                 ;;
365:             2)
366:                 ACCOUNT_TYPE="Dev"
367:                 ROLE_ARN_KEY="AWS_DEVELOPMENT_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN"
368:                 ACTION="assume"
369:                 break
370:                 ;;
371:             3)
372:                 ACCOUNT_TYPE="Prod"
373:                 ROLE_ARN_KEY="AWS_PRODUCTION_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN"
374:                 ACTION="assume"
375:                 break
376:                 ;;
377:             4)
378:                 ACTION="clean"
379:                 break
380:                 ;;
381:             5)
382:                 print_info "Operation cancelled."
383:                 script_exit 0
384:                 ;;
385:             "")
386:                 print_error "No selection made. Please enter a valid choice [1-5]."
387:                 ;;
388:             *)
389:                 print_error "Invalid choice: '$account_choice'. Please enter a valid choice [1-5]."
390:                 ;;
391:         esac

414:     ROLE_ARN="${DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN}"

416: elif [ "$ACCOUNT_TYPE" = "State" ] && [ -n "${STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN:-}" ]; then
417:     # GitHub Actions: Use STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN for state account
418:     ROLE_ARN="${STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN}"

422: if [ -z "$ROLE_ARN" ]; then

425:     if [ -z "$ROLE_SECRET_JSON" ]; then

427:         script_exit 1 "Failed to retrieve 'github-role' secret from AWS Secrets Manager"
428:     fi
429:     # Extract the selected account role ARN
430:     ROLE_ARN=$(get_secret_key_value "$ROLE_SECRET_JSON" "$ROLE_ARN_KEY" || echo "")
431:     if [ -z "$ROLE_ARN" ]; then

433:         script_exit 1 "Failed to retrieve ${ROLE_ARN_KEY} from secret"
434:     fi

440: # Fall back to AWS Secrets Manager if not found (only needed for Dev and Prod accounts)
441: EXTERNAL_ID=""

443:     if [ -n "${EXTERNAL_ID:-}" ]; then
444:         # GitHub Actions: Use EXTERNAL_ID directly
445:         print_info "Using ExternalId from EXTERNAL_ID environment variable"

448:         print_info "Retrieving ExternalId from AWS Secrets Manager..."
449:         EXTERNAL_ID=$(aws secretsmanager get-secret-value \

454:         if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
455:             print_error "Failed to retrieve 'external-id' secret from AWS Secrets Manager"
456:             print_error "Error: $EXTERNAL_ID"
457:             script_exit 1 "Failed to retrieve 'external-id' secret: $EXTERNAL_ID"
458:         fi
459:         if [ -z "$EXTERNAL_ID" ]; then
460:             print_error "ExternalId secret is empty"
461:             script_exit 1 "ExternalId secret is empty"
462:         fi
463:         print_success "Retrieved ExternalId from AWS Secrets Manager"
464:     fi
465: fi
466: if [ "$SILENT_MODE" = false ]; then
467:     echo ""
468: fi
469: # Assume the selected role
470: if [ -n "$EXTERNAL_ID" ]; then
471:     if ! assume_aws_role "$ROLE_ARN" "$EXTERNAL_ID" "${ACCOUNT_TYPE} Account role" "assume-github-role"; then
472:         script_exit 1 "Failed to assume ${ACCOUNT_TYPE} Account role"
473:     fi
474: else
475:     if ! assume_aws_role "$ROLE_ARN" "" "${ACCOUNT_TYPE} Account role" "assume-github-role"; then
476:         script_exit 1 "Failed to assume ${ACCOUNT_TYPE} Account role"
477:     fi
478: fi
479: # Check if error occurred in silent mode
480: if [ "$SILENT_MODE" = true ] && [ "$IS_SOURCED" = true ] && [ "$SCRIPT_ERROR" = true ]; then
481:     # In silent mode, we've already set the error flag
482:     # Don't exit - let the caller check credentials
483:     :
484: fi
485: if [ "$SILENT_MODE" = false ]; then
486:     echo ""
487: fi
488: # Handle output based on whether script is sourced or executed
489: if [ "$IS_SOURCED" = true ]; then
490:     # Script is sourced - credentials are already exported
491:     print_success "Script completed successfully!"
492:     print_info "AWS credentials are now exported in your current shell session."
493:     print_info "You can now run AWS CLI commands with the assumed role."
494:     if [ "$SILENT_MODE" = false ]; then
495:         echo ""
496:     fi
497: else
498:     # Script is executed - output export commands to stdout (for eval), messages to stderr
499:     print_success "Script completed successfully!" >&2
500:     print_info "AWS credentials ready. Export commands output below:" >&2
501:     print_info "Run: eval \$(./assume-github-role.sh ${1:-})" >&2
502:     echo "" >&2
503:     # Output export commands to stdout (can be eval'd)
504:     echo "export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=\"${ASSUMED_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID}\""
505:     echo "export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=\"${ASSUMED_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY}\""
506:     echo "export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN=\"${ASSUMED_AWS_SESSION_TOKEN}\""
507:     if [ -n "${AWS_REGION:-}" ]; then
508:         echo "export AWS_REGION=\"${AWS_REGION}\""
509:     fi
510: fi
```

## File: scripts/capture-openldap-logs.sh
```bash
 1: #!/usr/bin/env bash
 2: # Capture OpenLDAP pod logs and describe output from the ldap namespace.
 3: # Use when openldap_helm_atomic = false and the release has failed, so pods
 4: # are still present and logs can be collected before manual cleanup.
 5: #
 6: # Usage: ./scripts/capture-openldap-logs.sh [namespace]
 7: #   namespace defaults to "ldap"
 8: # Output: ./openldap-logs/capture-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS/ (or OPENLDAP_LOGS_DIR)
 9: set -euo pipefail
10: NAMESPACE="${1:-ldap}"
11: OUTPUT_BASE="${OPENLDAP_LOGS_DIR:-$(pwd)/openldap-logs}"
12: TIMESTAMP="$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
13: OUTPUT_DIR="$OUTPUT_BASE/capture-$TIMESTAMP"
14: mkdir -p "$OUTPUT_DIR"
15: echo "Capturing OpenLDAP logs to $OUTPUT_DIR"
16: # Pod list and describe
17: kubectl get pods -n "$NAMESPACE" -o wide > "$OUTPUT_DIR/pods.txt" 2>&1 || true
18: kubectl get pods -n "$NAMESPACE" -l app.kubernetes.io/name=openldap-stack-ha -o yaml > "$OUTPUT_DIR/pods-openldap.yaml" 2>&1 || true
19: for pod in $(kubectl get pods -n "$NAMESPACE" -l app.kubernetes.io/name=openldap-stack-ha -o name 2>/dev/null); do
20:   name="${pod#pod/}"
21:   kubectl describe "$pod" -n "$NAMESPACE" > "$OUTPUT_DIR/describe-$name.txt" 2>&1 || true
22:   kubectl logs "$pod" -n "$NAMESPACE" --all-containers --tail=1000 > "$OUTPUT_DIR/logs-$name.txt" 2>&1 || true
23: done
24: # ConfigMap env (LDAP_DOMAIN etc.)
25: kubectl get configmap -n "$NAMESPACE" -l "app.kubernetes.io/name=openldap-stack-ha" -o name 2>/dev/null | while read -r cm; do
26:   name="${cm#configmap/}"
27:   kubectl get "$cm" -n "$NAMESPACE" -o yaml > "$OUTPUT_DIR/configmap-$name.yaml" 2>&1 || true
28: done
29: # Events
30: kubectl get events -n "$NAMESPACE" --sort-by=.lastTimestamp > "$OUTPUT_DIR/events.txt" 2>&1 || true
31: echo "Done. Logs saved under $OUTPUT_DIR"
```

## File: scripts/get-eks-token.sh
```bash
 1: #!/bin/bash
 2: # get-eks-token.sh - Get EKS authentication token with optional cross-account role assumption
 3: #
 4: # Used by Terraform kubernetes and helm providers (exec plugin) for dynamic token generation.
 5: # Generates a fresh EKS token on every Kubernetes API call, preventing token expiration
 6: # issues during long Terraform operations (e.g., Helm releases with 20-minute timeouts).
 7: #
 8: # Environment variables (set by Terraform exec block's env map):
 9: #   EKS_CLUSTER_NAME   - EKS cluster name (required)
10: #   EKS_REGION         - AWS region (required)
11: #   ASSUME_ROLE_ARN    - Role ARN to assume before getting token (optional)
12: #   ASSUME_EXTERNAL_ID - ExternalId for role assumption (optional, used with ASSUME_ROLE_ARN)
13: #
14: # Usage in providers.tf:
15: #   exec {
16: #     api_version = "client.authentication.k8s.io/v1beta1"
17: #     command     = "${path.module}/../get-eks-token.sh"
18: #     env = {
19: #       EKS_CLUSTER_NAME   = local.cluster_name
20: #       EKS_REGION         = var.region
21: #       ASSUME_ROLE_ARN    = var.deployment_account_role_arn != null ? var.deployment_account_role_arn : ""
22: #       ASSUME_EXTERNAL_ID = var.deployment_account_external_id != null ? var.deployment_account_external_id : ""
23: #     }
24: #   }
25: #
26: # Credential flow:
27: #   GitHub Actions: Env has State Account creds → script assumes Deployment Account role → gets EKS token
28: #   Local dev:      Env already has Deployment Account creds → script skips assume-role → gets EKS token directly
29: set -euo pipefail
30: # Validate required environment variables
31: if [ -z "${EKS_CLUSTER_NAME:-}" ]; then
32:   echo "ERROR: EKS_CLUSTER_NAME environment variable is required" >&2
33:   exit 1
34: fi
35: if [ -z "${EKS_REGION:-}" ]; then
36:   echo "ERROR: EKS_REGION environment variable is required" >&2
37:   exit 1
38: fi
39: # If role ARN is provided, assume it first (cross-account access)
40: if [ -n "${ASSUME_ROLE_ARN:-}" ]; then
41:   ASSUME_ROLE_ARGS=(
42:     "sts" "assume-role"
43:     "--role-arn" "$ASSUME_ROLE_ARN"
44:     "--role-session-name" "terraform-eks-token-$(date +%s)"
45:     "--region" "$EKS_REGION"
46:     "--output" "json"
47:   )
48:   # Add ExternalId if provided (required for deployment account roles)
49:   if [ -n "${ASSUME_EXTERNAL_ID:-}" ]; then
50:     ASSUME_ROLE_ARGS+=("--external-id" "$ASSUME_EXTERNAL_ID")
51:   fi
52:   CREDS=$(aws "${ASSUME_ROLE_ARGS[@]}" 2>/dev/null)
53:   export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=$(echo "$CREDS" | jq -r '.Credentials.AccessKeyId')
54:   export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=$(echo "$CREDS" | jq -r '.Credentials.SecretAccessKey')
55:   export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN=$(echo "$CREDS" | jq -r '.Credentials.SessionToken')
56: fi
57: # Get and output the EKS token (ExecCredential JSON format)
58: exec aws eks get-token --cluster-name "$EKS_CLUSTER_NAME" --region "$EKS_REGION" --output json
```

## File: .github/workflows/03-backend_build_push.yaml
```yaml
  1: name: 03 - Backend Build and Push
  2: # This workflow can run in parallel with 03-frontend_build_push.yaml since they
  3: # modify different files (backend vs frontend values.yaml). The git operations
  4: # include fetch/rebase and retry logic to handle concurrent pushes gracefully.
  5: on:
  6:   # push:
  7:   #   branches:
  8:   #     - main
  9:   #   paths:
 10:   #     - 'application/backend/**'
 11:   #     - '.github/workflows/03-backend_build_push.yaml'
 12:   workflow_dispatch:
 13:     inputs:
 14:       environment:
 15:         description: 'Select Environment'
 16:         required: true
 17:         type: choice
 18:         default: prod
 19:         options:
 20:           - prod
 21:           - dev
 22: env:
 23:   AWS_REGION: us-east-1
 24:   IMAGE_NAME: ldap-2fa-backend
 25: jobs:
 26:   BuildAndPush:
 27:     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
 28:     permissions:
 29:       contents: write
 30:       id-token: write
 31:     outputs:
 32:       image_tag: ${{ steps.build.outputs.image_tag }}
 33:     steps:
 34:       - name: Checkout the repo code
 35:         uses: actions/checkout@v4
 36:         with:
 37:           token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
 38:           fetch-depth: 0  # Fetch full history for proper git operations
 39:       - name: Configure AWS credentials
 40:         uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
 41:         with:
 42:           role-to-assume: ${{ inputs.environment == 'prod' && secrets.AWS_PRODUCTION_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN || secrets.AWS_DEVELOPMENT_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN }}
 43:           role-session-name: GitHubActions-BackendBuildPush
 44:           aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
 45:       - name: Login to Amazon ECR
 46:         id: login-ecr
 47:         uses: aws-actions/amazon-ecr-login@v2
 48:       - name: Get ECR Repository URL
 49:         id: ecr-info
 50:         run: |
 51:           # Get ECR repository name from GitHub variable (set by backend_infra provisioning)
 52:           ECR_REPO_NAME="${{ vars.ECR_REPOSITORY_NAME }}"
 53:           if [ -z "$ECR_REPO_NAME" ]; then
 54:             echo "❌ Error: ECR_REPOSITORY_NAME GitHub variable is not set or is empty"
 55:             echo "   This variable is automatically set when you provision backend infrastructure."
 56:             echo "   Please run the 'Backend Infra Provisioning' workflow or setup-backend.sh script first."
 57:             exit 1
 58:           fi
 59:           ECR_REGISTRY="${{ steps.login-ecr.outputs.registry }}"
 60:           echo "ecr_registry=${ECR_REGISTRY}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
 61:           echo "ecr_repo_name=${ECR_REPO_NAME}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
 62:           echo "ecr_repo_url=${ECR_REGISTRY}/${ECR_REPO_NAME}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
 63:       - name: Build, tag, and push Docker image
 64:         id: build
 65:         working-directory: ./application/backend
 66:         run: |
 67:           # Generate image tag: commit SHA + run ID so re-runs get a unique tag (ECR tags are immutable)
 68:           IMAGE_TAG="${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}-${{ github.sha }}-${{ github.run_id }}"
 69:           # Build the Docker image
 70:           docker build -t ${{ steps.ecr-info.outputs.ecr_repo_url }}:${IMAGE_TAG} .
 71:           # Push to ECR
 72:           docker push ${{ steps.ecr-info.outputs.ecr_repo_url }}:${IMAGE_TAG}
 73:           echo "image_tag=${IMAGE_TAG}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
 74:           echo "full_image=${{ steps.ecr-info.outputs.ecr_repo_url }}:${IMAGE_TAG}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
 75:           echo "✅ Pushed image: ${{ steps.ecr-info.outputs.ecr_repo_url }}:${IMAGE_TAG}"
 76:       - name: Update Helm values with new image
 77:         run: |
 78:           # Update the values.yaml with new image repository and tag
 79:           VALUES_FILE="application/backend/helm/ldap-2fa-backend/values.yaml"
 80:           # Update image repository
 81:           sed -i "s|^  repository:.*|  repository: \"${{ steps.ecr-info.outputs.ecr_repo_url }}\"|" ${VALUES_FILE}
 82:           # Update image tag
 83:           sed -i "s|^  tag:.*|  tag: \"${{ steps.build.outputs.image_tag }}\"|" ${VALUES_FILE}
 84:           echo "✅ Updated ${VALUES_FILE} with new image:"
 85:           grep -A 3 "^image:" ${VALUES_FILE}
 86:       - name: Commit and push changes
 87:         run: |
 88:           git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
 89:           git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
 90:           VALUES_FILE="application/backend/helm/ldap-2fa-backend/values.yaml"
 91:           # Check if there are changes to commit
 92:           if git diff --quiet; then
 93:             echo "No changes to commit"
 94:             exit 0
 95:           fi
 96:           # Save the file content before any git operations
 97:           # This ensures we can re-apply changes if rebase fails
 98:           cat "${VALUES_FILE}" > /tmp/values_backup.yaml
 99:           # Stage and commit the changes first
100:           git add "${VALUES_FILE}"
101:           git commit -m "chore(backend): update image tag to ${{ steps.build.outputs.image_tag }}
102:           Automated update by GitHub Actions workflow.
103:           Commit: ${{ github.sha }}
104:           "
105:           # Fetch latest changes and rebase our commit on top
106:           # This handles parallel workflow runs where another workflow may have pushed
107:           echo "Fetching latest changes from remote..."
108:           git fetch origin main
109:           # Rebase our commit on top of the latest remote changes
110:           # Since workflows modify different files, this should succeed without conflicts
111:           if ! git rebase origin/main; then
112:             echo "⚠️ Rebase failed, resetting and re-applying changes..."
113:             git rebase --abort || true
114:             git reset --hard origin/main
115:             git checkout main
116:             # Restore our changes from backup
117:             cp /tmp/values_backup.yaml "${VALUES_FILE}"
118:             git add "${VALUES_FILE}"
119:             git commit -m "chore(backend): update image tag to ${{ steps.build.outputs.image_tag }}
120:           Automated update by GitHub Actions workflow.
121:           Commit: ${{ github.sha }}
122:           "
123:           fi
124:           # Push changes with retry logic to handle parallel workflow runs
125:           MAX_RETRIES=3
126:           RETRY_COUNT=0
127:           while [ $RETRY_COUNT -lt $MAX_RETRIES ]; do
128:             if git push origin main; then
129:               echo "✅ Changes committed and pushed successfully"
130:               break
131:             else
132:               RETRY_COUNT=$((RETRY_COUNT + 1))
133:               if [ $RETRY_COUNT -lt $MAX_RETRIES ]; then
134:                 echo "⚠️ Push failed, fetching latest changes and retrying (attempt $RETRY_COUNT/$MAX_RETRIES)..."
135:                 git fetch origin main
136:                 if ! git rebase origin/main; then
137:                   echo "⚠️ Rebase conflict during retry, resetting and re-applying..."
138:                   git rebase --abort || true
139:                   git reset --hard origin/main
140:                   git checkout main
141:                   # Restore our changes from backup
142:                   cp /tmp/values_backup.yaml "${VALUES_FILE}"
143:                   git add "${VALUES_FILE}"
144:                   git commit -m "chore(backend): update image tag to ${{ steps.build.outputs.image_tag }}
145:           Automated update by GitHub Actions workflow.
146:           Commit: ${{ github.sha }}
147:           "
148:                 fi
149:                 sleep 2
150:               else
151:                 echo "❌ Failed to push after $MAX_RETRIES attempts"
152:                 exit 1
153:               fi
154:             fi
155:           done
156:   Summary:
157:     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
158:     permissions:
159:       contents: read
160:     needs: BuildAndPush
161:     if: success()
162:     steps:
163:       - name: Build Summary
164:         run: |
165:           echo "## Backend Build Summary" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
166:           echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
167:           echo "✅ **Image Tag:** ${{ needs.BuildAndPush.outputs.image_tag }}" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
168:           echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
169:           echo "**Next Steps:**" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
170:           echo "- If ArgoCD Applications are registered, they will automatically detect the git changes and sync the deployment." >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
171:           echo "- For manual deployment, use the image tag above with Helm." >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
```

```yaml
111:           if ! git rebase origin/main; then

113:             git rebase --abort || true
114:             git reset --hard origin/main

120:           Automated update by GitHub Actions workflow.

124:           # Push changes with retry logic to handle parallel workflow runs
125:           MAX_RETRIES=3
126:           RETRY_COUNT=0
127:           while [ $RETRY_COUNT -lt $MAX_RETRIES ]; do
128:             if git push origin main; then
129:               echo "✅ Changes committed and pushed successfully"
130:               break
131:             else
132:               RETRY_COUNT=$((RETRY_COUNT + 1))
133:               if [ $RETRY_COUNT -lt $MAX_RETRIES ]; then

138:                   git rebase --abort || true

140:                   git checkout main

145:           Automated update by GitHub Actions workflow.

147:           "

152:                 exit 1
```

```python
  1: """Redis client for shared storage (SMS OTP and login challenges).
  2: All backend storage is in Redis so that single- and multi-replica deployments
  3: behave the same. In-memory storage is not used.
  4: """
  5: import json
  6: import logging
  7: from typing import Optional
  8: import redis
  9: from app.config import get_settings
 10: logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
 11: class RedisOTPClient:
 12:     """Redis client for SMS OTP operations.
 13:     Provides methods for storing, retrieving, and managing SMS OTP codes
 14:     with automatic TTL-based expiration.
 15:     """
 16:     def __init__(self) -> None:
 17:         """Initialize the Redis client (always attempt connection; Redis is required)."""
 18:         self._settings = get_settings()
 19:         self._client: Optional[redis.Redis] = None
 20:         self._connected = False
 21:         self._initialize_client()
 22:     def _initialize_client(self) -> None:
 23:         """Initialize the Redis client connection."""
 24:         try:
 25:             self._client = redis.Redis(
 26:                 host=self._settings.redis_host,
 27:                 port=self._settings.redis_port,
 28:                 password=self._settings.redis_password or None,
 29:                 db=self._settings.redis_db,
 30:                 ssl=self._settings.redis_ssl,
 31:                 decode_responses=True,
 32:                 socket_connect_timeout=5,
 33:                 socket_timeout=5,
 34:                 retry_on_timeout=True,
 35:             )
 36:             # Test connection
 37:             self._client.ping()
 38:             self._connected = True
 39:             logger.info(
 40:                 "Redis connected successfully to %s:%s",
 41:                 self._settings.redis_host,
 42:                 self._settings.redis_port,
 43:             )
 44:         except redis.ConnectionError as e:
 45:             logger.error("Failed to connect to Redis: %s", e)
 46:             self._connected = False
 47:             self._client = None
 48:         except redis.AuthenticationError as e:
 49:             logger.error("Redis authentication failed: %s", e)
 50:             self._connected = False
 51:             self._client = None
 52:     @property
 53:     def is_enabled(self) -> bool:
 54:         """Check if Redis is enabled in settings."""
 55:         return self._settings.redis_enabled
 56:     @property
 57:     def is_connected(self) -> bool:
 58:         """Check if Redis client is connected."""
 59:         if not self._connected or not self._client:
 60:             return False
 61:         try:
 62:             self._client.ping()
 63:             return True
 64:         except (redis.ConnectionError, redis.TimeoutError):
 65:             self._connected = False
 66:             return False
 67:     def _get_key(self, username: str) -> str:
 68:         """Generate the Redis key for a username."""
 69:         return f"{self._settings.redis_key_prefix}{username}"
 70:     def store_code(
 71:         self,
 72:         username: str,
 73:         code: str,
 74:         phone_number: str,
 75:         ttl_seconds: Optional[int] = None,
 76:     ) -> bool:
 77:         """Store OTP code with automatic TTL expiration.
 78:         Args:
 79:             username: The username to store the code for
 80:             code: The verification code
 81:             phone_number: The phone number (for reference)
 82:             ttl_seconds: Time-to-live in seconds (defaults to settings value)
 83:         Returns:
 84:             True if successful, False otherwise
 85:         """
 86:         if not self.is_connected:
 87:             logger.error("Redis not connected, cannot store code")
 88:             return False
 89:         try:
 90:             key = self._get_key(username)
 91:             value = json.dumps({
 92:                 "code": code,
 93:                 "phone_number": phone_number,
 94:             })
 95:             ttl = ttl_seconds or self._settings.sms_code_expiry_seconds
 96:             self._client.setex(key, ttl, value)
 97:             logger.debug("Stored OTP code for %s with TTL %ss", username, ttl)
 98:             return True
 99:         except redis.RedisError as e:
100:             logger.error("Failed to store OTP code: %s", e)
101:             return False
102:     def get_code(self, username: str) -> Optional[dict]:
103:         """Retrieve OTP code data if not expired.
104:         Args:
105:             username: The username to retrieve the code for
106:         Returns:
107:             Dictionary with 'code' and 'phone_number' keys, or None if not found
108:         """
109:         if not self.is_connected:
110:             logger.error("Redis not connected, cannot get code")
111:             return None
112:         try:
113:             key = self._get_key(username)
114:             value = self._client.get(key)
115:             if value is None:
116:                 logger.debug("No OTP code found for %s", username)
117:                 return None
118:             data = json.loads(value)
119:             logger.debug("Retrieved OTP code for %s", username)
120:             return data
121:         except redis.RedisError as e:
122:             logger.error("Failed to retrieve OTP code: %s", e)
123:             return None
124:         except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
125:             logger.error("Failed to decode OTP data: %s", e)
126:             return None
127:     def delete_code(self, username: str) -> bool:
128:         """Delete OTP code after successful verification.
129:         Args:
130:             username: The username to delete the code for
131:         Returns:
132:             True if successful, False otherwise
133:         """
134:         if not self.is_connected:
135:             logger.error("Redis not connected, cannot delete code")
136:             return False
137:         try:
138:             key = self._get_key(username)
139:             deleted = self._client.delete(key)
140:             logger.debug("Deleted OTP code for %s: %s", username, deleted > 0)
141:             return deleted > 0
142:         except redis.RedisError as e:
143:             logger.error("Failed to delete OTP code: %s", e)
144:             return False
145:     def _get_login_challenge_key(self, challenge_token: str) -> str:
146:         """Redis key for a login challenge (shared across replicas)."""
147:         return f"{self._settings.redis_key_prefix}login_challenge:{challenge_token}"
148:     _LOGIN_CHALLENGE_TTL_SECONDS = 300  # 5 minutes
149:     def store_login_challenge(
150:         self,
151:         challenge_token: str,
152:         user_id: str,
153:         username: str,
154:         remember_me: bool = False,
155:     ) -> bool:
156:         """Store login challenge for two-step auth (shared across backend replicas)."""
157:         if not self.is_connected:
158:             return False
159:         try:
160:             key = self._get_login_challenge_key(challenge_token)
161:             value = json.dumps({
162:                 "user_id": user_id,
163:                 "username": username,
164:                 "remember_me": remember_me,
165:             })
166:             self._client.setex(key, self._LOGIN_CHALLENGE_TTL_SECONDS, value)
167:             logger.debug("Stored login challenge for %s", username)
168:             return True
169:         except redis.RedisError as e:
170:             logger.error("Failed to store login challenge: %s", e)
171:             return False
172:     def get_login_challenge(self, challenge_token: str) -> Optional[dict]:
173:         """Get login challenge data if not expired."""
174:         if not self.is_connected:
175:             return None
176:         try:
177:             key = self._get_login_challenge_key(challenge_token)
178:             value = self._client.get(key)
179:             if value is None:
180:                 return None
181:             data = json.loads(value)
182:             return data
183:         except redis.RedisError as e:
184:             logger.error("Failed to get login challenge: %s", e)
185:             return None
186:         except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
187:             logger.error("Failed to decode login challenge: %s", e)
188:             return None
189:     def delete_login_challenge(self, challenge_token: str) -> bool:
190:         """Remove login challenge after successful verify."""
191:         if not self.is_connected:
192:             return False
193:         try:
194:             key = self._get_login_challenge_key(challenge_token)
195:             deleted = self._client.delete(key)
196:             return deleted > 0
197:         except redis.RedisError as e:
198:             logger.error("Failed to delete login challenge: %s", e)
199:             return False
200:     def code_exists(self, username: str) -> bool:
201:         """Check if valid OTP code exists for user.
202:         Args:
203:             username: The username to check
204:         Returns:
205:             True if code exists, False otherwise
206:         """
207:         if not self.is_connected:
208:             return False
209:         try:
210:             key = self._get_key(username)
211:             return self._client.exists(key) > 0
212:         except redis.RedisError as e:
213:             logger.error("Failed to check OTP code existence: %s", e)
214:             return False
215:     def get_ttl(self, username: str) -> int:
216:         """Get remaining TTL for a user's OTP code.
217:         Args:
218:             username: The username to check
219:         Returns:
220:             TTL in seconds, -1 if no expiry, -2 if key doesn't exist
221:         """
222:         if not self.is_connected:
223:             return -2
224:         try:
225:             key = self._get_key(username)
226:             return self._client.ttl(key)
227:         except redis.RedisError as e:
228:             logger.error("Failed to get TTL: %s", e)
229:             return -2
230:     def health_check(self) -> dict:
231:         """Perform health check on Redis connection.
232:         Returns:
233:             Dictionary with health status information
234:         """
235:         try:
236:             if self._client and self._client.ping():
237:                 info = self._client.info("server")
238:                 return {
239:                     "enabled": self.is_enabled,
240:                     "connected": True,
241:                     "status": "healthy",
242:                     "redis_version": info.get("redis_version", "unknown"),
243:                     "error": None,
244:                 }
245:         except redis.RedisError as e:
246:             return {
247:                 "enabled": self.is_enabled,
248:                 "connected": False,
249:                 "status": "unhealthy",
250:                 "redis_version": None,
251:                 "error": str(e),
252:             }
253:         return {
254:             "enabled": self.is_enabled,
255:             "connected": False,
256:             "status": "disconnected",
257:             "redis_version": None,
258:             "error": None,
259:         }
260: def store_login_challenge(
261:     challenge_token: str,
262:     user_id: str,
263:     username: str,
264:     remember_me: bool = False,
265: ) -> bool:
266:     """Store login challenge in Redis. Returns True if stored, False if Redis unavailable."""
267:     client = get_otp_client()
268:     return client.store_login_challenge(
269:         challenge_token, user_id, username, remember_me
270:     )
271: def get_login_challenge(challenge_token: str) -> Optional[dict]:
272:     """Get login challenge from Redis. Returns None if not found or Redis unavailable."""
273:     client = get_otp_client()
274:     return client.get_login_challenge(challenge_token)
275: def delete_login_challenge(challenge_token: str) -> bool:
276:     """Delete login challenge from Redis. Returns True if deleted or key absent."""
277:     client = get_otp_client()
278:     return client.delete_login_challenge(challenge_token)
279: _otp_client: Optional[RedisOTPClient] = None
280: def get_otp_client() -> RedisOTPClient:
281:     """Get Redis OTP client instance, reconnecting if needed."""
282:     global _otp_client
283:     if _otp_client is None or not _otp_client._connected:
284:         _otp_client = RedisOTPClient()
285:     return _otp_client
```

```python
  1: """SMS client for sending verification codes via AWS SNS.
  2: Uses Direct SMS: sns.publish(PhoneNumber=..., Message=..., MessageAttributes=...).
  3: No SNS topic is required. See:
  4: - Publish API: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/api/API_Publish.html
  5: - SMS to phone: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/sms_publish-to-phone.html
  6: - Message attributes (SMSType, SenderID): https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/sns-message-attributes.html
  7: """
  8: import logging
  9: import random
 10: import re
 11: import string
 12: from typing import Optional
 13: import hashlib
 14: import boto3
 15: from botocore.exceptions import BotoCoreError, ClientError
 16: from app.config import Settings, get_settings
 17: logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
 18: class SMSClient:
 19:     """Client for SMS operations using AWS SNS."""
 20:     # E.164 phone number format regex
 21:     E164_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^\+[1-9]\d{1,14}$")
 22:     def __init__(self, settings: Optional[Settings] = None):
 23:         """Initialize SMS client with settings."""
 24:         self.settings = settings or get_settings()
 25:         self._sns_client = None
 26:     @property
 27:     def sns_client(self):
 28:         """Get or create SNS client."""
 29:         if self._sns_client is None:
 30:             self._sns_client = boto3.client(
 31:                 "sns",
 32:                 region_name=self.settings.aws_region,
 33:             )
 34:         return self._sns_client
 35:     def validate_phone_number(self, phone_number: str) -> tuple[bool, str]:
 36:         """
 37:         Validate phone number format (E.164).
 38:         Args:
 39:             phone_number: Phone number to validate
 40:         Returns:
 41:             Tuple of (is_valid, error_message)
 42:         """
 43:         if not phone_number:
 44:             return False, "Phone number is required"
 45:         # Check E.164 format
 46:         if not self.E164_PATTERN.match(phone_number):
 47:             return False, (
 48:                 "Invalid phone number format. "
 49:                 "Use E.164 format: +[country code][number] (e.g., +14155552671)"
 50:             )
 51:         return True, ""
 52:     def generate_verification_code(self, length: int = 6) -> str:
 53:         """
 54:         Generate a random numeric verification code.
 55:         Args:
 56:             length: Length of the code (default: 6)
 57:         Returns:
 58:             Verification code string
 59:         """
 60:         return "".join(random.choices(string.digits, k=length))
 61:     def send_verification_code(
 62:         self,
 63:         phone_number: str,
 64:         code: str,
 65:         sender_id: Optional[str] = None,
 66:     ) -> tuple[bool, str, Optional[str]]:
 67:         """
 68:         Send a verification code via SMS.
 69:         Args:
 70:             phone_number: Recipient phone number (E.164 format)
 71:             code: Verification code to send
 72:             sender_id: Optional sender ID override
 73:         Returns:
 74:             Tuple of (success, message, message_id)
 75:         """
 76:         # Validate phone number
 77:         is_valid, error = self.validate_phone_number(phone_number)
 78:         if not is_valid:
 79:             return False, error, None
 80:         # Format message (AWS SNS: max 140 chars per segment, 1600 per Publish)
 81:         message = self.settings.sms_message_template.format(code=code)
 82:         if len(message) > 1600:
 83:             return False, "SMS message exceeds maximum length (1600 characters)", None
 84:         if len(message) > 140:
 85:             logger.info(
 86:                 "SMS message length %d exceeds 140 chars; SNS will send as multiple segments",
 87:                 len(message),
 88:             )
 89:         try:
 90:             # Reserved SMS message attributes per AWS (DataType String, StringValue)
 91:             message_attributes = {
 92:                 "AWS.SNS.SMS.SMSType": {
 93:                     "DataType": "String",
 94:                     "StringValue": self.settings.sms_type,
 95:                 }
 96:             }
 97:             effective_sender_id = sender_id or self.settings.sms_sender_id
 98:             if effective_sender_id:
 99:                 message_attributes["AWS.SNS.SMS.SenderID"] = {
100:                     "DataType": "String",
101:                     "StringValue": effective_sender_id,
102:                 }
103:             # Direct SMS: PhoneNumber (E.164), Message, MessageAttributes (no TopicArn)
104:             response = self.sns_client.publish(
105:                 PhoneNumber=phone_number,
106:                 Message=message,
107:                 MessageAttributes=message_attributes,
108:             )
109:             message_id = response.get("MessageId")
110:             logger.info(
111:                 "SMS sent successfully. MessageId: %s", message_id
112:             )
113:             return True, "Verification code sent", message_id
114:         except ClientError as e:
115:             error_code = e.response.get("Error", {}).get("Code", "Unknown")
116:             error_message = e.response.get("Error", {}).get("Message", str(e))
117:             logger.error("SNS ClientError sending SMS: %s - %s", error_code, error_message)
118:             # Handle specific error codes
119:             if error_code == "InvalidParameter":
120:                 return False, "Invalid phone number", None
121:             elif error_code == "OptedOut":
122:                 return False, "Phone number has opted out of SMS", None
123:             elif error_code == "InternalError":
124:                 return False, "SMS service temporarily unavailable", None
125:             else:
126:                 return False, f"Failed to send SMS: {error_message}", None
127:         except BotoCoreError as e:
128:             error_type = type(e).__name__
129:             logger.error(
130:                 "BotoCoreError sending SMS: %s - %s (check AWS credentials, "
131:                 "IRSA, VPC endpoint for SNS, and network connectivity)",
132:                 error_type,
133:                 e,
134:                 exc_info=True,
135:             )
136:             return False, "SMS service error", None
137:         except Exception as e:
138:             logger.error("Unexpected error sending SMS: %s", e)
139:             return False, "Failed to send verification code", None
140:     def check_opt_out_status(self, phone_number: str) -> tuple[bool, bool]:
141:         """
142:         Check if a phone number has opted out of SMS.
143:         Args:
144:             phone_number: Phone number to check
145:         Returns:
146:             Tuple of (success, is_opted_out)
147:         """
148:         try:
149:             response = self.sns_client.check_if_phone_number_is_opted_out(
150:                 phoneNumber=phone_number
151:             )
152:             return True, response.get("isOptedOut", False)
153:         except Exception as e:
154:             logger.error("Error checking opt-out status: %s", e)
155:             return False, False
156:     def opt_in_phone_number(self, phone_number: str) -> tuple[bool, str]:
157:         """
158:         Opt in a phone number that was previously opted out.
159:         Args:
160:             phone_number: Phone number to opt in
161:         Returns:
162:             Tuple of (success, message)
163:         """
164:         try:
165:             self.sns_client.opt_in_phone_number(phoneNumber=phone_number)
166:             phone_hash = hashlib.sha256(phone_number.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:8]
167:             logger.info("Phone number opted in (hash=%s)", phone_hash)
168:             return True, "Phone number opted in successfully"
169:         except ClientError as e:
170:             error_message = e.response.get("Error", {}).get("Message", str(e))
171:             logger.error("SNS opt-in error: %s", error_message)
172:             return False, f"Failed to opt in: {error_message}"
173:         except Exception as e:
174:             logger.error("Unexpected error opting in phone: %s", e)
175:             return False, "Failed to opt in phone number"
```

```css
 404: /* Button styles */
 405: .btn {

 418: .btn-primary {

1003:         align-items: flex-start;

1006:     .user-actions {

1009: }
1010: /* Dark mode support */
1011: @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
1012:     :root {
1013:         --background-color: #0f172a;
1014:         --card-background: #1e293b;
1015:         --text-primary: #f1f5f9;
1016:         --text-secondary: #94a3b8;
1017:         --border-color: #334155;
1018:         --input-background: #0f172a;
1019:     }
1020:     body {
1021:         background: linear-gradient(135deg, #1e1b4b 0%, #312e81 100%);
1022:     }
1023:     .form-group input:focus,
1024:     .form-group select:focus {
1025:         background: var(--card-background);
1026:     }
1027:     .qr-code {
1028:         background: white;
1029:     }
1030:     .user-card {

1038:     }

1040: /* Loading spinner */

1044:     }
1045: }
1046: .spinner {

1048:     height: 20px;
1049:     border: 2px solid transparent;
1050:     border-top-color: currentColor;

1053:     display: inline-block;
1054:     margin-right: 8px;

1066:     border-radius: 4px;
1067: }
1068: .admin-users-list::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb:hover {
1069:     background: var(--text-secondary);
1070: }
1071: /* ============================================
1072:    Top Navigation Bar
1073:    ============================================ */
1074: .top-bar {

1077:     left: 0;

1091:     padding: 0 24px;

1093: .top-bar-brand {
```

## File: application/providers.tf
```hcl
  1: terraform {
  2:   required_providers {
  3:     aws = {
  4:       source  = "hashicorp/aws"
  5:       version = ">= 6.21.0"
  6:     }
  7:     kubernetes = {
  8:       source  = "hashicorp/kubernetes"
  9:       version = "~> 2.0"
 10:     }
 11:     helm = {
 12:       source  = "hashicorp/helm"
 13:       version = "~> 2.0"
 14:     }
 15:     time = {
 16:       source  = "hashicorp/time"
 17:       version = "~> 0.9"
 18:     }
 19:     external = {
 20:       source  = "hashicorp/external"
 21:       version = "~> 2.0"
 22:     }
 23:   }
 24: 
 25:   backend "s3" {
 26:     # Backend configuration provided via backend.hcl file
 27:     encrypt      = true
 28:     use_lockfile = true
 29:   }
 30: 
 31:   required_version = "~> 1.14.0"
 32: }
 33: 
 34: provider "aws" {
 35:   region = var.region
 36: 
 37:   # Assume role in deployment account (Account B) if role ARN is provided
 38:   # This allows GitHub Actions to authenticate with Account A (for state)
 39:   # while Terraform provider uses Account B (for resource deployment)
 40:   # ExternalId is required for security when assuming cross-account roles
 41:   dynamic "assume_role" {
 42:     for_each = var.deployment_account_role_arn != null ? [1] : []
 43:     content {
 44:       role_arn    = var.deployment_account_role_arn
 45:       external_id = var.deployment_account_external_id
 46:     }
 47:   }
 48: }
 49: 
 50: # Provider alias for state account (where Route53 hosted zone resides)
 51: provider "aws" {
 52:   alias  = "state_account"
 53:   region = var.region
 54: 
 55:   # Assume role in state account if role ARN is provided
 56:   # This allows querying Route53 hosted zones from the state account
 57:   # while deploying resources to the deployment account
 58:   # Note: ACM certificates are in deployment accounts (public ACM requested per account)
 59:   # Note: ExternalId is not used for state account role assumption (by design)
 60:   dynamic "assume_role" {
 61:     for_each = var.state_account_role_arn != null ? [1] : []
 62:     content {
 63:       role_arn = var.state_account_role_arn
 64:     }
 65:   }
 66: }
 67: 
 68: # Read backend_infra backend.hcl to get bucket, region, and state key (BACKEND_PREFIX)
 69: # All remote state information comes from backend_infra since all states are in the same bucket
 70: data "local_file" "backend_infra_backend_config" {
 71:   filename = "${path.module}/../backend_infra/backend.hcl"
 72: }
 73: 
 74: # Read application_infra backend.hcl to get its state key (APPLICATION_INFRA_PREFIX)
 75: data "local_file" "application_infra_backend_config" {
 76:   filename = "${path.module}/../application_infra/backend.hcl"
 77: }
 78: 
 79: locals {
 80:   # Parse backend_infra backend.hcl to extract bucket and region
 81:   # All states are stored in the same S3 bucket, so we use backend_infra's bucket and region
 82:   # backend.hcl format: bucket = "value", region = "value"
 83:   # If backend.hcl doesn't exist, these will be null and remote state won't be used
 84:   backend_bucket = try(
 85:     regex("bucket\\s*=\\s*\"([^\"]+)\"", data.local_file.backend_infra_backend_config.content)[0],
 86:     null
 87:   )
 88: 
 89:   # Parse backend_infra backend.hcl to get BACKEND_PREFIX
 90:   # This ensures backend_infra uses its own prefix from repository variable
 91:   backend_key_backend_infra = try(
 92:     regex("key\\s*=\\s*\"([^\"]+)\"", data.local_file.backend_infra_backend_config.content)[0],
 93:     "backend_state/terraform.tfstate" # fallback if backend.hcl doesn't exist
 94:   )
 95: 
 96:   # Parse application_infra backend.hcl to get APPLICATION_INFRA_PREFIX
 97:   # This ensures application_infra uses its own prefix, separate from APPLICATION_PREFIX
 98:   backend_key_application_infra = try(
 99:     regex("key\\s*=\\s*\"([^\"]+)\"", data.local_file.application_infra_backend_config.content)[0],
100:     "application_infra_state/terraform.tfstate" # fallback if backend.hcl doesn't exist
101:   )
102: 
103:   backend_region = try(
104:     regex("region\\s*=\\s*\"([^\"]+)\"", data.local_file.backend_infra_backend_config.content)[0],
105:     var.region
106:   )
107: 
108:   # Determine workspace name: use provided variable or derive from region and env
109:   # This matches the workspace naming convention used in scripts: ${region}-${env}
110:   # The workspace argument in terraform_remote_state will handle the workspace prefix automatically
111:   terraform_workspace = coalesce(
112:     var.terraform_workspace,
113:     "${var.region}-${var.env}"
114:   )
115: }
116: 
117: # Retrieve cluster name and ECR info from backend_infra state
118: # Uses the workspace argument to automatically handle workspace-prefixed state keys
119: # Reference: https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/state/remote-state-data
120: data "terraform_remote_state" "backend_infra" {
121:   count   = local.backend_bucket != null ? 1 : 0
122:   backend = "s3"
123: 
124:   # Use workspace argument to specify which workspace state to access
125:   # For S3 backend: "default" workspace uses base key, other workspaces use env:/${workspace}/${key}
126:   # Always pass the workspace value explicitly to ensure correct state lookup
127:   workspace = local.terraform_workspace
128: 
129:   config = merge(
130:     {
131:       bucket = local.backend_bucket
132:       key    = local.backend_key_backend_infra
133:       region = local.backend_region
134:     },
135:     # Add assume_role block to assume state account role when accessing remote state
136:     # This allows cross-account state access without requiring provider configuration
137:     # Note: Terraform 1.6.0+ requires assume_role block instead of top-level role_arn
138:     var.state_account_role_arn != null ? {
139:       assume_role = {
140:         role_arn = var.state_account_role_arn
141:       }
142:     } : {}
143:   )
144: }
145: 
146: # Retrieve StorageClass, ArgoCD capability outputs, and ALB DNS from application_infra state
147: data "terraform_remote_state" "application_infra" {
148:   count   = local.backend_bucket != null ? 1 : 0
149:   backend = "s3"
150: 
151:   workspace = local.terraform_workspace
152: 
153:   config = merge(
154:     {
155:       bucket = local.backend_bucket
156:       key    = local.backend_key_application_infra
157:       region = local.backend_region
158:     },
159:     var.state_account_role_arn != null ? {
160:       assume_role = {
161:         role_arn = var.state_account_role_arn
162:       }
163:     } : {}
164:   )
165: }
166: 
167: locals {
168:   # Get cluster name from remote state if available, otherwise use provided value or calculate it
169:   cluster_name = coalesce(
170:     try(data.terraform_remote_state.backend_infra[0].outputs.cluster_name, null),
171:     var.cluster_name,
172:     "${var.prefix}-${var.region}-${var.cluster_name_component}-${var.env}"
173:   )
174: }
175: 
176: data "aws_eks_cluster" "cluster" {
177:   name = local.cluster_name
178: }
179: 
180: # EKS token exec configuration
181: # Uses get-eks-token.sh to generate fresh tokens on every Kubernetes API call,
182: # preventing token expiration during long Terraform operations (Helm releases, etc.).
183: # The script handles cross-account role assumption with ExternalId when needed.
184: locals {
185:   eks_exec_env = {
186:     EKS_CLUSTER_NAME   = local.cluster_name
187:     EKS_REGION         = var.region
188:     ASSUME_ROLE_ARN    = var.deployment_account_role_arn != null ? var.deployment_account_role_arn : ""
189:     ASSUME_EXTERNAL_ID = var.deployment_account_external_id != null ? var.deployment_account_external_id : ""
190:   }
191: }
192: 
193: provider "kubernetes" {
194:   host                   = data.aws_eks_cluster.cluster.endpoint
195:   cluster_ca_certificate = base64decode(data.aws_eks_cluster.cluster.certificate_authority[0].data)
196: 
197:   exec {
198:     api_version = "client.authentication.k8s.io/v1beta1"
199:     command     = "${path.module}/../scripts/get-eks-token.sh"
200:     env         = local.eks_exec_env
201:   }
202: }
203: 
204: provider "helm" {
205:   kubernetes {
206:     host                   = data.aws_eks_cluster.cluster.endpoint
207:     cluster_ca_certificate = base64decode(data.aws_eks_cluster.cluster.certificate_authority[0].data)
208: 
209:     exec {
210:       api_version = "client.authentication.k8s.io/v1beta1"
211:       command     = "${path.module}/../scripts/get-eks-token.sh"
212:       env         = local.eks_exec_env
213:     }
214:   }
215: }
```

```yaml
 1: {{- if not .Values.existingSecret }}
 2: apiVersion: v1
 3: kind: Secret
 4: metadata:
 5:   name: {{ template "openldap.fullname" . }}
 6:   labels:
 7:     {{- include "openldap.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
 8:     {{- with .Values.extraLabels }}
 9:     {{- toYaml . | nindent 4 }}
10:     {{- end }}
11: type: Opaque
12: data:
13:   LDAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD: {{ .Values.adminPassword | b64enc | quote }}
14:   LDAP_CONFIG_PASSWORD: {{ .Values.configPassword | b64enc | quote }}
15: {{- end }}
```

```hcl
 18:     }

 25:   }
 26: 
 27:   required_version = "~> 1.14.0"
 28: }
 29:

 32: 
 33:   # Assume role in deployment account (Account B) if role ARN is provided
 34:   # This allows GitHub Actions to authenticate with Account A (for state)
 35:   # while Terraform provider uses Account B (for resource deployment)
 36:   # ExternalId is required for security when assuming cross-account roles
 37:   dynamic "assume_role" {
 38:     for_each = var.deployment_account_role_arn != null ? [1] : []
 39:     content {
 40:       role_arn    = var.deployment_account_role_arn
 41:       external_id = var.deployment_account_external_id
 42:     }
 43:   }
 44: }
 45: 
 46: # Provider alias for state account (where Route53 hosted zone resides)
 47: provider "aws" {
 48:   alias  = "state_account"
 49:   region = var.region
 50: 
 51:   # Assume role in state account if role ARN is provided
 52:   # This allows querying Route53 hosted zones from the state account
 53:   # while deploying resources to the deployment account
 54:   # Note: ACM certificates are in deployment accounts (public ACM requested per account)
 55:   # Note: ExternalId is not used for state account role assumption (by design)
 56:   dynamic "assume_role" {
 57:     for_each = var.state_account_role_arn != null ? [1] : []
 58:     content {
 59:       role_arn = var.state_account_role_arn
 60:     }
 61:   }
 62: }
 63: 
 64: # Read backend_infra backend.hcl to get bucket, region, and state key (BACKEND_PREFIX)
 65: # All remote state information comes from backend_infra since that's where the state is stored
 66: data "local_file" "backend_infra_backend_config" {
 67:   filename = "${path.module}/../backend_infra/backend.hcl"
 68: }
 69: 
 70: locals {
 71:   # Parse backend_infra backend.hcl to extract bucket, region, and key
 72:   # backend.hcl format: bucket = "value", region = "value", key = "value"
 73:   # If backend.hcl doesn't exist, these will be null and remote state won't be used
 74:   backend_bucket = try(
 75:     regex("bucket\\s*=\\s*\"([^\"]+)\"", data.local_file.backend_infra_backend_config.content)[0],
 76:     null
 77:   )
 78: 
 79:   # Parse backend_infra backend.hcl to get BACKEND_PREFIX
 80:   # This ensures backend_infra uses its own prefix from repository variable
 81:   backend_key = try(
 82:     regex("key\\s*=\\s*\"([^\"]+)\"", data.local_file.backend_infra_backend_config.content)[0],
 83:     "backend_state/terraform.tfstate" # fallback if backend.hcl doesn't exist
 84:   )
 85: 
 86:   backend_region = try(
 87:     regex("region\\s*=\\s*\"([^\"]+)\"", data.local_file.backend_infra_backend_config.content)[0],
 88:     var.region
 89:   )
 90: 
 91:   # Determine workspace name: use provided variable or derive from region and env
 92:   # This matches the workspace naming convention used in scripts: ${region}-${env}
 93:   # The workspace argument in terraform_remote_state will handle the workspace prefix automatically
 94:   terraform_workspace = coalesce(
 95:     var.terraform_workspace,
 96:     "${var.region}-${var.env}"
 97:   )
 98: }
 99: 
100: # Retrieve cluster name from backend_infra state
101: # Uses the workspace argument to automatically handle workspace-prefixed state keys
102: # Reference: https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/state/remote-state-data
103: data "terraform_remote_state" "backend_infra" {
104:   count   = local.backend_bucket != null ? 1 : 0
105:   backend = "s3"
106: 
107:   # Use workspace argument to specify which workspace state to access
108:   # For S3 backend: "default" workspace uses base key, other workspaces use env:/${workspace}/${key}
109:   # Always pass the workspace value explicitly to ensure correct state lookup
110:   workspace = local.terraform_workspace
111: 
112:   config = merge(
113:     {
114:       bucket = local.backend_bucket
115:       key    = local.backend_key
116:       region = local.backend_region
117:     },
118:     # Add assume_role block to assume state account role when accessing remote state
119:     # This allows cross-account state access without requiring provider configuration
120:     # Note: Terraform 1.6.0+ requires assume_role block instead of top-level role_arn
121:     var.state_account_role_arn != null ? {
122:       assume_role = {
123:         role_arn = var.state_account_role_arn
124:       }
125:     } : {}
126:   )
127: }
128: 
129: locals {
130:   # Get cluster name from remote state if available, otherwise use provided value or calculate it
131:   cluster_name = coalesce(
132:     try(data.terraform_remote_state.backend_infra[0].outputs.cluster_name, null),
133:     var.cluster_name,
134:     "${var.prefix}-${var.region}-${var.cluster_name_component}-${var.env}"
135:   )
136: }
137: 
138: data "aws_eks_cluster" "cluster" {
139:   name = local.cluster_name
140: }
141: 
142: # EKS token exec configuration
143: # Uses get-eks-token.sh to generate fresh tokens on every Kubernetes API call,
144: # preventing token expiration during long Terraform operations (Helm releases, etc.).
145: # The script handles cross-account role assumption with ExternalId when needed.
146: locals {
147:   eks_exec_env = {
148:     EKS_CLUSTER_NAME   = local.cluster_name
149:     EKS_REGION         = var.region
150:     ASSUME_ROLE_ARN    = var.deployment_account_role_arn != null ? var.deployment_account_role_arn : ""
151:     ASSUME_EXTERNAL_ID = var.deployment_account_external_id != null ? var.deployment_account_external_id : ""
152:   }
153: }
154:

156:   host                   = data.aws_eks_cluster.cluster.endpoint
157:   cluster_ca_certificate = base64decode(data.aws_eks_cluster.cluster.certificate_authority[0].data)
158: 
159:   exec {
160:     api_version = "client.authentication.k8s.io/v1beta1"
161:     command     = "${path.module}/../scripts/get-eks-token.sh"
162:     env         = local.eks_exec_env
163:   }
164: }
165: 
166: provider "helm" {
167:   kubernetes {
168:     host                   = data.aws_eks_cluster.cluster.endpoint
169:     cluster_ca_certificate = base64decode(data.aws_eks_cluster.cluster.certificate_authority[0].data)
170: 
171:     exec {
172:       api_version = "client.authentication.k8s.io/v1beta1"
173:       command     = "${path.module}/../scripts/get-eks-token.sh"
174:       env         = local.eks_exec_env
175:     }
176:   }
177: }
```
