## File: scripts/mirror-images-to-ecr.sh
```bash
  1: #!/bin/bash
  2: # Script to mirror third-party container images (Redis, PostgreSQL, OpenLDAP) from Docker Hub to ECR
  3: # This eliminates Docker Hub rate limiting and external dependencies during deployments
  4: # Only mirrors images that don't already exist in ECR
  5: #
  6: # Usage: ./mirror-images-to-ecr.sh
  7: #   Requires Docker to be installed and running
  8: #   Uses AWS credentials from environment variables (set by setup-application-infra.sh)
  9: #   Retrieves ECR information from backend_infra Terraform state
 10: set -euo pipefail
 11: # Save caller's working directory before changing to script directory
 12: _MIRROR_CALLER_PWD="$(pwd)"
 13: cd "$(dirname "$0")"
 14: # Resolve BACKEND_FILE relative to caller's working directory
 15: # This ensures the script works correctly regardless of where it lives
 16: if [ -n "${BACKEND_FILE:-}" ] && [[ "$BACKEND_FILE" != /* ]] && [ -f "$_MIRROR_CALLER_PWD/$BACKEND_FILE" ]; then
 17:     BACKEND_FILE="$_MIRROR_CALLER_PWD/$BACKEND_FILE"
 18: fi
 19: # Colors for output (if not already defined by sourcing script)
 20: if [ -z "${RED:-}" ]; then
 21:     RED='\033[0;31m'
 22:     GREEN='\033[0;32m'
 23:     YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
 24:     BLUE='\033[0;34m'
 25:     NC='\033[0m' # No Color
 26: fi
 27: # Function to print colored messages (if not already defined by sourcing script)
 28: if ! declare -f print_error > /dev/null; then
 29:     print_error() {
 30:         echo -e "${RED}ERROR:${NC} $1" >&2
 31:     }
 32: fi
 33: if ! declare -f print_success > /dev/null; then
 34:     print_success() {
 35:         echo -e "${GREEN}SUCCESS:${NC} $1"
 36:     }
 37: fi
 38: if ! declare -f print_info > /dev/null; then
 39:     print_info() {
 40:         echo -e "${YELLOW}INFO:${NC} $1"
 41:     }
 42: fi
 43: info() { echo -e "${BLUE}[INFO]${NC} $*"; }
 44: # Check required tools
 45: for cmd in docker jq; do
 46:   if ! command -v "$cmd" &> /dev/null; then
 47:     print_error "$cmd is required but not installed."
 48:     exit 1
 49:   fi
 50: done
 51: # Check if Docker daemon is running
 52: if ! docker info &> /dev/null 2>&1; then
 53:   print_error "Docker daemon is not running. Please start Docker and try again."
 54:   exit 1
 55: fi
 56: info "Starting ECR image mirroring process..."
 57: echo ""
 58: # Get AWS account ID
 59: AWS_ACCOUNT_ID=$(aws sts get-caller-identity --query Account --output text)
 60: info "AWS Account ID: $AWS_ACCOUNT_ID"
 61: # Use AWS_REGION from environment (set by setup-application.sh)
 62: if [ -z "${AWS_REGION:-}" ]; then
 63:     print_error "AWS_REGION is not set. Run ./setup-application-infra.sh first."
 64:     exit 1
 65: fi
 66: info "AWS Region: $AWS_REGION"
 67: # Use BACKEND_FILE from environment if available, otherwise default to backend.hcl
 68: BACKEND_FILE="${BACKEND_FILE:-backend.hcl}"
 69: # Check if backend file exists
 70: if [ ! -f "$BACKEND_FILE" ]; then
 71:     print_error "$BACKEND_FILE not found. Run ./setup-application-infra.sh first."
 72:     exit 1
 73: fi
 74: # Parse backend configuration (bucket from application_infra backend; backend_infra state key from BACKEND_PREFIX or backend_infra/backend.hcl)
 75: BACKEND_BUCKET=$(grep 'bucket' "$BACKEND_FILE" | sed 's/.*"\(.*\)".*/\1/')
 76: # Backend_infra state key: use BACKEND_PREFIX (set by setup-application-infra.sh or CI) or parse from backend_infra/backend.hcl
 77: if [ -n "${BACKEND_PREFIX:-}" ]; then
 78:     BACKEND_KEY="$BACKEND_PREFIX"
 79:     info "Backend_infra state key (from BACKEND_PREFIX): $BACKEND_KEY"
 80: elif [ -f "../backend_infra/backend.hcl" ]; then
 81:     BACKEND_KEY=$(grep 'key' "../backend_infra/backend.hcl" | sed 's/.*"\(.*\)".*/\1/')
 82:     if [ -z "$BACKEND_KEY" ]; then
 83:         print_error "Could not parse key from ../backend_infra/backend.hcl"
 84:         exit 1
 85:     fi
 86:     info "Backend_infra state key (from ../backend_infra/backend.hcl): $BACKEND_KEY"
 87: else
 88:     print_error "Backend_infra state key not found. Set BACKEND_PREFIX or ensure ../backend_infra/backend.hcl exists."
 89:     exit 1
 90: fi
 91: info "Backend S3 bucket: $BACKEND_BUCKET"
 92: # Workspace: prefer TERRAFORM_WORKSPACE or AWS_REGION+ENVIRONMENT (same as set-k8s-env.sh) for local and CI
 93: if [ -n "${TERRAFORM_WORKSPACE:-}" ]; then
 94:     WORKSPACE="$TERRAFORM_WORKSPACE"
 95:     info "Terraform workspace (from TERRAFORM_WORKSPACE): $WORKSPACE"
 96: elif [ -n "${AWS_REGION:-}" ] && [ -n "${ENVIRONMENT:-}" ]; then
 97:     WORKSPACE="${AWS_REGION}-${ENVIRONMENT}"
 98:     info "Terraform workspace (from AWS_REGION and ENVIRONMENT): $WORKSPACE"
 99: else
100:     WORKSPACE=$(terraform workspace show 2>/dev/null || echo "default")
101:     info "Terraform workspace (from terraform workspace show): $WORKSPACE"
102: fi
103: # Determine state key based on workspace
104: if [ "$WORKSPACE" = "default" ]; then
105:     STATE_KEY="$BACKEND_KEY"
106: else
107:     STATE_KEY="env:/$WORKSPACE/$BACKEND_KEY"
108: fi
109: info "Fetching ECR repository information from s3://$BACKEND_BUCKET/$STATE_KEY"
110: # Fetch ECR URL from backend_infra state using State Account credentials
111: ECR_URL=$(aws s3 cp "s3://$BACKEND_BUCKET/$STATE_KEY" - 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.outputs.ecr_url.value' || echo "")
112: if [ -z "$ECR_URL" ] || [ "$ECR_URL" = "null" ]; then
113:     print_error "Could not retrieve ECR URL from backend_infra state."
114:     print_error "Make sure backend_infra has been deployed and outputs ecr_url."
115:     exit 1
116: fi
117: info "ECR Repository URL: $ECR_URL"
118: # Extract ECR repository name from URL (format: account.dkr.ecr.region.amazonaws.com/repo-name)
119: ECR_REPO_NAME=$(echo "$ECR_URL" | awk -F'/' '{print $NF}')
120: info "ECR Repository Name: $ECR_REPO_NAME"
121: echo ""
122: # ECR is in the Deployment Account, so we need to assume the Deployment Account role
123: # Check if DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN and EXTERNAL_ID are set (from setup-application-infra.sh)
124: if [ -z "${DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN:-}" ]; then
125:     print_error "DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN is not set. Run ./setup-application-infra.sh first."
126:     exit 1
127: fi
128: if [ -z "${EXTERNAL_ID:-}" ]; then
129:     print_error "EXTERNAL_ID is not set. Run ./setup-application-infra.sh first."
130:     exit 1
131: fi
132: print_info "Assuming Deployment Account role for ECR operations: $DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN"
133: print_info "Region: $AWS_REGION"
134: # Assume deployment account role with ExternalId
135: DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_SESSION_NAME="mirror-images-$(date +%s)"
136: DEPLOYMENT_ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT=$(aws sts assume-role \
137:     --role-arn "$DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN" \
138:     --role-session-name "$DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_SESSION_NAME" \
139:     --external-id "$EXTERNAL_ID" \
140:     --region "$AWS_REGION" 2>&1)
141: if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
142:     print_error "Failed to assume Deployment Account role: $DEPLOYMENT_ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT"
143:     exit 1
144: fi
145: # Extract Deployment Account credentials from JSON output
146: if command -v jq &> /dev/null; then
147:     export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=$(echo "$DEPLOYMENT_ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT" | jq -r '.Credentials.AccessKeyId')
148:     export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=$(echo "$DEPLOYMENT_ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT" | jq -r '.Credentials.SecretAccessKey')
149:     export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN=$(echo "$DEPLOYMENT_ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT" | jq -r '.Credentials.SessionToken')
150: else
151:     # Fallback: use sed for JSON parsing (works on both macOS and Linux)
152:     export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=$(echo "$DEPLOYMENT_ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT" | sed -n 's/.*"AccessKeyId"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
153:     export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=$(echo "$DEPLOYMENT_ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT" | sed -n 's/.*"SecretAccessKey"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
154:     export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN=$(echo "$DEPLOYMENT_ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT" | sed -n 's/.*"SessionToken"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
155: fi
156: if [ -z "$AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID" ] || [ -z "$AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY" ] || [ -z "$AWS_SESSION_TOKEN" ]; then
157:     print_error "Failed to extract Deployment Account credentials from assume-role output."
158:     print_error "Output was: $DEPLOYMENT_ASSUME_ROLE_OUTPUT"
159:     exit 1
160: fi
161: # Verify the Deployment Account credentials work
162: DEPLOYMENT_CALLER_ARN=$(aws sts get-caller-identity --region "$AWS_REGION" --query 'Arn' --output text 2>&1)
163: if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
164:     print_error "Failed to verify Deployment Account role credentials: $DEPLOYMENT_CALLER_ARN"
165:     exit 1
166: fi
167: # Extract Deployment Account ID from the ARN
168: DEPLOYMENT_ACCOUNT_ID=$(aws sts get-caller-identity --region "$AWS_REGION" --query 'Account' --output text 2>&1)
169: if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
170:     print_error "Failed to get Deployment Account ID: $DEPLOYMENT_ACCOUNT_ID"
171:     exit 1
172: fi
173: print_success "Successfully assumed Deployment Account role"
174: print_info "Deployment Account role identity: $DEPLOYMENT_CALLER_ARN"
175: print_info "Deployment Account ID: $DEPLOYMENT_ACCOUNT_ID"
176: echo ""
177: # Function to check if an image tag exists in ECR
178: check_ecr_image_exists() {
179:   local tag=$1
180:   # Query ECR for the specific image tag
181:   local result
182:   result=$(aws ecr describe-images \
183:     --repository-name "$ECR_REPO_NAME" \
184:     --region "$AWS_REGION" \
185:     --image-ids imageTag="$tag" \
186:     --query 'imageDetails[0].imageTags[0]' \
187:     --output text 2>/dev/null || echo "None")
188:   if [ "$result" != "None" ] && [ -n "$result" ]; then
189:     return 0  # Image exists
190:   else
191:     return 1  # Image does not exist
192:   fi
193: }
194: # Authenticate Docker to ECR (using Deployment Account ID since ECR is in Deployment Account)
195: info "Authenticating Docker to ECR..."
196: if aws ecr get-login-password --region "$AWS_REGION" | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin "$DEPLOYMENT_ACCOUNT_ID.dkr.ecr.$AWS_REGION.amazonaws.com" 2>/dev/null; then
197:   print_success "Docker authenticated to ECR"
198: else
199:   print_error "Failed to authenticate Docker to ECR"
200:   exit 1
201: fi
202: echo ""
203: # Define images to mirror with specific tags
204: # Format: "source_image:tag ecr_tag"
205: # Note: Using 'latest' tag for Bitnami images as other tags use SHA values
206: # busybox used by OpenLDAP chart init container (copy-custom-ldif); mirroring avoids Docker Hub rate limits
207: IMAGES=(
208:   "bitnami/redis:latest redis-latest"
209:   "bitnami/postgresql:latest postgresql-latest"
210:   "osixia/openldap:1.5.0 openldap-1.5.0"
211:   "osixia/phpldapadmin:0.9.0 phpldapadmin-0.9.0"
212:   "tiredofit/self-service-password:5.2.3 ltb-passwd-5.2.3"
213:   "busybox:1.36 busybox-1.36"
214: )
215: info "Checking which images need to be mirrored..."
216: echo ""
217: IMAGES_TO_MIRROR=()
218: IMAGES_ALREADY_EXIST=()
219: for image_spec in "${IMAGES[@]}"; do
220:   read -r SOURCE_IMAGE ECR_TAG <<< "$image_spec"
221:   if check_ecr_image_exists "$ECR_TAG"; then
222:     info "✓ Image already exists in ECR: $ECR_TAG"
223:     IMAGES_ALREADY_EXIST+=("$ECR_TAG")
224:   else
225:     info "✗ Image not found in ECR: $ECR_TAG (will be mirrored)"
226:     IMAGES_TO_MIRROR+=("$image_spec")
227:   fi
228: done
229: echo ""
230: if [ ${#IMAGES_ALREADY_EXIST[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
231:   print_success "${#IMAGES_ALREADY_EXIST[@]} image(s) already exist in ECR - skipping"
232: fi
233: if [ ${#IMAGES_TO_MIRROR[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
234:   print_success "All required images already exist in ECR. No mirroring needed."
235:   echo ""
236:   exit 0
237: fi
238: info "${#IMAGES_TO_MIRROR[@]} image(s) need to be mirrored to ECR..."
239: echo ""
240: for image_spec in "${IMAGES_TO_MIRROR[@]}"; do
241:   read -r SOURCE_IMAGE ECR_TAG <<< "$image_spec"
242:   info "Processing: $SOURCE_IMAGE -> $ECR_TAG"
243:   # Pull image from Docker Hub
244:   info "  Pulling $SOURCE_IMAGE from Docker Hub..."
245:   if ! docker pull --platform linux/amd64 "$SOURCE_IMAGE"; then
246:     print_error "  Failed to pull $SOURCE_IMAGE"
247:     exit 1
248:   fi
249:   print_success "  Successfully pulled $SOURCE_IMAGE"
250:   # Tag for ECR
251:   ECR_IMAGE="$ECR_URL:$ECR_TAG"
252:   info "  Tagging as $ECR_IMAGE..."
253:   docker tag "$SOURCE_IMAGE" "$ECR_IMAGE"
254:   # Push to ECR
255:   info "  Pushing to ECR..."
256:   if ! docker push "$ECR_IMAGE"; then
257:     print_error "  Failed to push $ECR_IMAGE"
258:     exit 1
259:   fi
260:   print_success "  Successfully pushed $ECR_IMAGE"
261:   # Clean up local images to save space
262:   info "  Cleaning up local images..."
263:   docker rmi "$SOURCE_IMAGE" "$ECR_IMAGE" 2>/dev/null || true
264:   echo ""
265: done
266: print_success "Image mirroring complete!"
267: echo ""
268: # List all images in ECR repository
269: info "Current images in ECR repository '$ECR_REPO_NAME':"
270: aws ecr describe-images --repository-name "$ECR_REPO_NAME" --region "$AWS_REGION" \
271:   --query 'sort_by(imageDetails,& imagePushedAt)[*].[imageTags[0],imagePushedAt,imageSizeInBytes]' \
272:   --output table 2>/dev/null || print_info "Could not list ECR images"
273: echo ""
274: print_success "ECR images are ready for deployment"
```

## File: scripts/set-k8s-env.sh
```bash
  1: #!/bin/bash
  2: # Script to set Kubernetes environment variables for Terraform Helm/Kubernetes providers
  3: # Fetches cluster name from backend_infra Terraform state
  4: # Works for both local development and CI/CD (bash scripts and GitHub Actions workflows)
  5: #
  6: # Usage: source ./set-k8s-env.sh
  7: #   Uses AWS credentials from environment variables (set by setup-application-infra.sh or CI/CD workflow)
  8: #
  9: # Backend_infra state key: use BACKEND_PREFIX (repo variable in CI) or parse from backend_infra/backend.hcl.
 10: # Backend_infra workspace resolution (for S3 state path env:/<workspace>/<BACKEND_PREFIX>):
 11: #   Callers should set one of the following so the correct state is read in all contexts:
 12: #   1. TERRAFORM_WORKSPACE  - explicit workspace (e.g. us-east-1-prod)
 13: #   2. AWS_REGION + ENVIRONMENT - script derives workspace as ${AWS_REGION}-${ENVIRONMENT}
 14: #   3. If neither: uses "terraform workspace show" in script dir (application_infra); only correct
 15: #      when run from application_infra after "terraform workspace select" has been run.
 16: #   GitHub workflows and bash scripts (setup/destroy application and application_infra) should
 17: #   export TERRAFORM_WORKSPACE or both AWS_REGION and ENVIRONMENT before sourcing this script.
 18: set -e
 19: # Get script directory - works correctly when script is sourced
 20: SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
 21: # Save original directory to restore at the end
 22: # IMPORTANT: This script may be sourced from other directories (e.g., application/)
 23: # We must restore the original directory before returning to avoid breaking calling scripts
 24: _SET_K8S_ENV_ORIGINAL_PWD="$(pwd)"
 25: cd "$SCRIPT_DIR"
 26: # Resolve BACKEND_FILE and VARIABLES_FILE relative to caller's working directory
 27: # (before cd changed us to script dir). This ensures the scripts work correctly
 28: # regardless of where the script lives (e.g., scripts/ instead of application_infra/).

271:   name: CLUSTER_NAME_PLACEHOLDER

275:     user: CLUSTER_NAME_PLACEHOLDER
276:   name: CLUSTER_NAME_PLACEHOLDER

306:     sed -i "s|KUBERNETES_MASTER_PLACEHOLDER|$KUBERNETES_MASTER|g" "$KUBE_CONFIG_PATH"
307:     sed -i "s|CLUSTER_NAME_PLACEHOLDER|$CLUSTER_NAME|g" "$KUBE_CONFIG_PATH"
308:     sed -i "s|AWS_REGION_PLACEHOLDER|$AWS_REGION|g" "$KUBE_CONFIG_PATH"
309: fi

312: print_info "kubectl will dynamically fetch tokens using current AWS credentials"

324: unset _SET_K8S_ENV_ORIGINAL_PWD
```

```python
 29:         """Get an admin connection to LDAP."""
 30:         return Connection(
 31:             self.server,
 32:             user=self.settings.ldap_admin_dn,
 33:             password=self.settings.ldap_admin_password,
 34:             auto_bind=True,
 35:             raise_exceptions=True,
 36:         )
 37:     def _get_user_search_base(self) -> str:
 38:         """Get the full user search base DN."""
 39:         user_search_base = self.settings.ldap_user_search_base
 40:         if not user_search_base.endswith(self.settings.ldap_base_dn):
 41:             user_search_base = f"{user_search_base},{self.settings.ldap_base_dn}"
 42:         return user_search_base
 43:     def _get_user_dn(self, username: str) -> str:
 44:         """Construct the user DN from username."""
 45:         return f"uid={escape_rdn(username)},{self._get_user_search_base()}"
 46:     def _get_group_search_base(self) -> str:
 47:         """Get the full group search base DN."""

 50:             group_search_base = f"{group_search_base},{self.settings.ldap_base_dn}"
 51:         return group_search_base
 52:     def _get_group_dn(self, group_name: str) -> str:
 53:         """Construct the group DN from group name."""
 54:         return f"cn={group_name},{self._get_group_search_base()}"
 55:     def _get_next_uid_number(self, conn: Connection) -> int:
 56:         """Get the next available UID number."""
 57:         try:
 58:             conn.search(

 60:                 search_filter="(objectClass=posixAccount)",

 62:             )

 70:         except Exception as e:

 75:         Authenticate a user against LDAP.

 79:         Returns:
 80:             Tuple of (success: bool, message: str)

147:             conn = self._get_admin_connection()
148:             safe_username = escape_filter_chars(username)
149:             search_filter = self.settings.ldap_user_search_filter.format(safe_username)
150:             conn.search(
151:                 search_base=self._get_user_search_base(),
152:                 search_filter=search_filter,
153:                 attributes=["uid"],
154:             )
155:             exists = len(conn.entries) > 0
156:             conn.unbind()
157:             return exists
158:         except LDAPException as e:
159:             logger.error("LDAP error checking user existence: %s", e)
160:             return False
161:     def get_user_attribute(
162:         self, username: str, attribute: str
163:     ) -> Optional[str]:
164:         """
165:         Get a user attribute from LDAP.
166:         Args:
167:             username: The username
168:             attribute: The attribute name to retrieve
169:         Returns:
170:             The attribute value or None if not found
171:         """
172:         try:
173:             conn = self._get_admin_connection()
174:             safe_username = escape_filter_chars(username)
175:             search_filter = self.settings.ldap_user_search_filter.format(safe_username)
176:             conn.search(
177:                 search_base=self._get_user_search_base(),
178:                 search_filter=search_filter,
179:                 attributes=[attribute],
180:             )
181:             if conn.entries:
182:                 entry = conn.entries[0]
183:                 if hasattr(entry, attribute):
184:                     value = getattr(entry, attribute).value
185:                     conn.unbind()
186:                     return value
187:             conn.unbind()
188:             return None
189:         except LDAPException as e:
190:             logger.error("LDAP error getting user attribute: %s", e)
191:             return None
192:     def create_user(
193:         self,
194:         username: str,
195:         password: str,
196:         first_name: str,
197:         last_name: str,
198:         email: str,
199:     ) -> tuple[bool, str]:
200:         """
201:         Create a new user in LDAP.
202:         Args:
203:             username: The username (uid)
204:             password: The user's password
205:             first_name: User's first name
206:             last_name: User's last name
207:             email: User's email address
208:         Returns:
209:             Tuple of (success: bool, message: str)
210:         """
211:         user_dn = self._get_user_dn(username)
212:         try:
213:             conn = self._get_admin_connection()
214:             # Check if user already exists
215:             if self.user_exists(username):
216:                 conn.unbind()
217:                 return False, f"User {username} already exists in LDAP"
218:             # Get next available UID number
219:             uid_number = self._get_next_uid_number(conn)
220:             # Build user attributes
221:             # Using inetOrgPerson + posixAccount for compatibility
222:             attributes = {
223:                 "objectClass": [
224:                     "inetOrgPerson",
225:                     "posixAccount",
226:                     "shadowAccount",
227:                     "top",
228:                 ],
229:                 "uid": username,
230:                 "cn": f"{first_name} {last_name}",
231:                 "sn": last_name,
232:                 "givenName": first_name,
233:                 "mail": email,
234:                 "userPassword": password,
235:                 "uidNumber": str(uid_number),
236:                 "gidNumber": str(self.settings.ldap_users_gid),
237:                 "homeDirectory": f"/home/{username}",
238:                 "loginShell": "/bin/bash",
239:             }
240:             # Create the user
241:             success = conn.add(user_dn, attributes=attributes)
242:             if success:
243:                 logger.info("Created LDAP user: %s (UID: %s)", username, uid_number)
244:                 conn.unbind()
245:                 return True, f"User {username} created successfully"
246:             else:
247:                 error_msg = conn.result.get("description", "Unknown error")
248:                 logger.error("Failed to create LDAP user %s: %s", username, error_msg)
249:                 conn.unbind()
250:                 return False, f"Failed to create user: {error_msg}"
251:         except LDAPException as e:
252:             logger.error("LDAP error creating user %s: %s", username, e)
253:             return False, f"LDAP error: {e!s}"
254:         except Exception as e:
255:             logger.error("Unexpected error creating user %s: %s", username, e)
256:             return False, f"Error creating user: {e!s}"
257:     def update_user(
258:         self,
259:         username: str,
260:         password: Optional[str] = None,
261:         first_name: Optional[str] = None,
262:         last_name: Optional[str] = None,
263:         email: Optional[str] = None,
264:     ) -> tuple[bool, str]:
265:         """
266:         Update an existing user in LDAP.
267:         Args:
268:             username: The username (uid)
269:             password: New password (optional)
270:             first_name: New first name (optional)
271:             last_name: New last name (optional)
272:             email: New email address (optional)
273:         Returns:
274:             Tuple of (success: bool, message: str)
275:         """
276:         user_dn = self._get_user_dn(username)
277:         try:
278:             conn = self._get_admin_connection()
279:             # Check if user exists
280:             if not self.user_exists(username):
281:                 conn.unbind()
282:                 return False, f"User {username} does not exist in LDAP"
283:             # Build modifications
284:             modifications = {}
285:             if password is not None:
286:                 modifications["userPassword"] = [(MODIFY_REPLACE, [password])]
287:             if first_name is not None and last_name is not None:
288:                 modifications["cn"] = [(MODIFY_REPLACE, [f"{first_name} {last_name}"])]
289:                 modifications["givenName"] = [(MODIFY_REPLACE, [first_name])]
290:                 modifications["sn"] = [(MODIFY_REPLACE, [last_name])]
291:             elif first_name is not None:
292:                 current_sn = self.get_user_attribute(username, "sn") or ""
293:                 modifications["givenName"] = [(MODIFY_REPLACE, [first_name])]
294:                 modifications["cn"] = [(MODIFY_REPLACE, [f"{first_name} {current_sn}"])]
295:             elif last_name is not None:
296:                 current_given = self.get_user_attribute(username, "givenName") or ""
297:                 modifications["sn"] = [(MODIFY_REPLACE, [last_name])]
298:                 modifications["cn"] = [(MODIFY_REPLACE, [f"{current_given} {last_name}"])]
299:             if email is not None:
300:                 modifications["mail"] = [(MODIFY_REPLACE, [email])]
301:             if not modifications:
302:                 conn.unbind()
303:                 return True, "No changes to apply"
304:             # Apply modifications
305:             success = conn.modify(user_dn, modifications)
306:             if success:
307:                 logger.info("Updated LDAP user: %s", username)
308:                 conn.unbind()
309:                 return True, f"User {username} updated successfully"
310:             else:
311:                 error_msg = conn.result.get("description", "Unknown error")
312:                 logger.error("Failed to update LDAP user %s: %s", username, error_msg)
313:                 conn.unbind()
314:                 return False, f"Failed to update user: {error_msg}"
315:         except LDAPException as e:
316:             logger.error("LDAP error updating user %s: %s", username, e)
317:             return False, f"LDAP error: {e!s}"
318:         except Exception as e:
319:             logger.error("Unexpected error updating user %s: %s", username, e)
320:             return False, f"Error updating user: {e!s}"
321:     def create_or_update_user(
322:         self,
323:         username: str,
324:         password: str,
325:         first_name: str,
326:         last_name: str,
327:         email: str,
328:     ) -> tuple[bool, str]:
329:         """
330:         Create a new user in LDAP or update if exists.
331:         Args:
332:             username: The username (uid)
333:             password: The user's password
334:             first_name: User's first name
335:             last_name: User's last name
336:             email: User's email address
337:         Returns:
338:             Tuple of (success: bool, message: str)
339:         """
340:         if self.user_exists(username):
341:             return self.update_user(
342:                 username=username,
343:                 password=password,
344:                 first_name=first_name,
345:                 last_name=last_name,
346:                 email=email,
347:             )
348:         else:
349:             return self.create_user(
350:                 username=username,
351:                 password=password,
352:                 first_name=first_name,
353:                 last_name=last_name,
354:                 email=email,
355:             )

383:     def is_admin(self, username: str) -> bool:
384:         """
385:         Check if a user is a member of the admin group.
386:         Args:
387:             username: The username to check
388:         Returns:
389:             True if user is an admin, False otherwise
390:         """
391:         try:
392:             conn = self._get_admin_connection()
393:             admin_group_dn = self.settings.ldap_admin_group_dn
394:             # Search for the admin group and check membership
395:             # Groups typically use 'member' or 'memberUid' attribute
396:             conn.search(
397:                 search_base=admin_group_dn,
398:                 search_filter="(objectClass=*)",
399:                 attributes=["member", "memberUid", "uniqueMember"],
400:             )
401:             if not conn.entries:
402:                 logger.debug("Admin group not found: %s", admin_group_dn)
403:                 conn.unbind()
404:                 return False
405:             entry = conn.entries[0]
406:             user_dn = self._get_user_dn(username)
407:             # Check different membership attribute types
408:             # member/uniqueMember uses full DN
409:             if hasattr(entry, "member") and entry.member.values:
410:                 if user_dn.lower() in [m.lower() for m in entry.member.values]:
411:                     conn.unbind()
412:                     return True
413:             if hasattr(entry, "uniqueMember") and entry.uniqueMember.values:
414:                 if user_dn.lower() in [m.lower() for m in entry.uniqueMember.values]:
415:                     conn.unbind()
416:                     return True
417:             # memberUid uses just the username
418:             if hasattr(entry, "memberUid") and entry.memberUid.values:
419:                 if username.lower() in [m.lower() for m in entry.memberUid.values]:
420:                     conn.unbind()
421:                     return True
422:             conn.unbind()
423:             return False
424:         except LDAPException as e:
425:             logger.error("LDAP error checking admin status for %s: %s", username, e)
426:             return False
427:         except Exception as e:
428:             logger.error("Unexpected error checking admin status for %s: %s", username, e)
429:             return False
430:     def _get_group_object_class(self, conn: Connection, group_dn: str) -> Optional[str]:
431:         """
432:         Determine the objectClass of a group to use the correct membership attribute.
433:         Returns: 'groupOfUniqueNames', 'groupOfNames', 'posixGroup', or None
434:         """
435:         try:
436:             conn.search(
437:                 search_base=group_dn,
438:                 search_filter="(objectClass=*)",
439:                 attributes=["objectClass"],
440:             )
441:             if conn.entries:
442:                 object_classes = [oc.lower() for oc in conn.entries[0].objectClass.values]
443:                 if "groupofuniquenames" in object_classes:
444:                     return "groupOfUniqueNames"
445:                 elif "groupofnames" in object_classes:
446:                     return "groupOfNames"
447:                 elif "posixgroup" in object_classes:
448:                     return "posixGroup"
449:         except Exception as e:
450:             logger.debug("Could not determine group objectClass: %s", e)
451:         return None
452:     def add_user_to_group(self, username: str, group_dn: str) -> tuple[bool, str]:
453:         """
454:         Add a user to an LDAP group.
455:         Args:
456:             username: The username to add
457:             group_dn: The DN of the group
458:         Returns:
459:             Tuple of (success: bool, message: str)
460:         """
461:         user_dn = self._get_user_dn(username)
462:         try:
463:             conn = self._get_admin_connection()
464:             # Determine group type to use correct membership attribute
465:             group_type = self._get_group_object_class(conn, group_dn)
466:             success = False
467:             if group_type == "groupOfUniqueNames":
468:                 # groupOfUniqueNames uses uniqueMember attribute
469:                 success = conn.modify(
470:                     group_dn,
471:                     {"uniqueMember": [(MODIFY_ADD, [user_dn])]}
472:                 )
473:             elif group_type == "groupOfNames":
474:                 # groupOfNames uses member attribute
475:                 success = conn.modify(
476:                     group_dn,
477:                     {"member": [(MODIFY_ADD, [user_dn])]}
478:                 )
479:             elif group_type == "posixGroup":
480:                 # posixGroup uses memberUid attribute (just username)
481:                 success = conn.modify(
482:                     group_dn,
483:                     {"memberUid": [(MODIFY_ADD, [username])]}
484:                 )
485:             else:
486:                 # Unknown group type, try uniqueMember first, then member, then memberUid
487:                 success = conn.modify(
488:                     group_dn,
489:                     {"uniqueMember": [(MODIFY_ADD, [user_dn])]}
490:                 )
491:                 if not success:
492:                     success = conn.modify(
493:                         group_dn,
494:                         {"member": [(MODIFY_ADD, [user_dn])]}
495:                     )
496:                 if not success:
497:                     success = conn.modify(
498:                         group_dn,
499:                         {"memberUid": [(MODIFY_ADD, [username])]}
500:                     )
501:             if success:
502:                 logger.info("Added user %s to group %s", username, group_dn)
503:                 conn.unbind()
504:                 return True, "User added to group successfully"
505:             else:
506:                 error_msg = conn.result.get("description", "Unknown error")
507:                 # Check if user is already a member (attribute or value exists)
508:                 if "already exists" in error_msg.lower() or "attribute or value exists" in error_msg.lower():
509:                     logger.info("User %s is already a member of group %s", username, group_dn)
510:                     conn.unbind()
511:                     return True, "User is already a member of the group"
512:                 logger.error("Failed to add %s to group: %s", username, error_msg)
513:                 conn.unbind()
514:                 return False, f"Failed to add to group: {error_msg}"
515:         except LDAPException as e:
516:             logger.error("LDAP error adding user to group: %s", e)
517:             return False, f"LDAP error: {e!s}"
518:         except Exception as e:
519:             logger.error("Unexpected error adding user to group: %s", e)
520:             return False, f"Error: {e!s}"
521:     def remove_user_from_group(self, username: str, group_dn: str) -> tuple[bool, str]:
522:         """
523:         Remove a user from an LDAP group.
524:         Args:
525:             username: The username to remove
526:             group_dn: The DN of the group
527:         Returns:
528:             Tuple of (success: bool, message: str)
529:         """
530:         user_dn = self._get_user_dn(username)
531:         try:
532:             conn = self._get_admin_connection()
533:             # Determine group type to use correct membership attribute
534:             group_type = self._get_group_object_class(conn, group_dn)
535:             success = False
536:             if group_type == "groupOfUniqueNames":
537:                 success = conn.modify(
538:                     group_dn,
539:                     {"uniqueMember": [(MODIFY_DELETE, [user_dn])]}
540:                 )
541:             elif group_type == "groupOfNames":
542:                 success = conn.modify(
543:                     group_dn,
544:                     {"member": [(MODIFY_DELETE, [user_dn])]}
545:                 )
546:             elif group_type == "posixGroup":
547:                 success = conn.modify(
548:                     group_dn,
549:                     {"memberUid": [(MODIFY_DELETE, [username])]}
550:                 )
551:             else:
552:                 # Unknown group type, try all
553:                 success = conn.modify(
554:                     group_dn,
555:                     {"uniqueMember": [(MODIFY_DELETE, [user_dn])]}
556:                 )
557:                 if not success:
558:                     success = conn.modify(
559:                         group_dn,
560:                         {"member": [(MODIFY_DELETE, [user_dn])]}
561:                     )
562:                 if not success:
563:                     success = conn.modify(
564:                         group_dn,
565:                         {"memberUid": [(MODIFY_DELETE, [username])]}
566:                     )
567:             if success:
568:                 logger.info("Removed user %s from group %s", username, group_dn)
569:                 conn.unbind()
570:                 return True, "User removed from group successfully"
571:             else:
572:                 error_msg = conn.result.get("description", "Unknown error")
573:                 logger.error("Failed to remove %s from group: %s", username, error_msg)
574:                 conn.unbind()
575:                 return False, f"Failed to remove from group: {error_msg}"
576:         except LDAPException as e:
577:             logger.error("LDAP error removing user from group: %s", e)
578:             return False, f"LDAP error: {e!s}"
579:         except Exception as e:
580:             logger.error("Unexpected error removing user from group: %s", e)
581:             return False, f"Error: {e!s}"
582:     def list_groups(self) -> list[dict]:
583:         """
584:         List all LDAP groups.
585:         Returns:
586:             List of group dictionaries with dn, name, description, and members
587:         """
588:         groups = []
589:         try:
590:             conn = self._get_admin_connection()
591:             # Search for all groups
592:             conn.search(
593:                 search_base=self._get_group_search_base(),
594:                 search_filter="(|(objectClass=groupOfNames)(objectClass=groupOfUniqueNames)(objectClass=posixGroup))",
595:                 attributes=["cn", "description", "member", "memberUid", "uniqueMember"],
596:             )
597:             for entry in conn.entries:
598:                 group_data = {
599:                     "dn": str(entry.entry_dn),
600:                     "name": entry.cn.value if hasattr(entry, "cn") else "",
601:                     "description": entry.description.value if hasattr(entry, "description") and entry.description.value else "",
602:                     "members": [],
603:                 }
604:                 # Get members from different attribute types
605:                 if hasattr(entry, "member") and entry.member.values:
606:                     group_data["members"].extend(entry.member.values)
607:                 if hasattr(entry, "uniqueMember") and entry.uniqueMember.values:
608:                     group_data["members"].extend(entry.uniqueMember.values)
609:                 if hasattr(entry, "memberUid") and entry.memberUid.values:
610:                     group_data["members"].extend(entry.memberUid.values)
611:                 groups.append(group_data)
612:             conn.unbind()
613:             logger.info("Listed %s LDAP groups", len(groups))
614:             return groups
615:         except LDAPException as e:
616:             logger.error("LDAP error listing groups: %s", e)
617:             return []
618:         except Exception as e:
619:             logger.error("Unexpected error listing groups: %s", e)
620:             return []
621:     def create_group(
622:         self,
623:         name: str,
624:         description: str = "",
625:     ) -> tuple[bool, str, Optional[str]]:
626:         """
627:         Create a new LDAP group.
628:         Args:
629:             name: The group name (cn)
630:             description: Group description
631:         Returns:
632:             Tuple of (success: bool, message: str, group_dn: Optional[str])
633:         """
634:         # Escape the group name before using it in a DN or as the cn attribute
635:         safe_name = escape_rdn(name)
636:         group_dn = self._get_group_dn(safe_name)
637:         try:
638:             conn = self._get_admin_connection()
639:             # Check if group already exists
640:             conn.search(
641:                 search_base=group_dn,
642:                 search_filter="(objectClass=*)",
643:                 attributes=["cn"],
644:             )
645:             if conn.entries:
646:                 conn.unbind()
647:                 return False, f"Group {name} already exists", None
648:             # Create group with groupOfNames objectClass
649:             # Note: groupOfNames requires at least one member, using admin as placeholder
650:             attributes = {
651:                 "objectClass": ["groupOfNames", "top"],
652:                 "cn": safe_name,
653:                 "description": description or f"Group: {name}",
654:                 "member": [self.settings.ldap_admin_dn],  # Required initial member
655:             }
656:             success = conn.add(group_dn, attributes=attributes)
657:             if success:
658:                 logger.info("Created LDAP group: %s", name)
659:                 conn.unbind()
660:                 return True, f"Group {name} created successfully", group_dn
661:             else:
662:                 error_msg = conn.result.get("description", "Unknown error")
663:                 logger.error("Failed to create LDAP group %s: %s", name, error_msg)
664:                 conn.unbind()
665:                 return False, f"Failed to create group: {error_msg}", None
666:         except LDAPException as e:
667:             logger.error("LDAP error creating group %s: %s", name, e)
668:             return False, f"LDAP error: {e!s}", None
669:         except Exception as e:
670:             logger.error("Unexpected error creating group %s: %s", name, e)
671:             return False, f"Error creating group: {e!s}", None

698:     def update_group(

727:                 conn.unbind()
728:                 return False, f"Failed to update group: {error_msg}"
729:         except LDAPException as e:
730:             logger.error("LDAP error updating group %s: %s", group_dn, e)
731:             return False, f"LDAP error: {e!s}"
732:         except Exception as e:

735:     def get_user_groups(self, username: str) -> list[dict]:
736:         """
737:         Get all groups a user belongs to.
738:         Args:
739:             username: The username to check
740:         Returns:
741:             List of group dictionaries with dn and name
742:         """

825:                     if conn.entries and hasattr(conn.entries[0], "mail"):

849:         Ensure required LDAP directory structure exists under the base DN.

888:             logger.error("Unexpected error ensuring directory structure: %s", e)

927:                         if parts:
928:                             uid = parts[0].split("=")[1] if "=" in parts[0] else ""
929:                             if uid:
930:                                 members.append(uid)
931:             conn.unbind()
932:             # Remove duplicates
933:             return list(set(members))

936:             return []
937:         except Exception as e:
938:             logger.error("Unexpected error getting group members for %s: %s", group_dn, e)
```

```bash
  1: #!/bin/bash

 12: unset AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY 2>/dev/null || true

173: #   role_arn: The ARN of the role to assume (required)
174: #   external_id: Optional external ID for cross-account role assumption
175: #   role_description: Optional description for logging (defaults to "role")
176: #   session_name_suffix: Optional suffix for session name (defaults to "destroy-application")
177: assume_aws_role() {
178:     local role_arn=$1
179:     local external_id=${2:-}
180:     local role_description=${3:-"role"}
181:     local session_name_suffix=${4:-"destroy-application"}
182:     if [ -z "$role_arn" ]; then
183:         print_error "Role ARN is required for assume_aws_role"
184:         return 1
185:     fi
186:     print_info "Assuming ${role_description}: $role_arn"
187:     print_info "Region: $AWS_REGION"
188:     # Assume the role
189:     local role_session_name="${session_name_suffix}-$(date +%s)"
190:     local assume_role_output
191:     # Assume role and capture output
192:     # Add external ID if provided
193:     if [ -n "$external_id" ]; then
194:         assume_role_output=$(aws sts assume-role \
195:             --role-arn "$role_arn" \
196:             --role-session-name "$role_session_name" \
197:             --external-id "$external_id" \
198:             --region "$AWS_REGION" 2>&1)
199:     else
200:         assume_role_output=$(aws sts assume-role \
201:             --role-arn "$role_arn" \
202:             --role-session-name "$role_session_name" \
203:             --region "$AWS_REGION" 2>&1)
204:     fi
205:     if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
206:         print_error "Failed to assume ${role_description}: $assume_role_output"
207:         return 1
208:     fi
209:     # Extract credentials from JSON output
210:     # Try using jq if available (more reliable), otherwise use sed/grep
211:     local access_key_id
212:     local secret_access_key
213:     local session_token
214:     if command -v jq &> /dev/null; then
215:         access_key_id=$(echo "$assume_role_output" | jq -r '.Credentials.AccessKeyId')
216:         secret_access_key=$(echo "$assume_role_output" | jq -r '.Credentials.SecretAccessKey')
217:         session_token=$(echo "$assume_role_output" | jq -r '.Credentials.SessionToken')
218:     else
219:         # Fallback: use sed for JSON parsing (works on both macOS and Linux)
220:         access_key_id=$(echo "$assume_role_output" | sed -n 's/.*"AccessKeyId"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
221:         secret_access_key=$(echo "$assume_role_output" | sed -n 's/.*"SecretAccessKey"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
222:         session_token=$(echo "$assume_role_output" | sed -n 's/.*"SessionToken"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
223:     fi
224:     if [ -z "$access_key_id" ] || [ -z "$secret_access_key" ] || [ -z "$session_token" ]; then
225:         print_error "Failed to extract credentials from assume-role output."
226:         print_error "Output was: $assume_role_output"
227:         return 1
228:     fi
229:     # Export credentials to environment variables
230:     export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="$access_key_id"
231:     export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="$secret_access_key"
232:     export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN="$session_token"
233:     print_success "Successfully assumed ${role_description}"
234:     # Verify the credentials work
235:     local caller_arn
236:     caller_arn=$(aws sts get-caller-identity --region "$AWS_REGION" --query 'Arn' --output text 2>&1)
237:     if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
238:         print_error "Failed to verify assumed role credentials: $caller_arn"
239:         return 1
240:     fi
241:     print_info "${role_description} identity: $caller_arn"
242:     return 0
243: }
244: # Warning about destructive operation
245: echo ""
246: print_warning "=========================================="
247: print_warning "  DESTRUCTIVE OPERATION WARNING"
248: print_warning "=========================================="
249: print_warning "This script will DESTROY all application"
250: print_warning "infrastructure in the selected region and environment."
251: print_warning ""
252: print_warning "This action CANNOT be undone!"
253: print_warning "=========================================="

259: fi

282: echo ""

490:     BACKEND_IMAGE_TAG="${BACKEND_IMAGE_TAG#\"}"; BACKEND_IMAGE_TAG="${BACKEND_IMAGE_TAG%\"}"

509:     if [ -n "$FRONTEND_IMAGE_TAG" ] && [ "$FRONTEND_IMAGE_TAG" != "tag:" ] && [ "$FRONTEND_IMAGE_TAG" != "latest" ]; then
510:         export TF_VAR_frontend_image_tag="$FRONTEND_IMAGE_TAG"
511:         print_success "Using frontend image tag: ${FRONTEND_IMAGE_TAG}"
512:     else
513:         export TF_VAR_frontend_image_tag=""

515:     fi
516: else
517:     export TF_VAR_frontend_image_tag=""

522: if ! assume_aws_role "$STATE_ROLE_ARN" "" "State Account role" "destroy-application"; then
523:     exit 1
524: fi

528: terraform plan -var-file="${VARIABLES_FILE}" -destroy -out terraform.tfplan
529: # Terraform apply (destroy)
530: print_warning "Applying destroy plan. This will DESTROY all application resources..."

534: print_info "All application resources in ${AWS_REGION} (${ENVIRONMENT}) have been destroyed."
```

```bash
  1: #!/bin/bash
  2: # Script to configure backend.hcl and variables.tfvars with user-selected region and environment
  3: # and run Terraform commands for application deployment

  5: set -euo pipefail

  7: SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
  8: cd "$SCRIPT_DIR"
  9: # Clean up any existing AWS credentials from environment to prevent conflicts
 10: # This ensures the script starts with a clean slate and uses the correct credentials

 12: unset AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY 2>/dev/null || true
 13: unset AWS_SESSION_TOKEN 2>/dev/null || true
 14: unset AWS_PROFILE 2>/dev/null || true

 17: GREEN='\033[0;32m'
 18: YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
 19: NC='\033[0m' # No Color

 23: VARIABLES_FILE="variables.tfvars"

 27: # Function to print colored messages

 30: }
 31: print_success() {
 32:     echo -e "${GREEN}SUCCESS:${NC} $1"
 33: }

 35:     echo -e "${YELLOW}INFO:${NC} $1"
 36: }
 37: print_warning() {
 38:     echo -e "${YELLOW}WARNING:${NC} $1"
 39: }

 42:     print_error "AWS CLI is not installed."
 43:     echo "Please install it from: https://aws.amazon.com/cli/"
 44:     exit 1

 48:     print_error "Terraform is not installed."

 51: fi

 71:     exit 1
 72: fi

 74: REPO_OWNER=$(gh repo view --json owner --jq '.owner.login' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
 75: REPO_NAME=$(gh repo view --json name --jq '.name' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
 76: if [ -z "$REPO_OWNER" ] || [ -z "$REPO_NAME" ]; then

 78:     echo "Please ensure you're in a git repository and have proper permissions."
 79:     exit 1

 82: # Function to get repository variable using GitHub CLI
 83: get_repo_variable() {

 85:     local value
 86:     value=$(gh variable list --repo "${REPO_OWNER}/${REPO_NAME}" --json name,value --jq ".[] | select(.name == \"${var_name}\") | .value" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
 87:     if [ -z "$value" ]; then
 88:         print_error "Repository variable '${var_name}' not found or not accessible."
 89:         return 1

 93: # Function to retrieve secret from AWS Secrets Manager
 94: get_aws_secret() {

110:         print_error "Error: $secret_json"

115:         print_error "Secret '${secret_name}' contains invalid JSON"
116:         return 1

118:     echo "$secret_json"
119: }
120: # Function to retrieve plain text secret from AWS Secrets Manager
121: get_aws_plaintext_secret() {
122:     local secret_name=$1
123:     local secret_value
124:     local exit_code
125:     # Retrieve secret from AWS Secrets Manager
126:     # Use AWS_REGION if set, otherwise default to us-east-1
127:     secret_value=$(aws secretsmanager get-secret-value \
128:         --secret-id "$secret_name" \
129:         --region "${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}" \
130:         --query SecretString \
131:         --output text 2>&1)
132:     # Capture exit code before checking
133:     exit_code=$?
134:     # Validate secret retrieval
135:     if [ $exit_code -ne 0 ]; then
136:         print_error "Failed to retrieve secret '${secret_name}' from AWS Secrets Manager"
137:         print_error "Error: $secret_value"
138:         return 1
139:     fi
140:     # Check if secret value is empty
141:     if [ -z "$secret_value" ]; then
142:         print_error "Secret '${secret_name}' is empty"
143:         return 1
144:     fi
145:     echo "$secret_value"
146: }
147: # Function to get key value from secret JSON
148: get_secret_key_value() {
149:     local secret_json=$1
150:     local key_name=$2
151:     local value
152:     # Validate JSON can be parsed
153:     if ! echo "$secret_json" | jq empty 2>/dev/null; then
154:         print_error "Invalid JSON provided to get_secret_key_value"
155:         return 1
156:     fi
157:     # Extract key value using jq
158:     value=$(echo "$secret_json" | jq -r ".[\"${key_name}\"]" 2>/dev/null)
159:     # Check if jq command succeeded
160:     if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
161:         print_error "Failed to parse JSON or extract key '${key_name}'"
162:         return 1
163:     fi
164:     # Check if key exists (jq returns "null" for non-existent keys)
165:     if [ "$value" = "null" ] || [ -z "$value" ]; then
166:         print_error "Key '${key_name}' not found in secret JSON or value is empty"
167:         return 1
168:     fi
169:     echo "$value"
170: }
171: # Function to assume an AWS IAM role and export credentials
172: # Usage: assume_aws_role <role_arn> [external_id] [role_description] [session_name_suffix]
173: #   role_arn: The ARN of the role to assume (required)
174: #   external_id: Optional external ID for cross-account role assumption
175: #   role_description: Optional description for logging (defaults to "role")
176: #   session_name_suffix: Optional suffix for session name (defaults to "setup-application")
177: assume_aws_role() {
178:     local role_arn=$1
179:     local external_id=${2:-}
180:     local role_description=${3:-"role"}
181:     local session_name_suffix=${4:-"setup-application"}
182:     if [ -z "$role_arn" ]; then
183:         print_error "Role ARN is required for assume_aws_role"
184:         return 1
185:     fi
186:     print_info "Assuming ${role_description}: $role_arn"
187:     print_info "Region: $AWS_REGION"
188:     # Assume the role
189:     local role_session_name="${session_name_suffix}-$(date +%s)"
190:     local assume_role_output
191:     # Assume role and capture output
192:     # Add external ID if provided
193:     if [ -n "$external_id" ]; then
194:         assume_role_output=$(aws sts assume-role \
195:             --role-arn "$role_arn" \
196:             --role-session-name "$role_session_name" \
197:             --external-id "$external_id" \
198:             --region "$AWS_REGION" 2>&1)
199:     else
200:         assume_role_output=$(aws sts assume-role \
201:             --role-arn "$role_arn" \
202:             --role-session-name "$role_session_name" \
203:             --region "$AWS_REGION" 2>&1)
204:     fi
205:     if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
206:         print_error "Failed to assume ${role_description}: $assume_role_output"
207:         return 1
208:     fi
209:     # Extract credentials from JSON output
210:     # Try using jq if available (more reliable), otherwise use sed/grep
211:     local access_key_id
212:     local secret_access_key
213:     local session_token
214:     if command -v jq &> /dev/null; then
215:         access_key_id=$(echo "$assume_role_output" | jq -r '.Credentials.AccessKeyId')
216:         secret_access_key=$(echo "$assume_role_output" | jq -r '.Credentials.SecretAccessKey')
217:         session_token=$(echo "$assume_role_output" | jq -r '.Credentials.SessionToken')
218:     else
219:         # Fallback: use sed for JSON parsing (works on both macOS and Linux)
220:         access_key_id=$(echo "$assume_role_output" | sed -n 's/.*"AccessKeyId"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
221:         secret_access_key=$(echo "$assume_role_output" | sed -n 's/.*"SecretAccessKey"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
222:         session_token=$(echo "$assume_role_output" | sed -n 's/.*"SessionToken"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
223:     fi
224:     if [ -z "$access_key_id" ] || [ -z "$secret_access_key" ] || [ -z "$session_token" ]; then
225:         print_error "Failed to extract credentials from assume-role output."
226:         print_error "Output was: $assume_role_output"
227:         return 1
228:     fi
229:     # Export credentials to environment variables
230:     export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="$access_key_id"
231:     export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="$secret_access_key"
232:     export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN="$session_token"
233:     print_success "Successfully assumed ${role_description}"
234:     # Verify the credentials work
235:     local caller_arn
236:     caller_arn=$(aws sts get-caller-identity --region "$AWS_REGION" --query 'Arn' --output text 2>&1)
237:     if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
238:         print_error "Failed to verify assumed role credentials: $caller_arn"
239:         return 1
240:     fi
241:     print_info "${role_description} identity: $caller_arn"
242:     return 0
243: }

346: # Extract OpenLDAP admin password from tf-vars secret (for backend LDAP bind / ldap-admin-secret)

353: # Export as environment variables for Terraform

416: # Function to check ArgoCD capability status from application_infra
417: check_argocd_status() {
418:     local infra_dir="../application_infra"
419:     local status_output
420:     local argocd_status
421:     # Check if application_infra directory exists
422:     if [ ! -d "$infra_dir" ]; then
423:         print_error "application_infra directory not found at $infra_dir"
424:         return 1
425:     fi
426:     # Check if backend.hcl exists in application_infra
427:     if [ ! -f "$infra_dir/backend.hcl" ]; then
428:         print_error "backend.hcl not found in application_infra. Ensure infrastructure is deployed first."
429:         return 1
430:     fi
431:     # Change to application_infra directory
432:     pushd "$infra_dir" > /dev/null || return 1
433:     # Initialize terraform if needed (quiet mode)
434:     if [ ! -d ".terraform" ]; then
435:         print_info "Initializing application_infra terraform for status check..."
436:         terraform init -backend-config="backend.hcl" > /dev/null 2>&1 || {
437:             print_error "Failed to initialize application_infra terraform"
438:             popd > /dev/null
439:             return 1
440:         }
441:     fi
442:     # Select workspace
443:     terraform workspace select "${WORKSPACE_NAME}" > /dev/null 2>&1 || {
444:         print_error "Failed to select workspace ${WORKSPACE_NAME} in application_infra"
445:         popd > /dev/null
446:         return 1
447:     }
448:     # Get ArgoCD capability status output
449:     status_output=$(terraform output -raw argocd_capability_status 2>/dev/null)
450:     local exit_code=$?
451:     # Return to original directory
452:     popd > /dev/null
453:     # Fail if status output command failed
454:     if [ $exit_code -ne 0 ]; then
455:         print_error "ArgoCD capability status not available (failed to retrieve from application_infra)"
456:         print_error "Please ensure ArgoCD capability is deployed in application_infra before deploying applications."
457:         return 1
458:     fi
459:     # Trim whitespace
460:     argocd_status=$(echo "$status_output" | tr -d '[:space:]')
461:     # Fail if status is empty or null
462:     if [ -z "$argocd_status" ] || [ "$argocd_status" = "null" ]; then
463:         print_error "ArgoCD capability status is not set or is null"
464:         print_error "Please ensure ArgoCD capability is deployed and active in application_infra before deploying applications."
465:         return 1
466:     fi
467:     print_info "ArgoCD capability status: ${argocd_status}"
468:     # Fail if status is not ACTIVE
469:     if [ "$argocd_status" != "ACTIVE" ]; then
470:         print_error "ArgoCD capability status is '${argocd_status}', but expected 'ACTIVE'"
471:         print_error "Please ensure ArgoCD capability is fully deployed and active before deploying applications."
472:         return 1
473:     fi
474:     print_success "ArgoCD capability is ACTIVE - proceeding with deployment"
475:     return 0
476: }

481:     if git pull --rebase origin main; then

502:     BACKEND_IMAGE_TAG=$(grep -E '^[[:space:]]*tag:' "$BACKEND_VALUES_FILE" | head -n 1 | sed -E 's/.*tag:[[:space:]]*//' | tr -d '\r')
503:     BACKEND_IMAGE_TAG="${BACKEND_IMAGE_TAG#\"}"; BACKEND_IMAGE_TAG="${BACKEND_IMAGE_TAG%\"}"

505:     if [ -z "$BACKEND_IMAGE_TAG" ] || [ "$BACKEND_IMAGE_TAG" = "tag:" ] || [ "$BACKEND_IMAGE_TAG" = "latest" ]; then
506:         print_error "Could not extract valid backend image tag from ${BACKEND_VALUES_FILE}"
507:         print_error "Found tag: '${BACKEND_IMAGE_TAG:-<empty>}'"

509:         exit 1

525:     FRONTEND_IMAGE_TAG=$(grep -E '^[[:space:]]*tag:' "$FRONTEND_VALUES_FILE" | head -n 1 | sed -E 's/.*tag:[[:space:]]*//' | tr -d '\r')
526:     FRONTEND_IMAGE_TAG="${FRONTEND_IMAGE_TAG#\"}"; FRONTEND_IMAGE_TAG="${FRONTEND_IMAGE_TAG%\"}"

528:     if [ -z "$FRONTEND_IMAGE_TAG" ] || [ "$FRONTEND_IMAGE_TAG" = "tag:" ] || [ "$FRONTEND_IMAGE_TAG" = "latest" ]; then
529:         print_error "Could not extract valid frontend image tag from ${FRONTEND_VALUES_FILE}"
530:         print_error "Found tag: '${FRONTEND_IMAGE_TAG:-<empty>}'"
531:         print_error "Run the 'Frontend Build and Push' workflow first. It will update the values.yaml with the correct tag."
532:         exit 1
533:     else

536:     fi

538: echo ""

541: if ! check_argocd_status; then

548: terraform init -backend-config="${BACKEND_FILE}"

551: terraform workspace select "${WORKSPACE_NAME}" 2>/dev/null || terraform workspace new "${WORKSPACE_NAME}"

558: print_info "Setting Kubernetes environment variables..."
559: if [ ! -f "../scripts/set-k8s-env.sh" ]; then

572: source ../scripts/set-k8s-env.sh
573: # Restore directory - critical to ensure terraform runs against correct state
574: cd "$SAVED_PWD"
575: if [ -z "$KUBERNETES_MASTER" ]; then

581: print_info "  - KUBE_CONFIG_PATH: ${KUBE_CONFIG_PATH}"
582: # Export as TF_VAR_ environment variables for Terraform

584: export TF_VAR_kube_config_path="$KUBE_CONFIG_PATH"
585: print_info "  - TF_VAR_kubernetes_master: ${TF_VAR_kubernetes_master}"
586: print_info "  - TF_VAR_kube_config_path: ${TF_VAR_kube_config_path}"
587: echo ""
588: # Assume State Account role for backend operations
589: if ! assume_aws_role "$STATE_ROLE_ARN" "" "State Account role" "setup-application"; then
590:     exit 1
591: fi
592: echo ""
593: # Terraform plan
594: print_info "Running terraform plan..."
595: terraform plan -var-file="${VARIABLES_FILE}" -out terraform.tfplan
596: # Terraform apply
597: print_info "Running terraform apply..."
598: terraform apply -auto-approve terraform.tfplan
599: echo ""
600: print_success "Script completed successfully!"
601: echo ""
602: print_warning "IMPORTANT: If you haven't already done so, you must run the 'Backend Build and Push' and 'Frontend Build and Push' workflows BEFORE ArgoCD can sync the applications."
603: print_info "These workflows should be run BEFORE running this script to ensure container images are available in ECR."
604: print_info "If ArgoCD Applications are enabled, ArgoCD will automatically detect the git changes from the build workflows and sync the deployments."
605: print_info "Without these images, ArgoCD cannot sync the 2FA applications and manual Helm deployment will fail."
606: echo ""
```
