 305:                     <p><strong>Note on State File Isolation:</strong> The <code>APPLICATION_INFRA_PREFIX</code> and <code>APPLICATION_PREFIX</code> variables ensure that infrastructure and application state files are stored separately in the same S3 bucket, preventing state conflicts. Both directories use the same <code>BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME</code> but different keys for complete isolation.</p>
 306:                 </li>
 307:                 <li><strong>For Local Deployment:</strong> GitHub CLI (<code>gh</code>), AWS CLI, Terraform, kubectl, and <code>jq</code> installed and configured</li>
 308:                 <li><strong>For Local Deployment:</strong> <strong>Docker</strong> must be installed and running for ECR image mirroring. The <code>scripts/mirror-images-to-ecr.sh</code> script requires Docker to pull images from Docker Hub and push them to ECR. This step is automatically executed by <code>setup-application-infra.sh</code> before Terraform operations.</li>
 309:                 <li><strong>For Local Deployment:</strong> AWS Secrets Manager configured with <code>github-role</code>, <code>tf-vars</code>, and <code>external-id</code> secrets (see <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/docs/auxiliary/reference/SECRETS_REQUIREMENTS.md">Secrets Requirements</a>)</li>
 310:             </ul>
 311:             <p><strong>For detailed prerequisites and setup:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/README.md#prerequisites">Prerequisites</a> | <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/README.md#secrets-configuration">Secrets Configuration</a> | <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/docs/auxiliary/reference/SECRETS_REQUIREMENTS.md">Secrets Requirements</a></p>
 312:         </div>
 313:         <h3 id="deployment-options">Deployment Options</h3>
 314:         <div class="deployment-options">
 315:             <div class="deployment-card">
 316:                 <h4 id="local-deployment">Local Deployment</h4>
 317:                 <p><strong>Recommended for:</strong> Development, testing, and local experimentation</p>
 318:                 <h5 id="local-step-1">Step 1: Deploy Terraform Backend State Infrastructure</h5>
 319:                 <p>Deploy the S3 bucket for Terraform state storage:</p>
 320:                 <pre><code>cd tf_backend_state
 321: ./set-state.sh</code></pre>
 322:                 <p>You can also run from the repo root: <code>./tf_backend_state/set-state.sh</code>. Both <code>set-state.sh</code> and <code>get-state.sh</code> change to their script directory before running, so Terraform and variables are found either way.</p>
 323:                 <p><strong>What the script does:</strong></p>
 324:                 <ul>
 325:                     <li>Retrieves <code>AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN</code> from AWS Secrets Manager</li>
 326:                     <li>Retrieves <code>AWS_REGION</code> and <code>BACKEND_PREFIX</code> from GitHub repository variables</li>
 327:                     <li>Assumes the IAM role and verifies credentials</li>
 328:                     <li>Checks if infrastructure exists (via <code>BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME</code> variable)</li>
 329:                     <li>If new: Runs Terraform init, validate, plan, and apply to create S3 bucket</li>
 330:                     <li>If exists: Downloads existing state file from S3 (if available)</li>
 331:                     <li>Saves/updates <code>BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME</code> to GitHub repository variables</li>
 332:                     <li>Uploads state file to S3</li>
 333:                 </ul>
 334:                 <p><strong>Alternative:</strong> Use <code>./get-state.sh</code> (or <code>./tf_backend_state/get-state.sh</code> from repo root) to download existing state file without provisioning</p>
 335:                 <h5 id="local-step-2">Step 2: Deploy Backend Infrastructure</h5>
 336:                 <p>Deploy VPC, EKS cluster, VPC endpoints, IRSA, and ECR:</p>
 337:                 <pre><code>cd backend_infra
 338: ./setup-backend.sh</code></pre>
 339:                 <p><strong>What the script does:</strong></p>
 340:                 <ul>
 341:                     <li>Prompts for AWS region (us-east-1 or us-east-2) and environment (prod or dev)</li>
 342:                     <li>Retrieves repository variables from GitHub (<code>BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME</code>, <code>BACKEND_PREFIX</code>)</li>
 343:                     <li>Retrieves role ARNs from AWS Secrets Manager (<code>github-role</code> secret)</li>
 344:                     <li>Retrieves ExternalId from AWS Secrets Manager (<code>external-id</code> secret)</li>
 345:                     <li>Assumes State Account role for backend operations</li>
 346:                     <li>Generates <code>backend.hcl</code> from template (if it doesn't exist)</li>
 347:                     <li>Updates <code>variables.tfvars</code> with selected region, environment, deployment account role ARN, and ExternalId</li>
 348:                     <li>Runs Terraform init, workspace select/new, validate, plan, and apply</li>
 349:                     <li><strong>Automatically saves ECR repository name</strong> to GitHub repository variable <code>ECR_REPOSITORY_NAME</code> (eliminates manual configuration)</li>
 350:                 </ul>
 351:                 <h5 id="local-step-3">Step 3: Deploy Application Infrastructure</h5>
 352:                 <p>Deploy OpenLDAP stack, ALB, Route53 records, ArgoCD Capability, and StorageClass:</p>
 353:                 <pre><code>cd application_infra
 354: ./setup-application-infra.sh</code></pre>
 355:                 <p><strong>What the script does:</strong></p>
 356:                 <ul>
 357:                     <li>Prompts for AWS region (us-east-1 or us-east-2) and environment (prod or dev)</li>
 358:                     <li>Retrieves repository variables from GitHub (<code>BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME</code>, <code>APPLICATION_INFRA_PREFIX</code>)</li>
 359:                     <li><strong>Mirrors Docker images to ECR</strong> (runs <code>scripts/mirror-images-to-ecr.sh</code> before Terraform operations):
 360:                         <ul>
 361:                             <li>Checks if images exist in ECR before mirroring (skips if already present)</li>
 362:                             <li>Pulls images from Docker Hub: <code>bitnami/redis:latest</code>, <code>bitnami/postgresql:latest</code>, <code>osixia/openldap:1.5.0</code></li>
 363:                             <li>Pushes images to ECR with tags: <code>redis-latest</code>, <code>postgresql-latest</code>, <code>openldap-1.5.0</code> (prevents Docker Hub rate limiting by using ECR images)</li>
 364:                             <li>Uses <code>BACKEND_PREFIX</code> (or <code>backend_infra/backend.hcl</code>) and <code>TERRAFORM_WORKSPACE</code> (or <code>AWS_REGION</code>+<code>ENVIRONMENT</code>) for correct backend_infra state path</li>
 365:                             <li>Uses State Account credentials to fetch ECR URL from backend_infra state</li>
 366:                             <li>Assumes Deployment Account role for ECR operations (with ExternalId)</li>
 367:                             <li>Authenticates Docker to ECR automatically</li>
 368:                             <li>Cleans up local images after pushing to save disk space</li>
 369:                             <li>Requires Docker to be installed and running</li>
 370:                             <li>Requires <code>jq</code> for JSON parsing (with fallback to sed for compatibility)</li>
 371:                         </ul>
 372:                     </li>
 373:                     <li>Retrieves role ARNs and ExternalId from AWS Secrets Manager</li>
 374:                     <li>Retrieves OpenLDAP password secrets from AWS Secrets Manager (<code>tf-vars</code> secret) and exports as environment variables:
 375:                         <ul>
 376:                             <li><code>TF_VAR_openldap_admin_password</code></li>
 377:                             <li><code>TF_VAR_openldap_config_password</code></li>
 378:                         </ul>
 379:                         Terraform writes these to a Kubernetes secret with keys
 380:                         <code>LDAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD</code> and
 381:                         <code>LDAP_CONFIG_PASSWORD</code> (osixia/openldap image).
 382:                     </li>
 383:                     <li>Assumes State Account role for backend operations</li>
 384:                     <li>Exports <code>TERRAFORM_WORKSPACE</code> before sourcing <code>scripts/set-k8s-env.sh</code> so the correct backend_infra state is read</li>
 385:                     <li>Generates <code>backend.hcl</code> from template using <code>APPLICATION_INFRA_PREFIX</code> for state file key (if it doesn't exist)</li>
 386:                     <li>Updates <code>variables.tfvars</code> with selected values</li>
 387:                     <li>Sets Kubernetes environment variables using <code>scripts/set-k8s-env.sh</code> (uses <code>BACKEND_PREFIX</code> and <code>TERRAFORM_WORKSPACE</code>; restores original directory after sourcing)</li>
 388:                     <li>Runs Terraform init, workspace select/new, validate, plan, and apply</li>
 389:                 </ul>
 390:                 <h5 id="local-step-4">Step 4: Build Container Images (Required Before Application Deployment)</h5>
 391:                 <p><strong>Important:</strong> Before deploying the application in Step 5, you <strong>must</strong> run both the <strong>03 - Backend Build and Push</strong> (<code>03-backend_build_push.yaml</code>) and <strong>03 - Frontend Build and Push</strong> (<code>03-frontend_build_push.yaml</code>) workflows to build and push the container images to ECR. These images are required for ArgoCD to sync the applications or for manual Helm deployment.</p>
 392:                 <p><strong>Why both are required:</strong></p>
 393:                 <ul>
 394:                     <li>Without the backend image, ArgoCD cannot sync the backend application (image pull fails)</li>
 395:                     <li>Without the frontend image, ArgoCD cannot sync the frontend application (image pull fails)</li>
 396:                     <li>Both container images do not exist in ECR until you run the build workflows</li>
 397:                     <li>Without these images, ArgoCD cannot sync the 2FA applications and manual Helm deployment will fail</li>
 398:                 </ul>
 399:                 <p><strong>Build and push both images using GitHub Actions:</strong></p>
 400:                 <ol>
 401:                     <li><strong>Build and push backend image:</strong>
 402:                         <ul>
 403:                             <li>Go to GitHub → Actions → "03 - Backend Build and Push" (<code>03-backend_build_push.yaml</code>)</li>
 404:                             <li>Click "Run workflow"</li>
 405:                             <li>Select environment (prod or dev)</li>
 406:                             <li>Click "Run workflow"</li>
 407:                             <li>Wait for the workflow to complete</li>
 408:                         </ul>
 409:                     </li>
 410:                     <li><strong>Build and push frontend image:</strong>
 411:                         <ul>
 412:                             <li>Go to GitHub → Actions → "03 - Frontend Build and Push" (<code>03-frontend_build_push.yaml</code>)</li>
 413:                             <li>Click "Run workflow"</li>
 414:                             <li>Select environment (prod or dev)</li>
 415:                             <li>Click "Run workflow"</li>
 416:                             <li>Wait for the workflow to complete</li>
 417:                         </ul>
 418:                     </li>
 419:                 </ol>
 420:                 <p><strong>Note:</strong> These workflows can be run in parallel since they modify different files. They will automatically handle git conflicts if both run simultaneously.</p>
 421:                 <h5 id="local-step-5">Step 5: Deploy Application</h5>
 422:                 <p>Deploy PostgreSQL, Redis, SES, SNS, ArgoCD Applications, and 2FA application (backend/frontend):</p>
 423:                 <pre><code>cd application
 424: ./setup-application.sh</code></pre>
 425:                 <p><strong>What the script does:</strong></p>
 426:                 <ul>
 427:                     <li>Prompts for AWS region (us-east-1 or us-east-2) and environment (prod or dev)</li>
 428:                     <li>Retrieves repository variables from GitHub (<code>BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME</code>, <code>APPLICATION_PREFIX</code>)</li>
 429:                     <li>Retrieves role ARNs and ExternalId from AWS Secrets Manager</li>
 430:                     <li>Retrieves password secrets from AWS Secrets Manager (<code>tf-vars</code>) and exports as environment variables:
 431:                         <ul>
 432:                             <li><code>TF_VAR_postgresql_database_password</code></li>
 433:                             <li><code>TF_VAR_redis_password</code></li>
 434:                             <li><code>TF_VAR_openldap_admin_password</code> (for backend ldap-admin-secret and optional admin-seed Job)</li>
 435:                             <li>Optional: <code>TF_VAR_admin_seed_*</code> (when <code>ADMIN_SEED_*</code> keys are present in <code>tf-vars</code>; enables first admin user seed)</li>
 436:                         </ul>
 437:                     </li>
 438:                     <li>Assumes State Account role for backend operations</li>
 439:                     <li>Generates <code>backend.hcl</code> from template using <code>APPLICATION_PREFIX</code> for state file key (if it doesn't exist)</li>
 440:                     <li>Updates <code>variables.tfvars</code> with selected values</li>
 441:                     <li>Extracts backend and frontend image tags from Helm values (<code>backend/helm/ldap-2fa-backend/values.yaml</code>, <code>frontend/helm/ldap-2fa-frontend/values.yaml</code>) and sets <code>TF_VAR_backend_image_tag</code> and <code>TF_VAR_frontend_image_tag</code> (defaults to <code>latest</code> if missing)</li>
 442:                     <li>Exports <code>TERRAFORM_WORKSPACE</code>, sources <code>scripts/set-k8s-env.sh</code>, then restores current directory so Terraform runs in <code>application/</code></li>
 443:                     <li><strong>Validates ArgoCD capability status</strong> - Ensures ArgoCD capability is "ACTIVE" before proceeding (prevents deployment failures)</li>
 444:                     <li>Runs Terraform init, workspace select/new, validate, plan, and apply</li>
 445:                     <li>References infrastructure outputs from <code>application_infra</code> remote state (including LDAP host, base DN, admin DN—used by the admin-seed Job and not hardcoded)</li>
 446:                 </ul>
 447:                 <p><strong>Note:</strong> Application components require infrastructure to be deployed first (Steps 1-3 completed). The script automatically validates that the ArgoCD capability status is "ACTIVE" before proceeding with deployment. If the capability is not ACTIVE, deployment will fail with a clear error message. Backend and frontend image tags are read from Helm values (updated by the build workflows); the build workflows push only the computed tag (no <code>:latest</code>).</p>
 448:                 <p><strong>First admin seed (optional):</strong> If you set all <code>ADMIN_SEED_*</code> keys in <code>tf-vars</code> (or GitHub Secrets), Terraform creates a one-time Job that seeds the first admin user with the same username/password as the LDAP admin, email/phone pre-verified, and membership in the LDAP admins group. See <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/docs/auxiliary/reference/SECRETS_REQUIREMENTS.md">Secrets Requirements</a> and <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/application/README.md">Application README</a>.</p>
 449:                 <p><strong>Deploying 2FA Applications (Backend and Frontend):</strong></p>
 450:                 <p>The 2FA application backend and frontend can be deployed via ArgoCD Applications (if enabled in <code>variables.tfvars</code>) or manually using Helm charts. For manual deployment instructions, see <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/docs/auxiliary/application/deployment/DEPLOY_2FA_APPS.md">Deploying the 2FA Application</a>.</p>
 451:                 <p><strong>After Step 5:</strong> If ArgoCD Applications are enabled, ArgoCD will automatically detect the git changes (from the build workflows in Step 4) and sync the deployments. The container images are already in ECR, so ArgoCD can successfully pull and deploy them.</p>
 452:                 <h5 id="local-step-6">Manual Deployment of 2FA Applications (Optional)</h5>
 453:                 <p><strong>Prerequisites:</strong> Infrastructure must be deployed (Steps 1-3 completed). Required tools: <code>kubectl</code> configured to access your EKS cluster, <code>helm</code> (v3.x), <code>aws</code> CLI, and optionally <code>docker</code> for manual builds.</p>
 454:                 <p><strong>Overview:</strong> The deployment process involves building and pushing Docker images, gathering configuration values, creating namespace, deploying backend and frontend Helm charts, and verifying deployment.</p>
 455:                 <p><strong>4.1: Build and Push Docker Images</strong></p>
 456:                 <p>You have two options for building and pushing images:</p>
 457:                 <p><strong>Option A: Using GitHub Actions (Recommended)</strong></p>
 458:                 <ol>
 459:                     <li><strong>Build and push backend image:</strong>
 460:                         <ul>
 461:                             <li>Go to GitHub → Actions → "03 - Backend Build and Push" (<code>03-backend_build_push.yaml</code>)</li>
 462:                             <li>Click "Run workflow"</li>
 463:                             <li>Select environment (prod or dev)</li>
 464:                             <li>Click "Run workflow"</li>
 465:                             <li>Wait for the workflow to complete</li>
 466:                             <li>Note the image tag from the workflow output (format: <code>ldap-2fa-backend-&lt;commit-sha&gt;-&lt;run-id&gt;</code>; unique per run to avoid ECR tag conflicts)</li>
 467:                         </ul>
 468:                     </li>
 469:                     <li><strong>Build and push frontend image:</strong>
 470:                         <ul>
 471:                             <li>Go to GitHub → Actions → "03 - Frontend Build and Push" (<code>03-frontend_build_push.yaml</code>)</li>
 472:                             <li>Click "Run workflow"</li>
 473:                             <li>Select environment (prod or dev)</li>
 474:                             <li>Click "Run workflow"</li>
 475:                             <li>Wait for the workflow to complete</li>
 476:                             <li>Note the image tag from the workflow output (format: <code>ldap-2fa-frontend-&lt;commit-sha&gt;-&lt;run-id&gt;</code>; unique per run to avoid ECR tag conflicts)</li>
 477:                         </ul>
 478:                     </li>
 479:                 </ol>
 480:                 <p>The GitHub Actions workflows automatically build Docker images, push to ECR, update Helm values.yaml files with new image tags, and commit changes to the repository.</p>
 481:                 <p><strong>Option B: Manual Build and Push</strong></p>
 482:                 <pre><code># Set variables
 483: export AWS_REGION="us-east-1"
 484: export ECR_REPO_NAME="talo-tf-us-east-1-docker-images-prod"  # Adjust based on your setup
 485: export AWS_ACCOUNT_ID="944880695150"  # Your deployment account ID
 486: # Get ECR login
 487: aws ecr get-login-password --region ${AWS_REGION} | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin ${AWS_ACCOUNT_ID}.dkr.ecr.${AWS_REGION}.amazonaws.com
 488: # Build and push backend
 489: cd application/backend
 490: docker build -t ${AWS_ACCOUNT_ID}.dkr.ecr.${AWS_REGION}.amazonaws.com/${ECR_REPO_NAME}:ldap-2fa-backend-$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) .
 491: docker push ${AWS_ACCOUNT_ID}.dkr.ecr.${AWS_REGION}.amazonaws.com/${ECR_REPO_NAME}:ldap-2fa-backend-$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
 492: # Build and push frontend
 493: cd ../frontend
 494: docker build -t ${AWS_ACCOUNT_ID}.dkr.ecr.${AWS_REGION}.amazonaws.com/${ECR_REPO_NAME}:ldap-2fa-frontend-$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) .
 495: docker push ${AWS_ACCOUNT_ID}.dkr.ecr.${AWS_REGION}.amazonaws.com/${ECR_REPO_NAME}:ldap-2fa-frontend-$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)</code></pre>
 496:                 <p><strong>5.2: Gather Required Configuration Values</strong></p>
 497:                 <p>Get the required values from Terraform outputs. <strong>Note:</strong> <code>ecr_url</code> comes from <code>backend_infra</code>; <code>route53_domain_name</code> comes from <code>application_infra</code>; most other values from <code>application</code>.</p>
 498:                 <pre><code># ECR URL (from backend_infra)
 499: cd backend_infra
 500: ECR_URL=$(terraform output -raw ecr_url 2>/dev/null || echo "")
 501: if [ -z "$ECR_URL" ]; then
 502:   echo "ECR URL not found. Make sure backend_infra has been deployed."
 503:   exit 1
 504: fi
 505: # Domain name (from application_infra)
 506: cd ../application_infra
 507: DOMAIN_NAME=$(terraform output -raw route53_domain_name)
 508: # All other values (from application)
 509: cd ../application
 510: INGRESS_CLASS=$(terraform output -raw alb_ingress_class_name)
 511: ALB_NAME=$(terraform output -raw alb_load_balancer_name 2>/dev/null || echo "")
 512: HOSTNAME="app.${DOMAIN_NAME}"
 513: echo "ECR URL: ${ECR_URL}"
 514: echo "Domain: ${DOMAIN_NAME}"
 515: echo "IngressClass: ${INGRESS_CLASS}"
 516: echo "ALB Name: ${ALB_NAME}"
 517: echo "Hostname: ${HOSTNAME}"
 518: BACKEND_TAG="ldap-2fa-backend-$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"  # Or use tag from GitHub Actions
 519: FRONTEND_TAG="ldap-2fa-frontend-$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"  # Or use tag from GitHub Actions
 520: SES_ROLE_ARN=$(terraform output -raw ses_iam_role_arn 2>/dev/null || echo "")
 521: SNS_ROLE_ARN=$(terraform output -raw sns_iam_role_arn 2>/dev/null || echo "")
 522: POSTGRES_HOST=$(terraform output -raw postgresql_host)
 523: REDIS_HOST=$(terraform output -raw redis_host)
 524: REDIS_PORT=$(terraform output -raw redis_port)
 525: SES_SENDER_EMAIL=$(terraform output -raw ses_sender_email)
 526: SMS_SENDER_ID=$(terraform output -raw sms_sender_id 2>/dev/null || echo "2FA")</code></pre>
 527:                 <p><strong>5.3: Create Namespace</strong></p>
 528:                 <pre><code>kubectl create namespace 2fa-app</code></pre>
 529:                 <p><strong>5.4: Deploy Backend Application</strong></p>
 530:                 <p>Create a values file for the backend deployment:</p>
 531:                 <pre><code>cat > /tmp/backend-values.yaml &lt;&lt;EOF
 532: # Image configuration
 533: image:
 534:   repository: "${ECR_URL}"
 535:   tag: "${BACKEND_TAG}"
 536: # Ingress configuration
 537: ingress:
 538:   enabled: true
 539:   className: "${INGRESS_CLASS}"
 540:   annotations:
 541:     alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/load-balancer-name: "${ALB_NAME}"
 542:   hosts:
 543:     - host: "${HOSTNAME}"
 544:       paths:
 545:         - path: /api
 546:           pathType: Prefix
 547: # Service account with IRSA annotation
 548: serviceAccount:
 549:   annotations:
 550:     eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: "${SES_ROLE_ARN}"  # Use SES role (includes SNS if enabled)
 551: # LDAP configuration (when deploying via Terraform/ArgoCD, LDAP host/base DN/admin DN come from application_infra outputs; adjust for manual deployment)
 552: ldap:
 553:   host: "openldap-stack-ha.ldap.svc.cluster.local"
 554:   port: 389
 555:   baseDn: "dc=ldap,dc=talorlik,dc=internal"
 556:   adminDn: "cn=admin,dc=ldap,dc=talorlik,dc=internal"
 557: # Database configuration
 558: database:
 559:   url: "postgresql+asyncpg://ldap2fa:CHANGE_ME@${POSTGRES_HOST}:5432/ldap2fa"
 560:   externalSecret:
 561:     enabled: true
 562:     secretName: "postgresql-secret"
 563:     passwordKey: "password"
 564: # Email configuration
 565: email:
 566:   enabled: true
 567:   senderEmail: "${SES_SENDER_EMAIL}"
 568:   appUrl: "https://${HOSTNAME}"
 569: # SMS configuration (if enabled; direct SMS - no topic)
 570: sms:
 571:   enabled: true  # Set to false if SMS 2FA is not enabled
 572:   awsRegion: "${REGION}"
 573:   senderId: "${SMS_SENDER_ID}"
 574: # Redis configuration (if SMS is enabled)
 575: redis:
 576:   enabled: true  # Set to false if SMS 2FA is not enabled
 577:   host: "${REDIS_HOST}"
 578:   port: ${REDIS_PORT}
 579:   existingSecret:
 580:     enabled: true
 581:     name: "redis-secret"
 582:     key: "redis-password"
 583: EOF</code></pre>
 584:                 <p>Deploy the backend:</p>
 585:                 <pre><code>cd application/backend/helm
 586: helm upgrade --install ldap-2fa-backend ldap-2fa-backend \
 587:   --namespace 2fa-app \
 588:   --create-namespace \
 589:   --values /tmp/backend-values.yaml \
 590:                   --wait \
 591:                   --timeout 10m</code></pre>
 592:                 <p><strong>5.5: Deploy Frontend Application</strong></p>
 593:                 <p>Create a values file for the frontend deployment:</p>
 594:                 <pre><code>cat > /tmp/frontend-values.yaml &lt;&lt;EOF
 595: # Image configuration
 596: image:
 597:   repository: "${ECR_URL}"
 598:   tag: "${FRONTEND_TAG}"
 599: # Ingress configuration
 600: ingress:
 601:   enabled: true
 602:   className: "${INGRESS_CLASS}"
 603:   annotations:
 604:     alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/load-balancer-name: "${ALB_NAME}"
 605:   hosts:
 606:     - host: "${HOSTNAME}"
 607:       paths:
 608:         - path: /
 609:           pathType: Prefix
 610: EOF</code></pre>
 611:                 <p>Deploy the frontend:</p>
 612:                 <pre><code>cd application/frontend/helm
 613: helm upgrade --install ldap-2fa-frontend ldap-2fa-frontend \
 614:   --namespace 2fa-app \
 615:   --create-namespace \
 616:   --values /tmp/frontend-values.yaml \
 617:   --wait \
 618:   --timeout 10m</code></pre>
 619:                 <p><strong>5.6: Verify Deployment</strong></p>
 620:                 <pre><code># Check pods
 621: kubectl get pods -n 2fa-app
 622: # Check services
 623: kubectl get svc -n 2fa-app
 624: # Check ingress
 625: kubectl get ingress -n 2fa-app
 626: # Check backend logs
 627: kubectl logs -n 2fa-app -l app=ldap-2fa-backend --tail=50
 628: # Check frontend logs
 629: kubectl logs -n 2fa-app -l app=ldap-2fa-frontend --tail=50
 630: # Test backend health endpoint
 631: kubectl run -it --rm test-backend --image=curlimages/curl --restart=Never -- \
 632:   curl -k https://${HOSTNAME}/api/healthz
 633: # Check ALB target health
 634: ALB_ARN=$(aws elbv2 describe-load-balancers --region ${REGION} --query "LoadBalancers[?LoadBalancerName=='${ALB_NAME}'].LoadBalancerArn" --output text)
 635: TARGET_GROUP_ARN=$(aws elbv2 describe-target-groups --region ${REGION} --load-balancer-arn ${ALB_ARN} --query "TargetGroups[?contains(TargetGroupName, 'backend')].TargetGroupArn" --output text | head -1)
 636: aws elbv2 describe-target-health --region ${REGION} --target-group-arn ${TARGET_GROUP_ARN}</code></pre>
 637:                 <p><strong>5.7: Access the Application</strong></p>
 638:                 <p>Once deployed, access the application at:</p>
 639:                 <ul>
 640:                     <li><strong>Frontend:</strong> <code>https://${HOSTNAME}</code> (e.g., <code>https://app.talorlik.com</code>)</li>
 641:                     <li><strong>Backend API:</strong> <code>https://${HOSTNAME}/api</code> (e.g., <code>https://app.talorlik.com/api</code>)</li>
 642:                     <li><strong>API Documentation:</strong> <code>https://${HOSTNAME}/api/docs</code> (Swagger UI)</li>
 643:                 </ul>
 644:                 <p><strong>5.8: Updating Deployments</strong></p>
 645:                 <p>To update the applications after code changes:</p>
 646:                 <ol>
 647:                     <li><strong>Rebuild and push images</strong> (via GitHub Actions or manually)</li>
 648:                     <li><strong>Update Helm values</strong> with new image tags</li>
 649:                     <li><strong>Upgrade Helm releases:</strong>
 650:                         <pre><code># Update backend
 651: helm upgrade ldap-2fa-backend application/backend/helm/ldap-2fa-backend \
 652:   --namespace 2fa-app \
 653:   --set image.tag="${NEW_BACKEND_TAG}" \
 654:   --reuse-values
 655: # Update frontend
 656: helm upgrade ldap-2fa-frontend application/frontend/helm/ldap-2fa-frontend \
 657:   --namespace 2fa-app \
 658:   --set image.tag="${NEW_FRONTEND_TAG}" \
 659:                   --reuse-values</code></pre>
 660:                     </li>
 661:                 </ol>
 662:                 <p><strong>5.9: Alternative: Enable ArgoCD Applications</strong></p>
 663:                 <p>If you prefer GitOps deployment via ArgoCD:</p>
 664:                 <ol>
 665:                     <li><strong>Enable ArgoCD applications</strong> in <code>variables.tfvars</code>:
 666:                         <pre><code>enable_argocd_apps = true</code></pre>
 667:                     </li>
 668:                     <li><strong>Configure sync policy</strong> (optional):
 669:                         <pre><code>argocd_app_sync_policy_automated = true
 670: argocd_app_sync_policy_prune     = true
 671: argocd_app_sync_policy_self_heal = true</code></pre>
 672:                     </li>
 673:                     <li><strong>Apply Terraform changes:</strong>
 674:                         <pre><code>cd application
 675: terraform apply</code></pre>
 676:                     </li>
 677:                     <li><strong>ArgoCD will automatically deploy</strong> the applications from Git</li>
 678:                 </ol>
 679:                 <p><strong>For detailed deployment instructions:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/docs/auxiliary/application/deployment/DEPLOY_2FA_APPS.md">Deploying the 2FA Application</a></p>
 680:                 <p><strong>For backend and frontend documentation:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/application/backend/README.md">Backend API Documentation</a> | <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/application/frontend/README.md">Frontend Application Documentation</a></p>
 681:                 <h5 id="local-destroy">Destroying Infrastructure (Local)</h5>
 682:                 <p><strong>⚠️ Warning:</strong> Destroy operations are permanent and cannot be undone. Always destroy in reverse order: Application → Application Infrastructure → Backend Infrastructure → State.</p>
 683:                 <ol>
 684:                     <li><strong>Destroy Application:</strong>
 685:                         <pre><code>cd application
 686: ./destroy-application.sh</code></pre>
 687:                         <p>The script retrieves PostgreSQL, Redis, OpenLDAP admin, and optional admin-seed secrets from AWS Secrets Manager (<code>tf-vars</code>) so Terraform can destroy ldap-admin-secret and admin-seed resources. It will prompt for region and environment, then require confirmation ('yes', then 'DESTROY').</p>
 688:                     </li>
 689:                     <li><strong>Destroy Application Infrastructure:</strong>
 690:                         <pre><code>cd application_infra
 691: ./destroy-application-infra.sh</code></pre>
 692:                         <p>Script will prompt for region and environment, then require confirmation ('yes', then 'DESTROY')</p>
 693:                     </li>
 694:                     <li><strong>Destroy Backend Infrastructure:</strong>
 695:                         <pre><code>cd backend_infra
 696: ./destroy-backend.sh</code></pre>
 697:                         <p>Script will prompt for region and environment, then require confirmation ('yes', then 'DESTROY')</p>
 698:                     </li>
 699:                     <li><strong>Destroy State Backend (if needed):</strong>
 700:                         <pre><code>cd tf_backend_state
 701: ./get-state.sh  # Download state file first (or ./tf_backend_state/get-state.sh from repo root)
 702: terraform plan -var-file="variables.tfvars" -destroy -out terraform.tfplan
 703: terraform apply -auto-approve terraform.tfplan</code></pre>
 704:                     </li>
 705:                 </ol>
 706:                 <p><strong>For detailed local setup instructions:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/README.md#method-2-local-development">Local Development Setup</a> | <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/tf_backend_state/README.md#option-2-local-execution">Terraform Backend State Local Execution</a></p>
 707:             </div>
 708:             <div class="deployment-card">
 709:                 <h4 id="github-actions-deployment">GitHub Actions Deployment</h4>
 710:                 <p><strong>Recommended for:</strong> Production deployments, CI/CD pipelines, automated workflows</p>
 711:                 <h5 id="github-step-1">Step 1: Deploy Terraform Backend State Infrastructure</h5>
 712:                 <ol>
 713:                     <li>Go to GitHub → <strong>Actions</strong> tab</li>
 714:                     <li>Select <strong>"00 - TF Backend State Provisioning"</strong> workflow (<code>00-tfstate_infra_provisioning.yaml</code>)</li>
 715:                     <li>Click <strong>"Run workflow"</strong> → <strong>"Run workflow"</strong></li>
 716:                     <li>Monitor the workflow execution</li>
 717:                 </ol>
 718:                 <p><strong>What the workflow does:</strong></p>
 719:                 <ul>
 720:                     <li>Uses <code>AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN</code> secret for OIDC authentication</li>
 721:                     <li>Defaults <code>AWS_REGION</code> to <code>us-east-1</code> when the repository variable is not set</li>
 722:                     <li>Validates Terraform configuration</li>
 723:                     <li>Creates S3 bucket with versioning and encryption</li>
 724:                     <li>Saves bucket name as <code>BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME</code> repository variable</li>
 725:                     <li>Uploads state file to S3</li>
 726:                 </ul>
 727:                 <h5 id="github-step-2">Step 2: Deploy Backend Infrastructure</h5>
 728:                 <ol>
 729:                     <li>Go to GitHub → <strong>Actions</strong> tab</li>
 730:                     <li>Select <strong>"01 - Backend Infra Provisioning"</strong> workflow (<code>01-backend_infra_provisioning.yaml</code>)</li>
 731:                     <li>Click <strong>"Run workflow"</strong></li>
 732:                     <li>Select <strong>region</strong> (us-east-1: N. Virginia or us-east-2: Ohio)</li>
 733:                     <li>Select <strong>environment</strong> (prod or dev)</li>
 734:                     <li>Click <strong>"Run workflow"</strong></li>
 735:                     <li>Monitor the workflow execution</li>
 736:                 </ol>
 737:                 <p><strong>What the workflow does:</strong></p>
 738:                 <ul>
 739:                     <li>Uses <code>AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN</code> for backend state operations</li>
 740:                     <li>Uses environment-specific deployment account role ARN (<code>AWS_PRODUCTION_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN</code> or <code>AWS_DEVELOPMENT_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN</code>)</li>
 741:                     <li>Uses <code>AWS_ASSUME_EXTERNAL_ID</code> for cross-account role assumption</li>
 742:                     <li>Runs Terraform operations to deploy VPC, EKS, VPC endpoints, IRSA, and ECR</li>
 743:                     <li><strong>Automatically saves ECR repository name</strong> to GitHub repository variable <code>ECR_REPOSITORY_NAME</code> (eliminates manual configuration)</li>
 744:                 </ul>
 745:                 <h5 id="github-step-3">Step 3: Deploy Application Infrastructure</h5>
 746:                 <ol>
 747:                     <li>Go to GitHub → <strong>Actions</strong> tab</li>
 748:                     <li>Select <strong>"02 - Application Infra Provisioning"</strong> workflow (<code>02-application_infra_provisioning.yaml</code>)</li>
 749:                     <li>Click <strong>"Run workflow"</strong></li>
 750:                     <li>Select <strong>region</strong> (us-east-1: N. Virginia or us-east-2: Ohio)</li>
 751:                     <li>Select <strong>environment</strong> (prod or dev)</li>
 752:                     <li>Click <strong>"Run workflow"</strong></li>
 753:                     <li>Monitor the workflow execution</li>
 754:                 </ol>
 755:                 <p><strong>What the workflow does:</strong></p>
 756:                 <ul>
 757:                     <li>Uses <code>AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN</code> for backend state operations</li>
 758:                     <li>Uses environment-specific deployment account role ARN</li>
 759:                     <li>Uses <code>AWS_ASSUME_EXTERNAL_ID</code> for cross-account role assumption</li>
 760:                     <li>Exports <code>TERRAFORM_WORKSPACE</code> and <code>BACKEND_PREFIX</code> for <code>set-k8s-env.sh</code> and state path consistency</li>
 761:                     <li>Retrieves repository variables (<code>BACKEND_BUCKET_NAME</code>, <code>APPLICATION_INFRA_PREFIX</code>) for backend state configuration</li>
 762:                     <li>Creates <code>backend.hcl</code> from template using <code>APPLICATION_INFRA_PREFIX</code> for state file key</li>
 763:                     <li>Retrieves OpenLDAP password secrets from GitHub repository secrets</li>
 764:                     <li>Runs Terraform operations to deploy OpenLDAP stack, ALB, Route53 records (for phpldapadmin and ltb-passwd), ArgoCD Capability, and StorageClass</li>
 765:                 </ul>
 766:                 <h5 id="github-step-4">Step 4: Build Container Images (Required Before Application Deployment)</h5>
 767:                 <ol>
 768:                     <li>Go to GitHub → <strong>Actions</strong> tab</li>
 769:                     <li>Run <strong>"03 - Backend Build and Push"</strong> workflow (<code>03-backend_build_push.yaml</code>):
 770:                         <ul>
 771:                             <li>Select the workflow</li>
 772:                             <li>Click <strong>"Run workflow"</strong></li>
 773:                             <li>Select environment (prod or dev)</li>
 774:                             <li>Click <strong>"Run workflow"</strong></li>
 775:                         </ul>
 776:                     </li>
 777:                     <li>Run <strong>"03 - Frontend Build and Push"</strong> workflow (<code>03-frontend_build_push.yaml</code>):
 778:                         <ul>
 779:                             <li>Select the workflow</li>
 780:                             <li>Click <strong>"Run workflow"</strong></li>
 781:                             <li>Select environment (prod or dev)</li>
 782:                             <li>Click <strong>"Run workflow"</strong></li>
 783:                         </ul>
 784:                     </li>
 785:                 </ol>
 786:                 <p><strong>What the workflows do:</strong></p>
 787:                 <p>Both workflows build Docker images, push them to ECR (only the computed image tag is pushed; no <code>:latest</code> tag), update Helm values.yaml files with new image tags, and commit changes to the repository. Application provisioning then reads these tags from Helm values. These workflows can be run in parallel since they modify different files.</p>
 788:                 <h5 id="github-step-5">Step 5: Deploy Application</h5>
 789:                 <ol>
 790:                     <li>Go to GitHub → <strong>Actions</strong> tab</li>
 791:                     <li>Select <strong>"04 - Application Provisioning"</strong> workflow (<code>04-application_provisioning.yaml</code>)</li>
 792:                     <li>Click <strong>"Run workflow"</strong></li>
 793:                     <li>Select <strong>region</strong> (us-east-1: N. Virginia or us-east-2: Ohio)</li>
 794:                     <li>Select <strong>environment</strong> (prod or dev)</li>
 795:                     <li>Click <strong>"Run workflow"</strong></li>
 796:                     <li>Monitor the workflow execution</li>
 797:                 </ol>
 798:                 <p><strong>What the workflow does:</strong></p>
 799:                 <ul>
 800:                     <li>Uses <code>AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN</code> for backend state operations</li>
 801:                     <li>Uses environment-specific deployment account role ARN</li>
 802:                     <li>Uses <code>AWS_ASSUME_EXTERNAL_ID</code> for cross-account role assumption</li>
 803:                     <li>Exports <code>TERRAFORM_WORKSPACE</code> and <code>BACKEND_PREFIX</code> for state path consistency</li>
 804:                     <li>Extracts backend and frontend image tags from Helm values and sets <code>TF_VAR_backend_image_tag</code> and <code>TF_VAR_frontend_image_tag</code> (so the correct images are deployed; no <code>:latest</code> dependency)</li>
 805:                     <li>Creates <code>backend_infra/backend.hcl</code> from template (needed for remote state access)</li>
 806:                     <li>Creates <code>application_infra/backend.hcl</code> from template (needed for ArgoCD status check and remote state access)</li>
 807:                     <li><strong>Validates ArgoCD capability status</strong> - Ensures ArgoCD capability is "ACTIVE" before proceeding (prevents deployment failures)</li>
 808:                     <li>Creates <code>backend.hcl</code> from template using <code>APPLICATION_PREFIX</code> for state file key</li>
 809:                     <li>Retrieves password secrets (PostgreSQL, Redis, OpenLDAP admin) from GitHub repository secrets</li>
 810:                     <li>Sets Kubernetes environment variables using <code>set-k8s-env.sh</code> (from application_infra)</li>
 811:                     <li>Runs Terraform operations to deploy PostgreSQL, Redis, SES, SNS, ArgoCD Applications, and Route53 record for 2FA app</li>
 812:                     <li>When optional <code>ADMIN_SEED_*</code> secrets are set, a one-time Job seeds the first admin user</li>
 813:                     <li>LDAP connection settings for the admin-seed Job are read from <code>application_infra</code> remote state (not hardcoded)</li>
 814:                 </ul>
 815:                 <h5 id="github-destroy">Destroying Infrastructure (GitHub Actions)</h5>
 816:                 <p><strong>⚠️ Warning:</strong> Destroy operations are permanent and cannot be undone. Always destroy in reverse order: Application → Application Infrastructure → Backend Infrastructure → State.</p>
 817:                 <p><strong>Confirmation required:</strong> Each destroy workflow requires you to type <strong>yes</strong> in the "Type 'yes' to confirm destruction" input when you run the workflow; otherwise the workflow will not proceed.</p>
 818:                 <ol>
 819:                     <li><strong>Destroy Application:</strong>
 820:                         <ul>
 821:                             <li>Go to GitHub → <strong>Actions</strong> tab</li>
 822:                             <li>Select <strong>"04 - Application Destroying"</strong> workflow (<code>04-application_destroying.yaml</code>)</li>
 823:                             <li>Click <strong>"Run workflow"</strong></li>
 824:                             <li>Type <strong>yes</strong> in the confirmation input</li>
 825:                             <li>Select environment (prod or dev) and region</li>
 826:                             <li>Click <strong>"Run workflow"</strong></li>
 827:                         </ul>
 828:                         <p><strong>What the workflow does:</strong></p>
 829:                         <ul>
 830:                             <li>Uses <code>AWS_STATE_ACCOUNT_ROLE_ARN</code> for backend state operations</li>
 831:                             <li>Uses environment-specific deployment account role ARN</li>
 832:                             <li>Uses <code>AWS_ASSUME_EXTERNAL_ID</code> for cross-account role assumption</li>
 833:                             <li>Exports <code>TERRAFORM_WORKSPACE</code> and <code>BACKEND_PREFIX</code> for state path consistency</li>
 834:                             <li>Creates <code>backend.hcl</code> from template using <code>APPLICATION_PREFIX</code> for state file key</li>
 835:                             <li>Creates <code>backend_infra/backend.hcl</code> from template (needed for remote state access)</li>
 836:                             <li>Creates <code>application_infra/backend.hcl</code> from template (needed for remote state access)</li>
 837:                             <li>Retrieves password secrets (PostgreSQL, Redis, OpenLDAP admin, and optional admin-seed) from GitHub repository secrets</li>
 838:                             <li>Sets Kubernetes environment variables using <code>set-k8s-env.sh</code> (from application_infra)</li>
 839:                             <li>Runs Terraform destroy operations to remove PostgreSQL, Redis, SES, SNS, ArgoCD Applications, and Route53 record for 2FA app</li>
 840:                         </ul>
 841:                     </li>
 842:                     <li><strong>Destroy Application Infrastructure:</strong>
 843:                         <ul>
 844:                             <li>Go to GitHub → <strong>Actions</strong> tab</li>
 845:                             <li>Select <strong>"02 - Application Infra Destroying"</strong> workflow (<code>02-application_infra_destroying.yaml</code>)</li>
 846:                             <li>Click <strong>"Run workflow"</strong></li>
 847:                             <li>Type <strong>yes</strong> in the confirmation input</li>
 848:                             <li>Select environment (prod or dev) and region</li>
 849:                             <li>Click <strong>"Run workflow"</strong></li>
 850:                         </ul>
 851:                     </li>
 852:                     <li><strong>Destroy Backend Infrastructure:</strong>
 853:                         <ul>
 854:                             <li>Go to GitHub → <strong>Actions</strong> tab</li>
 855:                             <li>Select <strong>"01 - Backend Infra Destroying"</strong> workflow (<code>01-backend_infra_destroying.yaml</code>)</li>
 856:                             <li>Click <strong>"Run workflow"</strong></li>
 857:                             <li>Type <strong>yes</strong> in the confirmation input</li>
 858:                             <li>Select environment (prod or dev) and region</li>
 859:                             <li>Click <strong>"Run workflow"</strong></li>
 860:                         </ul>
 861:                     </li>
 862:                     <li><strong>Destroy State Backend (if needed):</strong>
 863:                         <ul>
 864:                             <li>Go to GitHub → <strong>Actions</strong> tab</li>
 865:                             <li>Select <strong>"00 - TF Backend State Destroying"</strong> workflow (<code>00-tfstate_infra_destroying.yaml</code>)</li>
 866:                             <li>Click <strong>"Run workflow"</strong></li>
 867:                             <li>Type <strong>yes</strong> in the confirmation input</li>
 868:                             <li>Click <strong>"Run workflow"</strong></li>
 869:                         </ul>
 870:                     </li>
 871:                 </ol>
 872:                 <p><strong>For detailed GitHub Actions setup:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/README.md#github-repository-configuration">GitHub Repository Configuration</a> | <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/README.md#method-1-github-actions-cicd">GitHub Actions Deployment</a></p>
 873:             </div>
 874:         </div>
 875:         <h3 id="deployment-comparison">Deployment Comparison</h3>
 876:         <table>
 877:             <thead>
 878:                 <tr>
 879:                     <th>Feature</th>
 880:                     <th>Local Deployment</th>
 881:                     <th>GitHub Actions</th>
 882:                 </tr>
 883:             </thead>
 884:             <tbody>
 885:                 <tr>
 886:                     <td>Setup Complexity</td>
 887:                     <td>Medium (requires local tools)</td>
 888:                     <td>Low (web-based)</td>
 889:                 </tr>
 890:                 <tr>
 891:                     <td>Best For</td>
 892:                     <td>Development, testing</td>
 893:                     <td>Production, CI/CD</td>
 894:                 </tr>
 895:                 <tr>
 896:                     <td>Requires GitHub CLI</td>
 897:                     <td>Yes</td>
 898:                     <td>No</td>
 899:                 </tr>
 900:                 <tr>
 901:                     <td>Requires GitHub Secrets</td>
 902:                     <td>Optional (can use env vars)</td>
 903:                     <td>Required</td>
 904:                 </tr>
 905:                 <tr>
 906:                     <td>Automation Level</td>
 907:                     <td>Script-based</td>
 908:                     <td>Fully automated</td>
 909:                 </tr>
 910:             </tbody>
 911:         </table>
 912:         <h3 id="deployment-order">Deployment Order</h3>
 913:         <div class="card">
 914:             <p>The deployment follows a <strong>three-tier approach</strong> that must be executed in order. Each tier depends on the previous one:</p>
 915:             <ol>
 916:                 <li><strong>Deploy Terraform Backend State Infrastructure</strong>
 917:                     <ul>
 918:                         <li><strong>Purpose:</strong> Creates S3 bucket for storing Terraform state files</li>
 919:                         <li><strong>Components:</strong> S3 bucket with versioning, encryption, and file-based locking</li>
 920:                         <li><strong>Account:</strong> State Account (Account A)</li>
 921:                         <li><strong>Local:</strong> <code>cd tf_backend_state && ./set-state.sh</code> (or <code>./tf_backend_state/set-state.sh</code> from repo root; scripts change to their directory automatically)</li>
 922:                         <li><strong>GitHub Actions:</strong> "00 - TF Backend State Provisioning" (<code>00-tfstate_infra_provisioning.yaml</code>); defaults <code>AWS_REGION</code> to <code>us-east-1</code> when not set</li>
 923:                         <li><strong>See:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/tf_backend_state/README.md">Terraform Backend State README</a></li>
 924:                     </ul>
 925:                 </li>
 926:                 <li><strong>Deploy Backend Infrastructure</strong>
 927:                     <ul>
 928:                         <li><strong>Purpose:</strong> Creates foundational AWS infrastructure for Kubernetes workloads</li>
 929:                         <li><strong>Components:</strong> VPC with public/private subnets, EKS cluster (Auto Mode), VPC endpoints (SSM, STS, SNS), IRSA (OIDC provider), ECR repository</li>
 930:                         <li><strong>Account:</strong> Deployment Account (Account B)</li>
 931:                         <li><strong>Prerequisites:</strong> Terraform backend state must be deployed first</li>
 932:                         <li><strong>Local:</strong> <code>cd backend_infra && ./setup-backend.sh</code></li>
 933:                         <li><strong>GitHub Actions:</strong> "01 - Backend Infra Provisioning" (<code>01-backend_infra_provisioning.yaml</code>)</li>
 934:                         <li><strong>See:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/backend_infra/README.md">Backend Infrastructure README</a></li>
 935:                     </ul>
 936:                 </li>
 937:                 <li><strong>Deploy Application Infrastructure</strong>
 938:                     <ul>
 939:                         <li><strong>Purpose:</strong> Deploys LDAP stack, supporting services, ALB, Route53 records, and infrastructure for 2FA application on the EKS cluster</li>
 940:                         <li><strong>Components:</strong> OpenLDAP stack (HA), PhpLdapAdmin, LTB-passwd, ALB, Route53 records (for phpldapadmin and ltb-passwd), ArgoCD Capability (optional), StorageClass</li>
 941:                         <li><strong>Account:</strong> Deployment Account (Account B)</li>
 942:                         <li><strong>Prerequisites:</strong> Backend infrastructure (EKS cluster) must be deployed first</li>
 943:                         <li><strong>Additional Requirements:</strong> Route53 hosted zone (Account A) and ACM certificate (Account B) must exist
 944:                             <ul>
 945:                                 <li>Route53 hosted zone in State Account; ACM certificate in Deployment Account (ALB and cert must be in same account)</li>
 946:                                 <li>Automatically accessed via <code>state_account_role_arn</code> for Route53 (injected by scripts/workflows)</li>
 947:                                 <li>See <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/docs/auxiliary/application_infra/guides/CROSS_ACCOUNT_ACCESS.md">Cross-Account Access Documentation</a> for configuration details</li>
 948:                             </ul>
 949:                         </li>
 950:                         <li><strong>Local:</strong> <code>cd application_infra && ./setup-application-infra.sh</code></li>
 951:                         <li><strong>GitHub Actions:</strong> "02 - Application Infra Provisioning" (<code>02-application_infra_provisioning.yaml</code>)</li>
 952:                         <li><strong>See:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/application_infra/README.md">Application Infrastructure README</a> | <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/application/README.md">Application Deployment README</a></li>
 953:                     </ul>
 954:                 </li>
 955:                 <li><strong>Build Container Images</strong>
 956:                     <ul>
 957:                         <li><strong>Purpose:</strong> Build and push backend and frontend container images to ECR</li>
 958:                         <li><strong>Required:</strong> Must be completed <strong>BEFORE</strong> deploying the application</li>
 959:                         <li><strong>Workflows:</strong> "03 - Backend Build and Push" (<code>03-backend_build_push.yaml</code>) and "03 - Frontend Build and Push" (<code>03-frontend_build_push.yaml</code>) (can run in parallel)</li>
 960:                         <li><strong>Note:</strong> These workflows update Helm values.yaml files with new image tags and commit changes to git</li>
 961:                     </ul>
 962:                 </li>
 963:                 <li><strong>Deploy Application</strong>
 964:                     <ul>
 965:                         <li><strong>Purpose:</strong> Deploys the 2FA application components, including PostgreSQL, Redis, SES, SNS, ArgoCD Applications, and the 2FA application (backend/frontend)</li>
 966:                         <li><strong>Components:</strong> PostgreSQL (user registration data), Redis (SMS OTP and login challenge storage), AWS SES (email verification), AWS SNS (SMS 2FA), ArgoCD Applications (GitOps), Route53 record (for 2FA app), Backend application (Python FastAPI), Frontend application (HTML/JS/CSS + nginx)</li>
 967:                         <li><strong>Account:</strong> Deployment Account (Account B)</li>
 968:                         <li><strong>Prerequisites:</strong> Application infrastructure (Step 3) must be deployed first, including StorageClass, ArgoCD Capability, and ALB DNS name. <strong>Container images must be built and pushed to ECR before deployment</strong> (see Build Container Images step above).</li>
 969:                         <li><strong>Local:</strong> <code>cd application && ./setup-application.sh</code></li>
 970:                         <li><strong>GitHub Actions:</strong> "04 - Application Provisioning" (<code>04-application_provisioning.yaml</code>)</li>
 971:                         <li><strong>See:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/application/README.md">Application Deployment README</a> for complete deployment guide</li>
 972:                         <li><strong>Note:</strong> The 2FA application backend and frontend can be deployed via ArgoCD Applications (if enabled) or manually using Helm charts. See <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/docs/auxiliary/application/deployment/DEPLOY_2FA_APPS.md">Deploying the 2FA Application</a> for manual deployment instructions.</li>
 973:                     </ul>
 974:                 </li>
 975:             </ol>
 976:             <p><strong>Destroy Order:</strong> Always destroy in <strong>reverse order</strong>: Application → Application Infrastructure → Backend Infrastructure → State</p>
 977:             <p><strong>For detailed deployment information:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/README.md#deployment-methods">Deployment Methods</a> | <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/README.md#deployment-overview">Deployment Overview</a></p>
 978:         </div>
 979:     </section>
 980:     <!-- Architecture -->
 981:     <section id="architecture">
 982:         <h2>Architecture</h2>
 983:         <h3 id="multi-account-architecture">Multi-Account Architecture</h3>
 984:         <div class="card">
 985:             <p>This project uses a <strong>multi-account architecture</strong> for enhanced security. See the Prerequisites table above for a quick reference of what resides in each account.</p>
 986:             <ul>
 987:                 <li><strong>Account A (State Account)</strong>: Holds shared, centrally managed resources
 988:                     <ul>
 989:                         <li><strong>Terraform state</strong>: S3 bucket with versioning, encryption, and file-based locking</li>
 990:                         <li><strong>AWS Secrets Manager</strong>: Secrets <code>github-role</code>, <code>tf-vars</code>, <code>external-id</code> (role ARNs, passwords, ExternalId for local scripts)</li>
 991:                         <li><strong>Route53 Hosted Zone</strong>: Domain and DNS; CNAME records for ACM validation are created here</li>
 992:                         <li>GitHub Actions authenticates with Account A via OIDC for backend operations and Route53</li>
 993:                         <li>IAM-based access control (no access keys required)</li>
 994:                     </ul>
 995:                 </li>
 996:                 <li><strong>Account B (Deployment Account)</strong>: Holds infrastructure and applications
 997:                     <ul>
 998:                         <li>EKS cluster, VPC, ALB, ECR, application workloads</li>
 999:                         <li><strong>ACM Certificates</strong>: Requested and stored here (ALB and certificate must be in the same account); validated via CNAME records in Account A's Route53</li>
1000:                         <li>Separate roles for production and development environments (optional)</li>
1001:                         <li>Terraform provider assumes Account B role via cross-account role assumption</li>
1002:                     </ul>
1003:                 </li>
1004:             </ul>
1005:             <p><strong>For detailed architecture documentation:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/README.md#multi-account-architecture">Multi-Account Architecture</a> | <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/tf_backend_state/README.md">Terraform Backend State README</a></p>
1006:         </div>
1007:         <h3 id="how-it-works">How It Works</h3>
1008:         <div class="card">
1009:             <p>The multi-account architecture enables secure separation of concerns:</p>
1010:             <ol>
1011:                 <li><strong>GitHub Actions</strong> authenticates with Account A via OIDC (no access keys required) for Terraform backend access</li>
1012:                 <li><strong>Terraform backend</strong> uses Account A credentials to read/write state files in S3</li>
1013:                 <li><strong>Terraform AWS provider</strong> assumes Account B role (via <code>assume_role</code> with ExternalId) for resource deployment</li>
1014:                 <li><strong>Remote state</strong> data sources use Account A credentials to read state from Account A, enabling cross-tier dependencies</li>
1015:             </ol>
1016:             <p>This architecture ensures state files are isolated in a dedicated account while resource deployment uses separate credentials, providing enhanced security and better compliance capabilities.</p>
1017:         </div>
1018:         <h3 id="project-structure">Project Structure</h3>
1019:         <pre><code>ldap-2fa-on-k8s/
1020: ├── docs/auxiliary/   # Auxiliary documentation (reference, application, application_infra, troubleshooting)
1021: ├── tf_backend_state/      # Terraform state backend infrastructure (S3) - Account A
1022: ├── backend_infra/         # Core AWS infrastructure (VPC, EKS, VPC endpoints, IRSA) - Account B
1023: │   └── monitor-deployments.sh   # Backend-infra deployment monitoring
1024: ├── application_infra/      # Application infrastructure (OpenLDAP, ALB, ArgoCD Capability) - Account B
1025: │   ├── helm/              # Helm values for OpenLDAP stack
1026: │   ├── monitor-deployments.sh   # Application-infra deployment monitoring
1027: │   └── modules/           # Infrastructure Terraform modules (ALB, ArgoCD Capability, etc.)
1028: ├── application/           # 2FA Application code and dependencies - Account B
1029: │   ├── backend/           # 2FA Backend (Python FastAPI)
1030: │   ├── frontend/          # 2FA Frontend (HTML/JS/CSS + nginx)
1031: │   ├── helm/              # Helm values for PostgreSQL and Redis
1032: │   ├── monitor-deployments.sh   # Application deployment monitoring
1033: │   └── modules/           # Application Terraform modules (PostgreSQL, Redis, SES, SNS, ArgoCD Apps)
1034: ├── scripts/               # Shared scripts (run from repo root or workflows)
1035: │   ├── assume-github-role.sh   # AWS role assumption (State/Dev/Prod)
1036: │   ├── get-eks-token.sh        # EKS auth token for Terraform exec plugin
1037: │   ├── mirror-images-to-ecr.sh # Mirror Docker Hub images to ECR
1038: │   └── set-k8s-env.sh         # Kubernetes env and kubeconfig setup
1039: └── .github/workflows/     # GitHub Actions workflows for CI/CD</code></pre>
1040:         <h4 id="scripts-directory">Shared Scripts (scripts/)</h4>
1041:         <div class="card">
1042:             <p>Shared automation scripts live in <code>scripts/</code>. Workflows and setup/destroy scripts reference them as <code>../scripts/...</code>.</p>
1043:             <ul>
1044:                 <li><strong>assume-github-role.sh</strong>: Assume AWS roles (State, Dev, Prod). Used by the ArgoCD module and for manual role switching.</li>
1045:                 <li><strong>get-eks-token.sh</strong>: Used by Terraform Kubernetes and Helm providers (exec plugin) to generate a fresh EKS token on every API call, avoiding token timeout during long operations (e.g. 20-minute Helm timeouts). Supports optional cross-account role assumption via <code>ASSUME_ROLE_ARN</code> and <code>ASSUME_EXTERNAL_ID</code>.</li>
1046:                 <li><strong>mirror-images-to-ecr.sh</strong>: Mirrors Docker Hub images (OpenLDAP, Redis, PostgreSQL, phpldapadmin, ltb-passwd) to ECR. Run by <code>setup-application-infra.sh</code> and the 02 - Application Infra Provisioning workflow (<code>02-application_infra_provisioning.yaml</code>).</li>
1047:                 <li><strong>set-k8s-env.sh</strong>: Sets Kubernetes environment variables and updates kubeconfig from backend_infra Terraform state. Sourced by application_infra and application setup/destroy scripts and workflows.</li>
1048:             </ul>
1049:         </div>
1050:         <h3 id="backend-infrastructure-components">Backend Infrastructure Components</h3>
1051:         <div class="card">
1052:             <ul>
1053:                 <li><strong>VPC</strong> with public and private subnets across multiple availability zones</li>
1054:                 <li><strong>EKS Cluster</strong> in Auto Mode with automatic node provisioning and CloudWatch logging</li>
1055:                 <li><strong>IRSA (IAM Roles for Service Accounts)</strong> for secure pod-to-AWS-service authentication via OIDC</li>
1056:                 <li><strong>VPC Endpoints</strong> for private AWS service access:
1057:                     <ul>
1058:                         <li>SSM endpoints for secure node access (Session Manager)</li>
1059:                         <li>STS endpoint for IRSA (IAM role assumption) - enabled by default</li>
1060:                         <li>SNS endpoint for SMS 2FA (optional, requires <code>enable_sns_endpoint = true</code>)</li>
1061:                     </ul>
1062:                 </li>
1063:                 <li><strong>ECR Repository</strong> for container image storage with lifecycle policies</li>
1064:                 <li><strong>Terraform State Backend</strong> using S3 with file-based locking for state concurrency control (migrated from DynamoDB for simplicity and cost efficiency)</li>
1065:             </ul>
1066:         </div>
1067:         <h3 id="application-infrastructure-components">Application Infrastructure Components</h3>
1068:         <div class="card">
1069:             <ul>
1070:                 <li><strong>OpenLDAP Stack HA</strong> deployed via vendored Helm chart
1071:                     (<code>application_infra/charts/openldap-stack-ha</code>, version 5.0.0,
1072:                     osixia/openldap:1.5.0; see <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/application_infra/OPENLDAP_CHANGELOG.md">OPENLDAP_CHANGELOG.md</a>) with:
1073:                     <ul>
1074:                         <li>OpenLDAP StatefulSet (3 replicas for high availability)</li>
1075:                         <li>PhpLdapAdmin web interface</li>
1076:                         <li>LTB-passwd self-service password management</li>
1077:                         <li>Credentials from Terraform-managed Kubernetes secret (keys
1078:                             <code>LDAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD</code> and
1079:                             <code>LDAP_CONFIG_PASSWORD</code> for osixia image)</li>
1080:                         <li>ACM certificate configured in IngressClassParams (ALB module), not passed to OpenLDAP module</li>
1081:                     </ul>
1082:                 </li>
1083:                 <li><strong>Application Load Balancer (ALB)</strong> via EKS Auto Mode:
1084:                     <ul>
1085:                         <li>Internet-facing ALB with HTTPS/TLS termination</li>
1086:                         <li>Single ALB handles multiple Ingresses via host-based routing</li>
1087:                         <li>Automatic provisioning via IngressClass and IngressClassParams</li>
1088:                         <li>Certificate ARN and group name configured at cluster level</li>
1089:                     </ul>
1090:                 </li>
1091:                 <li><strong>ArgoCD Capability</strong> (AWS EKS managed service) for GitOps infrastructure with AWS Identity Center</li>
1092:                 <li><strong>Network Policies</strong> for securing pod-to-pod communication with cross-namespace support</li>
1093:                 <li><strong>Route53 DNS</strong> records for phpldapadmin and ltb-passwd subdomains pointing to ALB</li>
1094:                 <li><strong>Persistent Storage</strong> using EBS-backed StorageClass (shared by all namespaces)</li>
1095:             </ul>
1096:             <p><strong>For detailed infrastructure documentation:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/application_infra/README.md">Application Infrastructure README</a></p>
1097:         </div>
1098:         <h3 id="application-components">Application Components</h3>
1099:         <div class="card">
1100:             <ul>
1101:                 <li><strong>2FA Application</strong> with LDAP authentication integration:
1102:                     <ul>
1103:                         <li>Python FastAPI backend with TOTP and SMS MFA support (<a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/application/backend/README.md">Backend Documentation</a>)</li>
1104:                         <li>Static HTML/JS/CSS frontend with modern UI (<a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/application/frontend/README.md">Frontend Documentation</a>)</li>
1105:                         <li>Single domain routing (<code>app.&lt;domain&gt;</code>) with path-based access</li>
1106:                         <li>Self-service user registration with email/phone verification</li>
1107:                         <li>Admin dashboard for user management and group operations</li>
1108:                         <li>Interactive API documentation (Swagger UI and ReDoc)</li>
1109:                     </ul>
1110:                 </li>
1111:                 <li><strong>PostgreSQL</strong> (Bitnami Helm chart) for user registration and verification token storage</li>
1112:                 <li><strong>Redis</strong> (Bitnami Helm chart) for SMS OTP and login challenge storage with TTL-based expiration (required)</li>
1113:                 <li><strong>AWS SES</strong> integration for email verification and notifications (IRSA-based)</li>
1114:                 <li><strong>AWS SNS</strong> integration for SMS-based 2FA verification (optional, requires VPC endpoint)</li>
1115:                 <li><strong>ArgoCD Applications</strong> for GitOps-driven backend and frontend deployments</li>
1116:                 <li><strong>Route53 DNS</strong> record for 2FA application subdomain (<code>app.&lt;domain&gt;</code>)</li>
1117:             </ul>
1118:             <p><strong>For detailed application documentation:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/application/README.md">Application Deployment README</a></p>
1119:             <p><strong>Note:</strong> Application components require infrastructure to be deployed first. See <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/application_infra/README.md">Application Infrastructure README</a> for infrastructure deployment.</p>
1120:         </div>
