1324:     <!-- Access Information -->
1325:     <section id="access">
1326:         <h2>Accessing the Services</h2>
1327:         <p>After deployment, the following services are available:</p>
1328:         <h3 id="2fa-application-access">2FA Application</h3>
1329:         <div class="card">
1330:             <p><strong>URL:</strong> <code>https://app.&lt;your-domain&gt;</code> (e.g., <code>https://app.example.com</code>)</p>
1331:             <p>The full-stack 2FA application provides:</p>
1332:             <ul>
1333:                 <li><strong>Sign Up Flow:</strong> 
1334:                     <ul>
1335:                         <li>User signs up → status set to <strong>PENDING</strong> (email and phone verification sent)</li>
1336:                         <li>User verifies email → <code>email_verified = true</code></li>
1337:                         <li>User verifies phone → <code>phone_verified = true</code></li>
1338:                         <li>When both verified → status automatically changes to <strong>COMPLETE</strong></li>
1339:                         <li>Admin activates user and assigns group(s) (required) → status changes to <strong>ACTIVE</strong></li>
1340:                     </ul>
1341:                     <strong>Note:</strong> MFA method selection does not occur during signup. Users cannot log in while in PENDING or COMPLETE states.
1342:                 </li>
1343:                 <li><strong>Login Flow (ACTIVE users only):</strong> 
1344:                     <ul>
1345:                         <li>Step 1 – username and password only (with optional "Remember me" for longer-lived session and "Forgot your password?" link)</li>
1346:                         <li>Step 2 – MFA screen where the user chooses Authenticator app or SMS and enters the 6-digit code (from the app or sent via SMS)</li>
1347:                         <li>Dual MFA methods (TOTP and SMS) are supported</li>
1348:                         <li>Users enroll in their preferred MFA method during login</li>
1349:                         <li>Once logged in, users can execute actions based on their assigned group(s) (e.g., Admin group members see admin dashboard, User group members have standard access)</li>
1350:                     </ul>
1351:                 </li>
1352:                 <li><strong>Forgot/Reset password:</strong> User requests a reset link by email; opening the link shows a set-new-password form; after submitting, they are redirected to login and sign in with the new password.</li>
1353:                 <li>Authenticator app: one-time setup with QR code (or manual secret); on subsequent logins the user just enters the code. User can choose Authenticator or SMS on every login.</li>
1354:                 <li>SMS: user requests a code on the MFA step; 6-digit OTP is sent via AWS SNS; user enters it in the same verification code field.</li>
1355:                 <li>User profile management with email change (verification link), phone change (SMS code), and password change</li>
1356:                 <li>Admin dashboard for user management, group CRUD operations, and approval workflows (visible to LDAP admin group members only)</li>
1357:                 <li><strong>First admin (optional):</strong> You can seed the first admin so they use the same username/password as the LDAP admin; set <code>ADMIN_SEED_*</code> secrets (see <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/docs/auxiliary/reference/SECRETS_REQUIREMENTS.md">Secrets Requirements</a>). The seeded admin does not have MFA pre-configured; they follow the same two-step login flow and set up Authenticator or use SMS like any other user.</li>
1358:                 <li><strong>Interactive API Documentation</strong> (always enabled):
1359:                     <ul>
1360:                         <li><code>/api/docs</code> - Swagger UI for interactive API exploration and testing</li>
1361:                         <li><code>/api/redoc</code> - ReDoc alternative API documentation interface</li>
1362:                         <li><code>/api/openapi.json</code> - OpenAPI schema in JSON format</li>
1363:                     </ul>
1364:                 </li>
1365:             </ul>
1366:             <p><strong>Documentation:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/application/backend/README.md">Backend API Documentation</a> | <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/application/frontend/README.md">Frontend Application Documentation</a></p>
1367:         </div>
1368:         <h3 id="phpldapadmin-access">PhpLdapAdmin</h3>
1369:         <div class="card">
1370:             <p><strong>URL:</strong> <code>https://phpldapadmin.&lt;your-domain&gt;</code> (e.g., <code>https://phpldapadmin.example.com</code>)</p>
1371:             <ul>
1372:                 <li>Web-based LDAP administration interface for managing directory entries</li>
1373:                 <li>Internet-facing access via Application Load Balancer with HTTPS/TLS termination</li>
1374:                 <li>Requires OpenLDAP admin credentials for authentication</li>
1375:             </ul>
1376:         </div>
1377:         <h3 id="ltb-passwd-access">LTB-passwd</h3>
1378:         <div class="card">
1379:             <p><strong>URL:</strong> <code>https://passwd.&lt;your-domain&gt;</code> (e.g., <code>https://passwd.example.com</code>)</p>
1380:             <ul>
1381:                 <li>Self-service password management UI for LDAP users</li>
1382:                 <li>Allows users to reset their LDAP passwords without administrator intervention</li>
1383:                 <li>Internet-facing access via Application Load Balancer with HTTPS/TLS termination</li>
1384:             </ul>
1385:         </div>
1386:         <h3 id="argocd-access">ArgoCD</h3>
1387:         <div class="card">
1388:             <p><strong>URL:</strong> Retrieved from Terraform output <code>argocd_server_url</code> (if ArgoCD is enabled)</p>
1389:             <ul>
1390:                 <li>AWS EKS managed ArgoCD service for GitOps deployments</li>
1391:                 <li>Declarative, Git-driven application deployments</li>
1392:                 <li>AWS Identity Center (SSO) authentication for secure access</li>
1393:                 <li>Automatic synchronization and self-healing capabilities</li>
1394:             </ul>
1395:         </div>
1396:         <h3 id="ldap-service-access">LDAP Service</h3>
1397:         <div class="card">
1398:             <p><strong>Access:</strong> Cluster-internal only (ClusterIP service)</p>
1399:             <ul>
1400:                 <li><strong>Port:</strong> 389 (LDAP), 636 (LDAPS)</li>
1401:                 <li><strong>Not Exposed:</strong> LDAP ports are not accessible outside the cluster</li>
1402:             </ul>
1403:         </div>
1404:         <h3 id="mfa-methods">MFA Methods</h3>
1405:         <table>
1406:             <thead>
1407:                 <tr>
1408:                     <th>Method</th>
1409:                     <th>Description</th>
1410:                     <th>Infrastructure Required</th>
1411:                 </tr>
1412:             </thead>
1413:             <tbody>
1414:                 <tr>
1415:                     <td><strong>TOTP</strong></td>
1416:                     <td>Time-based One-Time Password using authenticator apps (Google Authenticator, Authy, etc.)</td>
1417:                     <td>None (codes generated locally)</td>
1418:                 </tr>
1419:                 <tr>
1420:                     <td><strong>SMS</strong></td>
1421:                     <td>Verification codes sent via AWS SNS to user's phone</td>
1422:                     <td>SNS VPC endpoint, IRSA role</td>
1423:                 </tr>
1424:             </tbody>
1425:         </table>
1426:     </section>
1427:     <!-- Security Considerations -->
1428:     <section id="security">
1429:         <h2>Security Considerations</h2>
1430:         <h3 id="key-security-features">Key Security Features</h3>
1431:         <div class="card">
1432:             <p>This project implements defense-in-depth security across multiple layers:</p>
1433:             <ul>
1434:                 <li><strong>Secrets Management</strong>: Passwords managed via GitHub repository secrets (CI/CD) or AWS Secrets Manager (local) with automated retrieval—never committed to version control</li>
1435:                 <li><strong>IRSA (IAM Roles for Service Accounts)</strong>: Pods assume IAM roles via OIDC—no long-lived AWS credentials stored in containers or environment variables</li>
1436:                 <li><strong>VPC Endpoints</strong>: AWS service access (SSM, STS, SNS) routed through private endpoints—no public internet exposure for sensitive operations</li>
1437:                 <li><strong>TLS/HTTPS</strong>: TLS termination at ALB using ACM certificates; OpenLDAP uses auto-generated self-signed certificates (cert-manager module available but not used)</li>
1438:                 <li><strong>LDAP Security</strong>: ClusterIP service only (not exposed externally); cross-namespace access restricted to secure ports (443, 636, 8443)</li>
1439:                 <li><strong>Network Policies</strong>: Kubernetes Network Policies restrict pod-to-pod communication to encrypted ports with cross-namespace support for authorized services</li>
1440:                 <li><strong>Storage Encryption</strong>: EBS volumes encrypted by default; S3 state files encrypted with AES256 server-side encryption</li>
1441:                 <li><strong>Network Isolation</strong>: EKS nodes deployed in private subnets with no public IPs; access via SSM Session Manager</li>
1442:                 <li><strong>Multi-Account Architecture</strong>: State storage (Account A) isolated from resource deployment (Account B) for enhanced security and compliance</li>
1443:                 <li><strong>State Locking</strong>: S3 file-based locking prevents concurrent Terraform operations and state corruption</li>
1444:                 <li><strong>OIDC Authentication</strong>: GitHub Actions authenticates with AWS via OIDC—no access keys required</li>
1445:                 <li><strong>Cross-Account Security</strong>: ExternalId required for cross-account role assumption to prevent confused deputy attacks; bidirectional trust relationships</li>
1446:                 <li><strong>Helm Release Safety</strong>: Comprehensive Helm release attributes (atomic, force_update, replace, cleanup_on_fail, recreate_pods, wait, wait_for_jobs, upgrade_install) for safer deployments</li>
1447:                 <li><strong>ECR Image Support</strong>: All modules (OpenLDAP, PostgreSQL, Redis) use ECR images instead of Docker Hub to prevent rate limiting</li>
1448:                 <li><strong>Kubeconfig Auto-Update</strong>: Automatic kubeconfig updates prevent stale cluster endpoints and DNS lookup errors</li>
1449:             </ul>
1450:             <p><strong>For detailed security documentation:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/docs/auxiliary/application_infra/guides/SECURITY_IMPROVEMENTS.md">Security Improvements</a></p>
1451:         </div>
1452:     </section>
1453:     <!-- Contributing & Support -->
1454:     <section id="support">
1455:         <h2>Contributing & Support</h2>
1456:         <h3 id="operations-monitoring">Operations & Monitoring</h3>
1457:         <div class="card">
1458:             <h4>Deployment Monitoring Scripts</h4>
1459:             <p>There are three layer-specific monitoring scripts. Each prompts for region and environment, retrieves credentials from AWS Secrets Manager, updates kubeconfig, and produces a report suitable for agent investigation or manual review.</p>
1460:             <ul>
1461:                 <li><strong>backend_infra/monitor-deployments.sh</strong> - Backend infrastructure (EKS, VPC, ECR, etc.)</li>
1462:                 <li><strong>application_infra/monitor-deployments.sh</strong> - Application infrastructure (ArgoCD, OpenLDAP, ALB, ingress)</li>
1463:                 <li><strong>application/monitor-deployments.sh</strong> - Application layer (PostgreSQL, Redis, 2FA app, ingress, ALB)</li>
1464:             </ul>
1465:             <p>Each script provides interactive setup, cluster access, layer-specific health checks, and color-coded output. Exit code 0 = healthy, 1 = issues found. Prerequisites: <code>jq</code>, <code>kubectl</code>, <code>helm</code>, AWS CLI; optional: GitHub CLI (<code>gh</code>).</p>
1466:             <h5>Usage</h5>
1467:             <pre><code>cd backend_infra &amp;&amp; ./monitor-deployments.sh
1468: cd application_infra &amp;&amp; ./monitor-deployments.sh
1469: cd application &amp;&amp; ./monitor-deployments.sh</code></pre>
1470:             <h4>Role Assumption Script (scripts/assume-github-role.sh)</h4>
1471:             <p>The role assumption script is located in <code>scripts/assume-github-role.sh</code>. It allows you to switch between AWS account roles (State, Dev, Prod) when working in the terminal.</p>
1472:             <h5>Features</h5>
1473:             <ul>
1474:                 <li><strong>Account Role Switching:</strong> Switch between State Account, Development Account, or Production Account roles</li>
1475:                 <li><strong>Automatic Configuration:</strong> Retrieves role ARNs from AWS Secrets Manager (secret: <code>github-role</code>)</li>
1476:                 <li><strong>Credential Persistence:</strong> Credentials persist in your current shell when script is sourced</li>
1477:                 <li><strong>Clean Option:</strong> Remove all AWS credentials with <code>clean</code> option</li>
1478:                 <li><strong>Interactive Mode:</strong> Prompts for account selection if no argument is provided</li>
1479:             </ul>
1480:             <h5>Usage</h5>
1481:             <pre><code># Source the script (recommended - credentials persist in current shell)
1482: source ./scripts/assume-github-role.sh [state|dev|prod|clean]
1483: # Or use eval
1484: eval $(./scripts/assume-github-role.sh [state|dev|prod|clean])
1485: # Interactive mode (prompts for account selection)
1486: source ./scripts/assume-github-role.sh</code></pre>
1487:             <h5>Options</h5>
1488:             <ul>
1489:                 <li><code>state</code> - Assume State Account role (for backend state operations)</li>
1490:                 <li><code>dev</code> - Assume Development Account role</li>
1491:                 <li><code>prod</code> - Assume Production Account role</li>
1492:                 <li><code>clean</code> - Remove all AWS credentials from environment</li>
1493:                 <li>No argument - Interactive prompt for account selection</li>
1494:             </ul>
1495:             <p><strong>Note:</strong> The script must be <strong>sourced</strong> for credentials to persist. Use <code>source ./scripts/assume-github-role.sh [option]</code> or <code>eval $(./scripts/assume-github-role.sh [option])</code>.</p>
1496:             <p><strong>For detailed documentation:</strong> See <a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/README.md#operations--monitoring">Operations &amp; Monitoring</a> in the main README.</p>
1497:         </div>
1498:         <h3 id="troubleshooting">Troubleshooting</h3>
1499:         <div class="card">
1500:             <p><strong><a href="https://github.com/talorlik/ldap-2fa-on-k8s/blob/main/docs/auxiliary/troubleshooting/INDEX.md">Troubleshooting Index</a></strong> – Central index (deployment, application layer, LDAP admin seed, secrets, debug commands).</p>
